text:
Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was a spoiled boy who never listened to his mom and dad. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He saw a big slide and wanted to play on it.

His mom told him to wait for his turn, but Tim didn't want to. He pushed the other kids away and didn't yield. He climbed the slide and went down very fast. At the bottom of the slide, he saw a big puddle of mud. Tim didn't know what to do.

He tried to find the exit, but he slipped and fell into the mud. Tim was all dirty and sad. His mom came to help him, but she was not happy. Tim had to go home and take a bath. He didn't get to play at the park anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, her mom gave her a new backpack made of leather. Lily loved it and wanted to show it to her friends.

The next day, Lily went to the park with her backpack. Her friends were impressed and asked her to show them what was inside. Lily opened her backpack and started to load it with her toys.

Suddenly, Lily saw a big dog barking at her. She was scared and didn't know what to do. But then she remembered that her mom had told her to stay calm and not run away from dogs. So, Lily stayed still and the dog sniffed her backpack. The dog liked the smell of the leather and started to wag its tail. Lily's friends were amazed and Lily was happy that she wasn't scared anymore.

John was a 3 year old boy who had a very big network of friends. But one day, he got very angry when he found out that his friends were ignoring him. He just couldn't understand why his friends were doing this!

John tried to talk to his friends and ask them why they were ignoring him, but nobody was listening. This made him feel very sad and he decided to find some new friends.

John was lucky to find some really nice friends who were very easy to talk to. He was happy that he could talk, laugh and play with them - they didn't ignore him like his old friends did!

John learned an important lesson that day - that when your friends ignore you, it's time to find some new ones who will appreciate you and make it easy to have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat yummy cookies. One day, Timmy's mom set a plate of cookies on the table. Timmy was so happy! He ate all the cookies and smiled. 

After eating the cookies, Timmy wanted to go for a ride in his jeep. His dad had a big jeep that Timmy loved. His dad set Timmy in the jeep and they drove around the neighborhood. Timmy loved the bumpy ride in the jeep. 

When they got back home, Timmy's mom had set out some more cookies. Timmy was so happy to see them! He ate them all up and said, "Yummy, these cookies are so good!" Timmy was so full and happy. He went to bed dreaming of more yummy cookies and bumpy jeep rides. The end.

Once there was a bunny who wanted to brush her fur. She hopped all around the garden looking for a brush, but she couldn't find one.

She hopped over to the pond and saw a frog. The frog asked her why she was hopping around. The bunny told the frog about her need for a brush. 

The frog thought for a moment, then hopped away. He soon hopped back with a lily pad in his mouth. On the lily pad was the brush the bunny needed!

The bunny was so happy. She thanked the frog and hopped all the way home. Once she arrived home, she brushed her fur until it was so soft and shiny. She was so tired after her long search that she fell asleep right away.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a calm little stream. Every morning, at sunrise, the birds would sing and the fish would swim. The water was so clear, and everyone loved the stream.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the stream. He saw a fish and said, "Hello, Mr. Fish! Can I wash my hands in your stream?" The fish looked at Tim and said, "Yes, Tim! You can wash your hands here. The water is very clean."

Tim washed his hands in the stream. He was very happy. The fish was happy too. They both enjoyed the sunrise together. From that day on, Tim and the fish became good friends. They would always meet at the calm stream, every morning, to enjoy the sunrise.

John was very enthusiastic as he woke up in the morning. He ran to his window and shouted "Good morning sun". He could see trees outside shaking their branches as if in response. He smiled and slammed the window shut before getting ready to go out.

John had been looking forward to this day for a long time. He had heard about the special event held in his school every year. Everyone told him it was good fun. He was so excited.

John walked into school, eyes wide with anticipation. He could see the stage in front with everyone eagerly awaiting the show. When the show began everyone bowed with respect as the music started playing.

John watched as the performers jumped up onto the stage, their moves full of energy. He clapped enthusiastically and sang along to the words. He was having so much fun!

When the show ended, everyone bowed in appreciation. John bowed too and shouted out "Thank you!". He knew he would never forget this special morning.

Once upon a time, there was a bear who was very competitive. He loved to compete with his friends and was always looking for a challenge. One day, the bear decided to climb a big mountain and see who could get to the top first. His friends followed him, and they began to rise up the mountain.

It was a long and tough climb. The bear got very tired, and he wanted to give up. But then, he heard his friends calling out words of encouragement and it made him keep going. He kept pushing himself, and eventually he made it to the top of the mountain!

The bear was so proud, and his friends celebrated his victory with him. Just then, the bear noticed something special happening outside. It was spring, and the sun was rising higher in the sky. He realized that he had just completed the biggest challenge he had ever faced and he was happy. 

The bear and his friends celebrated the new season, and looked forward to more competitions in the future. He knew that with enough determination and courage, he could rise to any challenge!

Once upon a time, there was a famous pool. Every day, lots of people would come from all around to get a chance to go in the pool.

One day, a little girl named Susie decided she wanted to get in the pool too. So she put on her swimming costume, grabbed her goggles, and ran over to the pool.

When Susie arrived, she was so excited to get in the pool! She climbed into the water and splashed around with her friends. She was so happy she got to go in the famous pool.

The pool was so much fun, and Susie didn't want the day to end. She played in the water until the sun went down and it was time to go home.

Susie loved getting to go in the famous pool and knew she would never forget the fun she had that day.

Jack was a very tired 3 year old boy. He was so tired that he yawned continuously on his way to school.

At school, his friends were so excited. They were wearing their best clothes, which were mostly pink. Everyone was talking about the fun activities they were going to do throughout the day. Jack yawned again. 

Suddenly, one of Jack's classmates noticed how tired Jack was and asked him why he kept yawning. Jack replied that he was feeling really tired but he was also really excited to learn new things at school. His friend felt sorry for Jack and offered to help him get through the day.

From that day on, Jack couldn't help but yawn in class, but he also couldn't help but smile with his friends.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Jane and Jack. They liked to play together every day, but sometimes they disagreed.

One day they were arguing about what to do on their holiday. Jane wanted to go to the park and play, but Jack wanted to stay at home and watch TV. Jane said, â€œWe can stay independent and do what we want.â€

Jack thought about it and then said, â€œI want to stay home.â€ Jane said, â€œNo, letâ€™s go to the park.â€ They kept arguing until finally Jack said, â€œOkay, letâ€™s go to the park!â€ 

So, on their holiday, Jane and Jack had a great time at the park. They played together, laughed together and made lots of new friends! They learned that being independent was still fun, even if they didnâ€™t always agree.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses with the blocks. Anna has a lot of red blocks and Ben has a lot of blue blocks.

"Look at my tower!" Anna says. "It is very tall and strong."

"I like your tower," Ben says. "But I like my house more. It has a door and a window."

"Can I add some red blocks to your house?" Anna asks.

"OK," Ben says. "But only a few. I don't want my house to be too red."

Anna adds some red blocks to Ben's house. She makes a roof and a chimney. She thinks the house looks better now.

"Thank you, Anna," Ben says. "The house is very pretty now."

But then, mother comes in. She sees the blocks on the floor. She is not happy.

"Anna and Ben, what are you doing?" mother says. "You made a big mess. You have to clean up the blocks now."

Anna and Ben are uncomfortable. They don't want to clean up the blocks. They want to keep playing.

"But mother, we are having fun," Anna says.

"We made a tower and a house," Ben says.

"I'm sorry, but you have to put the blocks away," mother says. "It is time for lunch. You can play with the blocks later."

Anna and Ben sigh. They pick up the blocks and put them in a box. They follow mother to the kitchen. They hope they can play with the blocks again soon.

Joe and his sister were playing in the garden. The sun was shining and they were having a great time. Joe picked up a twig and said to his sister, "I'm gonna snap this twig and see what happens!" His sister replied, "Be careful, Joe. You don't want to get hurt!" Joe was determined and he snapped the twig. Suddenly, Joe felt helpless and he fell to the ground. His sister ran to him and said, "Oh no, Joe. Are you okay?" Joe said, "I'm okay. Everything just feels a bit numb." His sister helped him and soon Joe felt better. He forgot all about the twig and they continued to play together in the garden. The sun was bright and the sunflowers swayed in the wind. Joe and his sister were happy and didn't worry about the twig anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty butterfly named Bella. Bella loved to fly around the garden and visit all her friends. One day, Bella met a little ant named Andy.

"Hi, Andy! Do you want to fly with me?" asked Bella.

"I can't fly, but I can walk fast!" replied Andy.

Bella thought for a moment and said, "I know! Let's bury some treasure and come back for it later. That will be fun!"

So, Bella and Andy buried a shiny rock in the dirt and promised to come back for it. They flew and walked around the garden, playing and having fun. When it was time to go home, they remembered their treasure and went back to dig it up.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" said Andy.

"I know, right? Let's bury it again and come back for it another day," said Bella.

And so, they buried their treasure again and went home, happy and excited for their next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely little boy. His name was Jack. He had just moved to a new town and was feeling very lonely. No one was around to play with.

Jack began to cry. Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"I love you," said a voice.

Jack looked up in surprise. He saw an old woman. She smiled at him.

"Do you want to come with me?" the old woman asked.

Jack was hesitant. "Yes," he replied.

The old woman took Jack to her house. She showed him her old wooden chair, which had a buckle on the back.

Jack reached out and touched the buckle. "I love it," he said.

The old woman smiled. She had never seen Jack so happy. "I love you too," she said.

Jack and the old woman spent the day together, playing games and eating snacks. For the first time in a long time, Jack didn't feel so lonely.

Once there was a cute little girl. She was just three and she had a new scarf. She was so excited to wear it because it was very pretty. But when she tried to put it on, it was too difficult for her. She started to cry.

Her mom saw that she was feeling bad and she wanted to help. She tried to put the scarf on the little girl, but it was too hard. Then she got an idea! She ran to the kitchen and came back with a big spoon. She used the spoon to help fix the scarf and it worked!

The little girl was very happy and she couldn't believe how funny it looked. She gave her mom a big hug and said thank you. Her mom said she was welcome and told her not to spoil it. That way she could always wear it!

Once upon a time, there was a family. They went on a vacation to the beach. They saw a lot of things like the sun, sand, and shells. The family had a useful umbrella to stay cool. The little girl wanted to show her brother the pretty shells she found. They had so much fun on their vacation!

Once upon a time, there was a strong man and his wife. They lived in a small house near the woods. They were very happy together.

One day, the strong man and his wife found a lost dog. It was very sad and hungry. The wife said, "Let's help the dog and give it food." The strong man agreed. They took care of the dog, and soon it was happy and healthy.

The dog loved the strong man and his wife very much. It stayed with them and kept them safe. The strong man, his wife, and the dog lived happily together. In the end, they learned that helping others makes us happy too.

One day, Tom wanted to drive his toy car. He was very excited. He took his car and went to the living room. The sun was shining outside, and it was a beautiful day.

In the living room, there was a big lamp. The lamp was tall and bright. Tom's toy car drove fast around the lamp. The car went round and round. Tom was having a lot of fun.

But then, Tom's toy car got confused. It did not know which way to go. Tom helped his car by showing it the right way. The car was happy again. They played until it was time for bed. Tom and his toy car had a great day.

Once, there was a red tunnel. It was long and dark, and it seemed to go on forever.

One day, a little boy came upon the tunnel. He was only three years old, and he had never seen anything like it before. He was scared of the dark, but he bravely stepped inside.

As he went, he started to count. One, two, three, four and so on. Every time he said a number, he felt a bit braver. He kept counting until he finally reached the end of the tunnel.

When he was done, he was so proud of himself. He had conquered the darkness and made it to the other side. And from then on, he was never scared of the dark again.

Lily and Ben like to play with trains. They have a big box of train toys and a long rail to make tracks. They take turns to send the trains on the rail and make them go fast or slow.

One day, Lily wants to send a red train on the rail, but Ben says no. He says the red train is his and he does not want to share. Lily gets angry and says she will send the red train anyway. Ben gets angry too and says he will stop her.

They start to fight over the red train and pull it from each other. The red train breaks in two and they both cry. They hear a loud noise and look up. Their mom is standing at the door and she looks very mad.

She says they have been very bad and they have to go to their rooms. She says they have to give back all their train toys and they will not play with them for a long time. She says they have to learn to share and be nice.

Lily and Ben feel very sad and sorry. They wish they did not fight over the red train. They wish they could play with their train toys again. They wish they could say sorry to each other and to their mom. But it is too late. They have to go to their rooms and they have no trains to play with. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to pretend that she was a princess and would wear a sparkly crown on her head. One day, Lily's mommy told her that they were going to have fun at the park.

At the park, Lily saw a big slide and wanted to go down it. But her mommy said it was too dangerous for her to go alone. So, Lily's mommy went down the slide with her. They had so much fun together!

As they were leaving the park, Lily's mommy said, "Remember when we went down the slide together? It's always safer to have someone with you when you do something dangerous." Lily smiled and pretended that she was a brave princess who always had someone by her side.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. They played on the swings and the slide, but when it started to get dark, Lily's mom said it was time to go home.

Lily didn't want to leave yet, but her mom said they had to go. Lily felt sad because she wanted to play more. As they walked home, Lily noticed her shadow following her. She asked her mom, "Why does my shadow follow me?"

Her mom replied, "Your shadow follows you because it's connected to your feet."

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "I wish my shadow could play with me too."

Her mom smiled and said, "Maybe one day it will, but for now, we have to go home. Everything has to end eventually."

Lily understood and they continued walking home, with her shadow still following her.

Once there was a little girl called Sally. She liked to play in the park with her friends.One day she saw something that made her very jealous. Her friends had gotten a swing!

Sally wanted a swing too, so she asked her daddy if she could have one. With a smile he said yes, and brought it home the next day. Sally couldn't believe it! 

It was a big swing with a comfy seat. She wanted to swing all day. Sally was so excited she spent every day in the park, helping her daddy hang the swing for her.

When it was finally finished, Sally felt so happy. She was so proud of her new swing. Now she had one just like her friends!

John was a little boy. He was three years old. One day, he was walking home from the park with his mom. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It scared him and he started to panic. His mom noticed and gave him a big smile. She said "It's okay John, it's just a car". John felt a little better but he still felt frightened. He stayed close to his mom and she squeezed him tightly. When they got home, he felt much safer. Now he knew that he could trust his mom to help him when he was scared. He smiled and felt much better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a dark envelope on the ground. She picked it up and looked inside, but there was nothing there. Suddenly, the ground started to tremble and Lily got scared. 

She ran to her friends and showed them the envelope. They all looked at it and wondered where it came from. As they were talking, the ground trembled again and they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck driving by! 

Lily and her friends continued to play in the park, but they couldn't stop thinking about the mysterious envelope. They decided to take it to the lost and found in case someone was looking for it. As they walked, Lily's hands trembled with excitement. They finally arrived at the lost and found and gave the envelope to the kind lady behind the desk. She smiled and thanked them for being so helpful. Lily and her friends felt proud of themselves for doing a good deed.

Once there were two friends. They liked to play together every day. They liked to guess what the other would do. Sometimes, they laughed and said funny things. 

One day, they wanted to guess who could jump the highest. They both jumped very high and landed with a thump! They counted to three and then jumped again. 

They laughed as they did this and had so much fun! Soon, it was time for them to go home. As they said goodbye, they both agreed that guessing was a really fun thing to do.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bill and Bob. Bill was a brave little boy who loved to explore.

One day Bill wanted to try something new and he said to Bob, "I dare you to play the drums." Bob was so excited. He had always wanted to try playing the drums.

But Bob was also a bit clumsy. While Bill watched, Bob tried to play the drums but he hit the wrong way and the drums sounded funny.

Still, Bill was so impressed that he said, "Bob I think you did a good job! You played the drums great!"

Bob smiled and said, "Thanks Bill. That was lots of fun. Let's do it again sometime!"

Once there was a girl who was scared. She was lost and alone in the park, and didn't know where to go. Just then, she saw a lawyer. He was wearing a big black suit and carried a big brown bag.

The lawyer smiled at the girl. He said he would help her. He asked the girl her name and then made a call on his phone.

Soon a fire truck appeared. The firefighters got out and talked to the lawyer. He explained that the girl was lost and needed to be rescued.

The firefighters put the girl in the truck and drove her to her home. As they drove, the girl felt a little less scared. When they arrived, her parents were so happy to see her.

The girl was very thankful that the lawyer had helped rescue her. She was also happy to be back home, safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom and brought her favorite bag with her. The bag was very useful because it had all of her toys inside.

While playing at the park, Lily saw some other kids playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, but the other kids ignored her and wouldn't let her join in. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do.

But then, she remembered her mom telling her that it's okay if others ignore you, as long as you don't ignore yourself. So, Lily took out her toys from her bag and started playing by herself. Soon, the other kids noticed how much fun she was having and asked if they could join in too.

Lily learned that even if others ignore you, you should never ignore yourself and the things that make you happy. And her useful bag of toys helped her make new friends and have fun at the park. The end.

John was a little boy with a very clumsy waist. Whenever he hopped around you could hear it jingle and shake. Everyone in the park always laughed whenever he walked past the swings.

One day John decided he wanted to try the swings too. He waddled over and sat down on the swing. With a deep breath and a strong push, he began to swing. 

As he reached the height of the swing, John yelled, â€œI'm flying!"

Suddenly, his clumsy waist got tangled in the swing and he stopped flying right away. 

John let out a deep sigh as he looked up at the other kids happily playing on their swings. He felt really sad he couldn't join them and his eyes filled with tears. 

Just then two friendly little girls ran over and said, â€œHey John, we want to help you untangle yourself. Can you tell us how we can help?" 

John smiled and said, "I think you should push me while I swing forward, one of you should help me hold my waist so the swing won't get tangled again!" 

The two girls pushed John and he started to swing. He reached the top of the swing again and yelled, "Yay, I'm flying!" 

John thanked his helpful friends and kept swinging until sunset.

Once upon a time, there was a bee who was very bright. She was buzzing happily around outside, when she saw something interesting. It was a big step! She flew close and landed on the step. She was very curious, so she started to step up the step.

One step, two steps, three steps! The bee kept going and going. Then, when she almost reached the top, she stopped and looked around. Everything was so bright and beautiful! It made the bee so happy.

Soon, the bee flew away and back home. It was such a wonderful day, and the bee would never forget the bright step.

Once there was a little child. He was very tired, so he decided to have a nap. He lay down on his bed and closed his eyes. His blanket was heavy and warm. It felt so good that he quickly fell asleep.

The child dreamed of running and jumping in the park. He played tag with his friends and even won a race. After all the fun, the little one was very tired. He wanted to sleep even more, so he took another long nap.

The heavy blanket kept the child nice and cozy. He slept for a long time, until he heard his mom calling. The child woke up, feeling refreshed and happy. He smiled and decided to have another nap another day.

Ben likes to ride his board. His board has four wheels and he can go fast on it. He likes to ride his board in the park with his friend Sam. Sam has a board too, but his board is bigger and has a picture of a dragon on it.

One day, Ben and Sam go to the park to ride their boards. They see a big hill and they want to go down it. Ben goes first. He pushes his board and gets on it. He feels the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He is happy.

But then he sees a big puddle at the bottom of the hill. He tries to stop his board, but he can't. He goes into the puddle and gets wet and dirty. His board gets wet and dirty too. He falls off his board and lands on the grass. He is sad.

Sam comes down the hill after him. He sees Ben and his board in the puddle. He stops his board and gets off it. He runs to Ben and helps him up.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Sam asks.

"I'm okay, but my board is not okay," Ben says. "It's wet and dirty and it doesn't work."

Sam looks at Ben's board. He sees that it is wet and dirty, but he also sees something else.

"Ben, look!" Sam says. "Your board has a picture on it too!"

Ben looks at his board. He sees that the dirt has made a picture on his board. It looks like a star.

"Wow, you're right!" Ben says. "My board has a star on it!"

Ben and Sam smile. They don't mind being wet and dirty. They like their boards. They like their pictures. They like their ride. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They had a special cap which belonged to mum. Every time mum wore the cap, she felt happy. 

One day, mum said, "Let's bury the cap!" Dad said, "Why? It will be sad to put it away." 

Mum smiled and said, "No, burying the cap will make us very happy." 

So, dad got his shovel and they went out to the back garden. They dug a hole and put the cap in it. Then they filled it up with soil and patted it down. 

The happy family stood back and smiled. Now they had a special place in the garden where they could say hello to the cap and remember how happy it made them.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Tom finds a hammer in his dad's tool box. He thinks it is a fun toy. He wants to show Anna.

He goes to Anna's house and knocks on the door. Anna opens the door and sees Tom with the hammer. She is scared.

"Tom, what are you doing with that hammer?" she asks.

"I want to play with it. It is a useful toy. Look, I can write with it," Tom says. He hits the wall with the hammer. He makes a big hole and a loud noise.

"Tom, stop! You are breaking the wall. That is not a toy. That is a tool. You are making a mess," Anna says. She tries to take the hammer from Tom.

But Tom does not listen. He likes the hammer. He thinks it is fun. He hits the wall again and again. He makes more holes and more noise.

Anna's mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is going on. She sees Tom with the hammer and Anna with tears. She is angry.

"Tom, what are you doing? You are ruining the wall. Give me that hammer right now. You are in big trouble. Go home and tell your dad what you did," she says.

Tom is scared. He gives the hammer to Anna's mom. He runs away. He cries.

Anna is sad. She does not want to play with Tom anymore. He is not a good friend. He is a bad boy. She does not like him.

One day, a little boy named Tim and his mom decided to prepare for a fun safari. They wanted to see all the animals in the big park. Tim was so excited and grateful to go on this adventure.

As they got ready, Tim's mom said, "Tim, we need to pack some food and water for our safari trip." Tim replied, "Okay, Mom! I will help you." They put sandwiches, fruit, and juice in a big bag. They also packed a hat and sunglasses for the sunny day.

On the safari, they saw lions, zebras, and giraffes. Tim and his mom took many pictures and had a great time. At the end of the day, they were tired but happy. Tim said, "Thank you, Mom, for the best day ever!"

Once upon a time there was a Mommy and a little girl. The Mommy was kind and warm. The little girl liked looking out the window. 

One day the little girl noticed something special. Outside the window she saw a new curtain. It was bright and colourful. It seemed to wave at her. 

The little girl wanted to go outside and look closer. The Mommy said, "Yes, you can go look at the curtain, just stay close." 

So the little girl and the Mommy went outside. The warm sun was shining and the little girl was so happy. She ran to the curtain and looked closely at all the bright colours. 

The little girl loved the curtain and she said, "Mommy, this curtain is the best ever!" The Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, the curtain is very special." 

They both hugged each other and the little girl couldn't stop smiling. She felt so happy and warm.

Lily liked to collect shiny things. She found them in the park, in the street, in the trash. She had a box full of shiny things in her room. She had coins, buttons, keys, rings, and more.

One day, she saw something very shiny in the dirt. It was a mineral. It was red and sparkly. Lily wanted it very much. She tried to pick it up, but it was stuck. She pulled and pulled, but it did not move. She got angry and frustrated.

She did not notice that the mineral had sharp edges. She cut her hand on the mineral. It hurt a lot. She cried and cried. She dropped the mineral and ran to her mom. Her mom cleaned her wound and put a bandage on it. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, sweetie. You should be careful with shiny things. Some of them are sharp and dangerous. They can hurt you."

Lily learned a lesson that day. She realized that shiny things are not always good. She decided to be more careful with what she collected. She also decided to share some of her shiny things with her friends. She found out that sharing was more fun than hoarding. She was happier and safer.

Once upon a time, there was a goose named Gigi. Gigi was very special because she had original feathers that were rainbow-colored. Everyone in the park loved Gigi and would come to see her every day.

One day, a naughty boy came to the park and scared Gigi. Gigi was so scared that she flew away and didn't come back for a long time. Everyone in the park was very sad because they missed Gigi.

But one day, a little girl came to the park with a bag of bread. She saw Gigi and threw some bread to her. Gigi remembered the park and all her friends, so she decided to come back.

The little girl was happy to see Gigi back in the park, and everyone else was too. They all played together and had a great time. From that day on, Gigi was never scared again and would always stay in the park with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a lonely tree in a village. She was very sad because she had no friends to play with. 

One day, Tweety decided to go to the village to make some friends. She met a group of birds who were playing and having fun. Tweety wanted to join them, but they didn't let her play with them. They made fun of her and joked about her small size.

Tweety felt very sad and lonely again. She went back to her tree and cried. But then she remembered something her mother had told her: "Always be kind to others, even if they are not kind to you." 

So the next day, Tweety went back to the village and saw the group of birds again. This time, she didn't let their jokes and teasing bother her. Instead, she smiled and said hello to them. She even told them a joke she had heard. The birds were surprised and started to laugh. They realized that Tweety was a friendly bird and they wanted to be her friend.

From that day on, Tweety had many friends to play with. She learned that being kind and having a sense of humor can make a big difference in making friends. The moral of the story is that it's important to treat others with kindness and respect, even if they are different from us.

Roger was walking around the park when he saw something that made him stop. There was an ugly hanger lying on the ground and he wanted to pick it up. But, when he reached it, the hanger suddenly began to move! 

"Hoowaaah!" the hanger said. "What are you doing here? Are you going to take me with you?"

Roger was so surprised that he could not answer. He just stared.

"Oh come on, don't be scared!" the hanger laughed. "Why don't you yield me to your house and we can be friends!"

Roger thought about it for a moment, then he smiled and agreed. He called it 'Hanger' and from that day on they were good friends. Whenever anything ugly happened, Hanger was there for Roger!

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to go on the swing. The swing is fun. It goes up and down.

One day, Lily and Ben go to the park. But the swing is broken. The rope is torn. The seat is on the ground. Lily and Ben are sad. They cannot go on the swing.

Lily says, "Who broke the swing? I want to go on the swing."

Ben says, "I don't know. Maybe a big dog. Or a bad boy. I want to go on the swing too."

They look around. They see a man. He has a tool box. He is fixing the swing. He is putting a new rope. He is lifting the seat.

Lily and Ben run to the man. They say, "Hello, mister. Are you fixing the swing?"

The man says, "Yes, I am. I work for the park. I saw the swing was broken. I came to fix it. Do you like the swing?"

Lily and Ben say, "Yes, we do. We love the swing. It is our favorite. Thank you for fixing it."

The man says, "You're welcome. It's almost done. You can go on the swing soon. But be careful. Don't swing too high. And don't push each other. And have fun."

Lily and Ben say, "OK, we will. Thank you, mister."

The man finishes fixing the swing. He says, "There you go. The swing is ready. You can go on it now. Have a nice day."

Lily and Ben say, "Thank you, mister. Have a nice day too."

They go on the swing. They are happy. They swing up and down. They laugh and smile. They are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to go on the swing. The swing is fun. It goes up and down.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. The elephant was very slow and walked slowly all day long. The people in the village liked to watch the elephant walk. They trusted the elephant to be slow and not to hurt anyone.

One day, a little girl went to see the elephant. She wanted to touch the elephant's trunk. But the elephant was not happy. The little girl got too close and the elephant got scared. The elephant moved quickly and accidentally stepped on the little girl. The little girl was hurt very badly.

Everyone was sad. They didn't trust the elephant anymore. They knew the elephant didn't mean to hurt the little girl, but they couldn't forget what happened. From that day on, the elephant had to stay in a special place where no one could get too close.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck who loved to swim in the pond. One day, the little duck went too far and got lost. The duck was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, the duck saw the shore and swam towards it.

When the little duck reached the shore, it was wet and cold. The duck tried to settle down and find a warm place to rest. But the shore was too rocky and the duck couldn't find a good spot. 

As the sun started to set, the little duck got even colder and more tired. It tried to fly back to the pond, but it was too weak. Sadly, the little duck passed away on the shore. The other ducks in the pond never forgot about their friend and always remembered to be careful when swimming too far.

There were two friends, Jill and Jack. They liked to play together and were very popular. One day, they wanted to build an igloo. They took lots of blocks and started to build. Soon, they had a big igloo.

But as they played, they started to argue. They shouted at each other and their voices got louder and louder. Suddenly, their igloo split apart! The blocks fell to the ground and they were very sad.

Jack and Jill had a big fight then and they decided not to be friends any more. Everyone was surprised and the two were no longer so popular. From then on, they went their separate ways.

Once upon a time, there was a happy bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around in the grass and play with his friends. One day, Benny's friend, a little bird named Billy, fell from his nest and hurt his wing. Benny was sad to see his friend in pain, so he hopped over to Billy and snuggled up next to him to comfort him. 

Benny knew that when he was feeling sad or hurt, being with his friends always made him feel better. So, he stayed with Billy and kept him company until his wing felt better. Soon enough, Billy was feeling cheerful again and ready to fly back up to his nest. 

Benny was happy to see his friend feeling better and even happier to be able to play with him again in the grass. From that day on, Benny knew that being there for his friends and comforting them when they were feeling down was the best thing he could do to make them feel better.

Once upon a time, there was an orange emergency. Everyone got scared and started to scatter. Little Lily was running around and couldn't find her mum. But before she knew it, she found her dad. He knew what to do in an emergency, so he held Lily's hand and hurried away from the orange emergency.

Soon, they arrived in a big field and there were lots of other people scattered around. Lily saw that all the people had big smiles on their faces. That's when she knew that everything was going to be OK.

Meanwhile, her dad was talking to some other dads about what had happened. Lily saw that they were all getting ready to help. Before she knew it, they were all on their way back to the orange emergency.

When they arrived, they started to help. Everyone worked together to clear the orange emergency away. It was hard work, but everyone was smiling and feeling very proud.

Soon, the orange emergency was gone and everyone was happy. Everyone gave each other high-fives and Lily's dad hugged her tight.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys in the living room when she accidentally knocked over a box. All the toys inside the box scatter on the floor. Lily's mom came into the room and helped her pick up the toys.

Later that day, Lily's family sat down for dinner. They had yummy spaghetti and meatballs. Lily's dad accidentally spilled some black sauce on his shirt. Lily thought it was funny and giggled.

After dinner, Lily's mom took her outside to play. They looked up at the sky and saw lots of stars. Lily's mom pointed out the Big Dipper and they made a wish on a shooting star. It was a happy day for Lily and her family.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to play soccer. They were on the same team with other kids. One day, they had a big game against another team. Sara and Ben wanted to win.

Before the game, their coach said, "You have to work together as a team. Pass the ball to each other and help each other. Don't be selfish and try to score all the goals by yourself."

Sara and Ben nodded. They ran to the field and waited for the whistle. The game started and Sara got the ball. She saw Ben open and tried to pass the ball to him. But a boy from the other team was faster and took the ball away. He ran to the goal and scored.

Sara was sad. She wanted to score a goal too. She thought, "Next time, I will keep the ball and not pass it to Ben. He is too slow."

The game continued and Sara got the ball again. She saw Ben open again, but she ignored him. She tried to dribble past the other team by herself. But she was not fast enough and the other team took the ball away again. They scored another goal.

Ben was mad. He wanted to help Sara and the team. He thought, "Sara is selfish. She doesn't pass the ball to me or anyone else. She thinks she can do everything by herself."

The game ended and the other team won. Sara and Ben were sad and angry. They walked to the bench and sat down. Their coach came to them and said, "What happened? You didn't play like a team. You didn't pass the ball or hold each other's hands. You were selfish and tried to do everything by yourself. That's not how you play soccer. You have to share and cooperate and have fun."

Sara and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they did. They said, "We're sorry, coach. We were selfish. We didn't play like a team. We didn't hold each other's hands. We didn't have fun."

The coach smiled and said, "It's okay. You can learn from your mistake. Next time, remember to play like a team. Pass the ball and hold each other's hands. And don't forget to have fun. That's what soccer is all about."

Sara and Ben nodded. They hugged each other and said, "We're sorry, friend. We will play like a team next time. We will pass the ball and hold each other's hands. And we will have fun."

They smiled and ran to join the other kids. They learned their lesson and played better as a team. They had fun and made more goals. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kind sack. Every day when the sun came up, the sack was happy.

One morning, the sack saw a little girl walking by. She had pigtails and a big bow in her hair. She was carrying a stuffed bear. 

The sack said, "Hello!" 

The little girl stopped and looked at the sack. "Hello," she said. "What are you?" 

The sack smiled. "I'm a kind sack," it said. "My friends tell me stories all day, and I get to listen. Would you like to tell me a story?" 

The little girl smiled. She sat down and told the sack all about her packed lunch, and the games she liked to play with her friends. 

The sack thought the little girl's stories were very fun. It thanked her for sharing them and waved goodbye as she walked away. 

And that was the story of the kind sack and the little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and feel the sun on her face. One day, while she was playing, she found a shiny rock on the ground. It was a gift from the earth!

Lily was so happy and felt gifted to have found such a pretty rock. But then she accidentally dropped it and it broke into pieces. She felt so sad that she began to weep. 

Her mommy came outside and saw that Lily was crying. She asked what was wrong, and Lily showed her the broken rock. Mommy hugged her and said it was okay, that they could still keep the pieces and remember the special gift from the ground. And Lily felt a little better, knowing that she still had a piece of the gift.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the jungle to read her favorite book. She sat under a tree and started reading. Suddenly, a big crocodile appeared in front of her. Lily was scared and closed her book.

The crocodile said, "Hello little girl, why are you scared?" Lily replied, "I am scared because you are big and I don't know you." The crocodile said, "Don't be scared, I am a friendly crocodile. I am also very flexible."

Lily was surprised and asked, "What does flexible mean?" The crocodile replied, "It means I can move my body in many ways." Lily smiled and said, "That's cool! Can you show me?" The crocodile then showed Lily how he could twist and turn his body. Lily was amazed and said, "Wow, you are really flexible!" From that day on, Lily and the crocodile became good friends and they would often read books together under the tree in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a big festival in a town. There were lots of people and music and yummy food. A little girl went to the festival with her mom and dad. She saw lots of things like balloons and clowns and a big stage.

Suddenly, the little girl saw a soft, fluffy puppy. She wanted to pet the puppy, but it ran away. She was sad, but then she remembered she had a phone. She called her mom and dad and told them about the puppy. They helped her find the puppy and she was happy again.

At the end of the festival, the little girl was tired but had lots of fun. She was happy she got to see the puppy and call her mom and dad. She couldn't wait to go to the festival again next year. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a youth named Jack. Jack loved to play with his friends in the park. They would run, jump and laugh together. One day, Jack saw a big boy who looked mean. Jack didn't like him, but he didn't say anything.

A few days later, Jack and his friends were playing when they saw the mean boy again. This time, he came over and started to fight with Jack's friend. Jack didn't know what to do, but he knew it was important to help his friend. So, he ran over and pushed the mean boy away. The mean boy fell down and ran away.

From that day on, Jack knew that it was important to stand up for his friends. He learned that sometimes, you have to fight to protect the people you care about. And even though he was just a youth, Jack knew that he could make a difference in the world.

Once upon a time, a boy went for a ride on his boat. He saw a big fish and it tried to bite his boat. The boy was scared but he kept going. He saw a smooth rock and he stopped to touch it. It was nice and smooth. Then, he saw a bird and it tried to bite him. The boy ran away and went back home. He was happy to be safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. But one day, it started to rain. Lily didn't like the rain because it made everything wet and she couldn't play outside. 

Lily's mommy told her to go check the mailbox for the mail. But when Lily went to the mailbox, she saw that it was stuck shut. She tried and tried but she couldn't open it. She felt helpless and didn't know what to do. 

Just then, her big brother came along and saw that she was having trouble. He helped her open the mailbox and they found a letter inside. It was from their grandma and it made Lily very happy. Even though it was raining, Lily felt better because she got to read a letter from her grandma.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to draw and read. She did not have many friends at school, because she was afraid to talk to them. She wished she could be brave and make new friends.

One day, her class went on a trip to the mountain. Lily was excited to see the big rocks and trees, but she was also nervous. She did not know anyone on the bus, and she sat by herself. She looked out the window and saw the mountain getting closer and closer.

When they arrived, the teacher told them to stay in groups and explore the mountain. Lily followed the others, but she did not join any group. She walked by herself, looking at the flowers and birds. She felt lonely and sad.

She saw a small cave and decided to go inside. Maybe she would find something interesting. She crawled into the cave and saw a shiny stone. She reached out to touch it, but then she heard a loud roar. She turned around and saw a big bear blocking the entrance. She was scared and screamed.

"Help! Help! There is a bear in the cave!" she shouted.

Some of the other kids heard her and ran to the cave. They saw the bear and Lily. They were scared too, but they wanted to help Lily.

"Hey, bear! Go away! Leave Lily alone!" they yelled.

They threw some sticks and stones at the bear, trying to scare it away. The bear growled and moved back. It did not like the noise and the pain. It ran away from the cave, leaving Lily free.

Lily crawled out of the cave and hugged the kids who helped her. She was happy and grateful. They were happy too, and proud.

"Thank you for helping me! You are very brave and kind!" Lily said.

"You are welcome, Lily! We are glad you are okay!" they said.

They smiled and became friends. Lily was not shy anymore. She learned that she could be brave and make friends. She enjoyed the rest of the trip to the mountain. She had fun and learned a lot. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there were two kittens who were best friends. They were both playful and loved to play all day. 

One day, the two kittens were walking in the park and noticed a big pile of cardboard boxes. They had so much fun playing in the boxes that they decided to bring some back home.

The kittens asked their mom if they could keep the cardboard, but she said no. She said, â€œNo, you canâ€™t keep the cardboard. You must remove it from the house.â€

The two cats were sad, but they did as their mom said and removed the cardboard. Later that night, they went back to the park and found many more cardboard boxes to play in.

The moral of the story is that it is important to obey your parents. Even if it may seem like fun, itâ€™s important to remember to follow their rules so that you can have a happy and safe life.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a long pole on the ground. Lily wants to play with it.

"Look, Ben, a long pole! Let's play with it!" Lily says.

Ben is not sure. He thinks the pole is dirty and sharp.

"I don't want to play with it, Lily. It looks bad. Let's play with the ball instead." Ben says.

Lily does not listen. She picks up the pole and runs with it. She swings it in the air and laughs.

"Look, Ben, I'm a knight! I have a sword!" Lily says.

Ben stares at Lily. He is scared. He thinks Lily will hurt herself or someone else.

"Lily, stop! You will get hurt! Put down the pole!" Ben says.

Lily does not stop. She runs faster and faster. She does not see the big dog that is coming towards her. The dog is angry. It thinks Lily is attacking it. It barks and growls.

Lily sees the dog. She is scared. She tries to stop, but she slips and falls. The pole hits her in the head. She cries out loud.

Ben runs to Lily. He sees blood on her head. He is very scared. He calls for help.

"Help! Help! Lily is hurt! Help!" Ben says.

The dog runs away. A man comes to help. He calls an ambulance. He tries to calm Ben and Lily.

"Lily, Ben, don't worry. The ambulance is coming. You will be okay." The man says.

But Lily is not okay. She has a big wound on her head. She needs stitches. She has a concussion. She has to stay in the hospital for a long time. She can't play with Ben anymore. She can't play with the pole anymore. She is sad. Ben is sad. The pole is bad. The end.

One day, Pete and his mum were going to the park. Pete was very excited and said, "Mum, can I get a sail?" His mum replied, "No, Pete. You can't gain a sail today". But Pete was very selfish and kept asking for a sail.

Suddenly, Pete spotted a big sail boat in the park which he wanted to gain. He asked his mum again and again, but she said no. Then, Pete disobeyed his mum and hopped in the boat. 

The boat started to drift away with Pete in it. As it started to sail out to sea, Pete's mum screamed, "Pete, come back!" But it was too late. Pete was too far away and couldn't hear her. 

Pete was very scared and tried to sail the boat back to shore, but the boat got stuck in the middle of the sea. Pete couldn't get back and was never seen again.

Anna and Ben liked to play with their toy boat. They made it sail on the water in the bathtub. They pretended they were pirates and explorers.

One day, they decided to take their boat to the theater. The theater was a big place where people watched stories on a stage. Anna and Ben wanted to see a story about a princess and a dragon.

They sneaked their boat inside their backpack and went with their mom to the theater. They found their seats and waited for the story to start. They were very excited.

When the lights went down and the curtain opened, they saw a big dragon on the stage. It had scales, horns, and wings. It roared and breathed fire. Anna and Ben were scared. They thought the dragon was real and dangerous.

They took out their boat and whispered to it. "Don't worry, boat. We will protect you from the dragon. We are brave pirates and explorers. We have swords and cannons."

They held their boat close to their chest and pretended to fight the dragon. They made noises like "bang" and "slash". They did not notice that the people around them were looking at them and shushing them.

The dragon was not real and dangerous. It was harmless. It was a puppet that someone was moving with strings. The princess on the stage was not afraid of the dragon. She was friends with it. She sang a song to it and gave it a hug.

Anna and Ben stopped fighting the dragon. They listened to the song and watched the hug. They realized that the dragon was nice and friendly. They felt silly and sorry.

They put their boat back in their backpack and said to it. "Sorry, boat. We were wrong. The dragon is not bad. It is good. We are not pirates and explorers. We are just kids who like to play."

They smiled and clapped for the story. They enjoyed the rest of the theater. They learned that things are not always what they seem. They learned to be kind and curious.

Once upon a time, there was a pig named Wilbur. Wilbur loved to have fun, and he especially loved to play outside in the sunshine! 

One hot day, Wilbur decided he wanted to go swimming. He ran down to the lake and jumped in with a big splash. Wilbur loved the way the water felt on his back and he wanted to stay in the water all day long. 

So Wilbur started to twist and turn, he even tried to do somersaults! He was having so much fun when suddenly he felt something grab his tail. Wilbur was scared and he quickly jumped out of the water.

It was his mommy! She had come to find Wilbur after he had run away. Wilbur was happy to see her but he was also embarrassed because he had gone swimming without asking. 

His mom gave him a big hug and said, "Sometimes I just need to know where you are so I can wake up knowing that you are safe.â€ Wilbur smiled and hugged his mom back, glad that she was there to keep him safe. Then they both headed back home, ready for a nice nap in the cool shade.

One day, two friends went for a walk in the woods together. They saw an arrow on the ground. They thought it was so cool! They wanted to know who had made it. They followed the arrow and soon met an old man. He was very kind and friendly. He told them about the arrow. He said it was made from a flexible tree branch. He said he could make more arrows. The two friends were very excited. They asked him to show them how it is done. He agreed and they watched while he made another arrow. The two friends thanked the old man, said goodbye, and took the arrows home with them. They had a great day and learned something new.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the big park. They liked to run, jump, slide and swing. But their favorite thing was to climb the tall tree. The tree had many branches and leaves. It was fun to see the birds and the sky from the top.

One day, they saw a new thing on the tree. It was a leather bag. It was brown and shiny. It had a zipper and a strap. Ben and Lily wondered what was inside. They wanted to see.

"Let's climb the tree and get the bag," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said.

They climbed the tree, branch by branch. They reached the bag. Ben grabbed it and opened the zipper. He looked inside.

"Wow, look at this!" he said. He pulled out a shiny thing. It was a clear bottle. It had a label with words and pictures. Ben could not read the words, but he saw the picture of a skull and crossbones.

"What is it?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, but it looks cool," Ben said. He opened the bottle and smelled it. It smelled bad. He made a face.

"Yuck, it stinks!" he said.

"Let me see," Lily said. She took the bottle from Ben and smelled it too. She also made a face.

"Maybe we should put it back," she said.

But it was too late. The bottle slipped from her hand and fell to the ground. It broke and spilled. The liquid was green and bubbly. It burned the grass and the flowers. It made a hissing sound.

Ben and Lily heard a loud voice. It was a man. He was angry.

"Hey, you kids! What have you done? That's my poison! I was going to use it to kill the rats! Now you've ruined everything!"

He ran to the tree. He saw Ben and Lily. He looked mean. He had a stick in his hand.

"Get down here, you little brats! I'll teach you a lesson!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They tried to climb down, but they were too high. They could not find a way. They cried for help, but no one heard them. The man reached the tree. He swung his stick. He hit Ben and Lily. They fell to the ground. They did not get up. They did not play anymore.

Once upon a time there was a little elephant called Ellie. Ellie had a playful soul and a very creative mind. One day, Ellie went on a journey and while walking through a dense forest, she started to shiver.

"Whoa!" she thought, "It's so chilly." She looked around and saw a big trunk filled with blankets. "What a gem!" she shouted, smiling from ear to ear.

Slowly, she stepped towards the trunk and started to pick one blanket for herself. Just then, a little bird flew out of the trunk and said "These blankets don't belong to you! They belong to everyone in the forest, so please take just one blanket or everyone will be cold."

Ellie felt bad for taking more than one blanket. She decided to take only one and put the others back in the trunk. From that day, she knew the importance of sharing with others.

The end

Once upon a time, there was a charming little bird named Billy. Billy loved to fly high in the sky. One day, he saw a big place with lots of big birds. It was an airport.

Billy wanted to make friends with the big birds, but they didn't value Billy because he was so small. This made Billy sad. But he didn't give up. He thought of a plan to show the big birds how special he was.

One day, a big storm came to the airport. The big birds were scared and couldn't fly. But Billy was brave. He flew up into the sky and showed the big birds how to fly in the storm. The big birds saw how brave Billy was and they learned to value him. From that day on, Billy and the big birds were the best of friends.

Once there was a swan who flew high in the sky. The sky was clear and calm. The swan flew through the sky and stopped at the lake. The lake was so beautiful and peaceful.

The swan looked around and saw many other animals playing around the lake. The swan wanted to join the fun but it had to do something important first so it decided to delay the fun, for now.

The swan flew away from the lake and went in search of the most perfect feathers. The swan looked for a long time but it couldn't find the perfect feathers. Soon the sun was setting and the swan still hadn't found the feathers.

Finally, the swan spotted a beautiful feather in a tree. The swan immediately grabbed it and flew back to the lake. When it got there the swan noticed that the lake was even more beautiful at sunset.

The swan was so happy and proud of the feather it had found. The swan decided to delay playing with the other animals and spend some time just enjoying the sunset. The swan settled down and settled watched the calm beauty of the lake at sunset.

The swan was so content taking in the beauty and peacefulness of the lake. From then on, the swan always stopped to enjoy the calm beauty of the lake.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy and his mom went for a walk in the park. Suddenly, a big storm started. Timmy got scared and started crying.

His mom hugged him and said, "Don't be afraid, Timmy. The storm will pass soon." Timmy asked, "Why does the storm happen?" His mom explained, "Sometimes, the clouds get angry and start making loud noises. That's the storm."

As they walked back home, they saw a man who was lost. He asked for directions, but Timmy's mom didn't answer him. Timmy asked, "Why didn't you speak to him, Mom?" His mom replied, "I was ignorant, Timmy. I didn't want to help him. But we should always be kind and help others, even if we don't know them."

The moral of the story is that we should always be kind and help others, even if we don't know them.

Lily and Ben were playing with scissors and paper. They wanted to make shapes and animals. Lily had a shiny pair of scissors that cut very well. Ben had a dull pair of scissors that did not cut very well.

"Can I use your scissors, Lily?" Ben asked. "Mine are not good."

"No, these are mine!" Lily said. "You have your own scissors. Go away!"

Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to make a nice shape too. He tried to cut with his scissors, but they only made a small tear. He looked at Lily's scissors again. They were so shiny and sharp.

He decided to take them from her. He waited until she was busy with her paper. Then he grabbed her scissors and ran away.

"Hey, give them back!" Lily shouted. She ran after him. She was very mad.

They both ran around the room, holding the scissors. They did not see the rug on the floor. They tripped and fell. The scissors flew out of their hands. They landed on the couch.

Lily and Ben both cried. They had cuts on their knees and hands. They hurt a lot.

Mom heard them and came to see what happened. She saw the scissors and the paper and the cuts. She was very upset.

"What were you doing with the scissors?" she asked. "You know they are dangerous. You could have hurt yourselves or each other."

Lily and Ben both tried to explain. They both wanted the shiny scissors. They both demanded them. They both were sorry.

Mom hugged them and cleaned their cuts. She put band-aids on them. She told them to be careful and share. She took away the scissors and gave them crayons and stickers instead.

Lily and Ben said they were sorry to each other. They decided to make shapes and animals with crayons and stickers. They had fun and forgot about the scissors. They learned a lesson.

Once there was a thin house. In the garden, there was a trap. The trap was for catching rabbits. One day, it worked! The man was so happy that he went to bury the rabbit in the garden. He dug a very deep hole and put the rabbit in it. Then he filled the hole so the rabbit was safely buried. His work was done. The end.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. Swing is their favorite. They take turns on the swing. They push each other high and fast.

One day, Sara pushes Tom too hard. Tom flies off the swing. He falls on the ground. He cries. He has pain in his arm and leg. They are dirty and bloody. Sara is scared. She runs to Tom.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry. Are you okay?" Sara says.

Tom shakes his head. He still cries. He shows Sara his arm and leg.

"Ouch, that hurts. You need help. Come on, let's go to the nurse. She will make you better." Sara says.

She helps Tom stand up. They walk to the nurse. The nurse is kind. She cleans and bandages Tom's arm and leg. She gives him a hug and a sticker. Tom smiles. He feels better.

"Thank you, nurse. You are nice." Tom says.

"You're welcome, Tom. You are brave. Be careful next time, okay?" The nurse says.

Sara and Tom nod. They say goodbye to the nurse. They hold hands. They go back to the park. They play again. But they don't swing. They slide and jump. They are still friends. They have fun.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play by the river. They had a raft that they made from wood and rope. They liked to pretend they were pirates and explore the water.

One day, they saw a big red boat on the other side of the river. It looked like a fire boat, with a hose and a ladder. Tim wanted to go and see it, but Sam was scared.

"Let's go to the fire boat, Sam. It looks fun!" Tim said.

"No, Tim. It is too far and too dangerous. The water is fast and deep. And the fire boat might be spicy. It might burn us or spray us with water. We should mind our raft and stay here." Sam said.

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He was curious and brave. He took the raft and paddled towards the fire boat. Sam stayed on the shore and watched.

Tim got closer and closer to the fire boat. He saw some men in red suits and helmets. They looked busy and angry. They did not see Tim or his raft.

Suddenly, the fire boat made a loud noise. It was a siren. It was going to a fire somewhere. It started to move very fast. It made big waves in the water.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with pots and pans. They also liked to fill the sink with water and bubbles and wash the dishes. But they had to be careful not to make a mess or spill the water.

One day, Lily had a foolish idea. She saw a big plug in the sink that stopped the water from going away. She wondered what would happen if she removed it. She said to Tom, "Look, Tom, I have a surprise for you. Come and see."

Tom was curious and followed Lily to the sink. He saw the plug in her hand and the water in the sink. He said, "What are you going to do, Lily?"

Lily smiled and said, "Watch this!" She pulled the plug out of the sink and threw it on the floor. The water started to go away very fast. It made a loud noise and a big whirlpool.

Tom was scared and said, "Lily, stop! You are making a big mistake!"

But Lily did not listen. She thought it was fun and said, "Look, Tom, the water is going away. It is like a magic trick."

But the water did not go away completely. It went down the pipe and came back up from another pipe under the sink. It sprayed all over the kitchen and made a huge flood. It wet the floor, the walls, the cabinets, the stove, and the fridge. It also wet Lily and Tom and their clothes.

Lily and Tom were shocked and screamed. They tried to stop the water, but they could not. They ran out of the kitchen and called for their mom.

Mom came and saw the disaster. She was very angry and said, "Lily and Tom, what have you done? You have ruined the kitchen and wasted the water. You are very naughty and foolish. You are in big trouble."

Lily and Tom felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had never removed the plug from the sink. They learned their lesson and never played with the sink again.

"Why did it do that?" Tim asks. "Why did it hurt the tree?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mother went for a walk in the park. They saw some pretty flowers and decided to gather them. But then, Lily saw a little boy crying. He had lost his toy.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in Lily's room. Lily's room is messy. There are toys and clothes on the floor. Lily's mom tells them to clean up. But they do not listen. They want to have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who lived with her mommy and daddy. One day, when the girl was playing outside, she noticed a paper in the middle of the street. She quickly ran over to the paper and tried to pick it up. But the paper was too big and heavy for her to move.

"Doctor, can you help me?" asked Lily. The doctor smiled and said, "Of course, I can help you. Let me put a bandage on your hand." The doctor carefully put the bandage on Lily's hand. Lily felt better and thanked the doctor.

Lily went home and told her friends about the kind doctor. They all decided to be more careful when they played, so they wouldn't get hurt. They also learned that it was important to help others, just like the doctor helped Lily. The charming town became a happier place because everyone started to care for one another.

Tom and Mia are friends. They go to the same school. They like to play and learn together. Today, they have a quiz. The quiz is about animals. The quiz is important. The teacher says they have to study hard.

Tom and Mia go home after school. They have their books and pictures of animals. They want to study for the quiz. But Tom sees his bike. He likes his bike. He wants to ride his bike. He says to Mia, "Let's go to the park. We can ride our bikes. The quiz is easy. We know all the animals."

Mia shakes her head. She says, "No, Tom. We have to study. The quiz is not easy. We have to remember the names and sounds of the animals. The teacher will be sad if we do not do well. Come on, let's study."

Tom makes a face. He says, "No, Mia. I do not want to study. I want to have fun. Studying is boring. Riding bikes is fun. Come on, let's go to the park."

Mia and Tom are not happy. They are angry at each other. They do not know what to do. They want to be friends, but they have different ideas. They look at each other. They do not say anything. They are quiet.

One day, a fancy cat named Tom went for a walk. He saw a big truck. The truck was loading rocks. Tom wanted to help. He said, "Can I help load rocks too?"

The truck driver said, "Yes, you can help me!" Tom was very happy. He started to load rocks with the driver. They worked together and had fun.

Suddenly, there was an earthquake. The ground shook a lot. Tom was scared. The driver said, "Don't worry, Tom. I will keep you safe." They hid under the truck until the earthquake stopped.

When the earthquake was over, they went back to loading rocks. They finished the job and the driver thanked Tom for his help. Tom felt proud and went back home to tell his friends about his big adventure.

Ben and Mia were playing in the yard. They saw a big pile of ash near the fence. It was from the fire that burned the old shed last week.

"Look, ash!" Ben said. He picked up some and threw it in the air. It made a gray cloud.

"Stop, Ben!" Mia said. "Ash is dirty. It can hurt your eyes and nose."

Ben did not listen. He ran to the pile and dug a hole. He found something shiny inside. It was a metal spoon.

"Wow, a spoon!" Ben said. He showed it to Mia. "Maybe we can feed the birds with it."

Mia liked the idea. She ran to the house and got some bread. She tore it into small pieces. She and Ben filled the spoon with bread and walked to the big tree. There were many birds on the branches. They had wide wings and bright colors.

"Hello, birds!" Mia said. "We have food for you. Come and eat!"

The birds saw the bread and flew down. They landed on the ground and pecked at the spoon. Ben and Mia smiled. They felt happy to feed the birds.

But one bird was not happy. It was a crow. It had black feathers and a sharp beak. It did not like the bread. It wanted the spoon. It flew to the pile of ash and waited.

When Ben and Mia were not looking, it swooped down and grabbed the spoon. It flew away with it.

"Hey, that's our spoon!" Ben shouted. He and Mia ran after the crow. But the crow was too fast. It flew over the fence and disappeared.

Ben and Mia were sad. They lost their spoon. They went back to the yard and sat on the grass.

"Maybe we can find another spoon," Mia said.

"Maybe," Ben said. "But I liked that one. It was shiny and special."

They hugged each other and looked at the sky. They hoped the crow would bring back their spoon someday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, she found a big, red tomato. She picked it up and held it in her hands. It was heavy, and she wondered how much it weighed.

Lily loved her peaceful garden, but one day a big, mean dog came and scared her. She ran away, leaving her tomato behind. The dog saw the tomato and ate it all up. Lily was sad that she lost her tomato, but she was happy that the dog was peaceful again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who liked to go camping. One summer day, the family decided to take a long drive to their favorite cabin. 

As they drove, they could see a lot of trees and hills. When they arrived, they were excited to explore. 

They opened the door to the cabin and stepped inside. Suddenly, they heard a loud clatter! A clumsy bear was rummaging around the kitchen. The family gasped in shock and stepped back. 

"Oh no!" the mom said. The dad grabbed their camping bag and said, "Let's go!" 

The family quickly ran out of the cabin and into their car. As they drove away, they could still hear the clumsy bear say, "Oh hi!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his drum. He would bang on it all day long. One day, Timmy went outside to play. It was very cold outside, and everything was icy. Timmy's friend, Billy, came over to play.

"Can we play together?" asked Billy.

"Sure!" said Timmy. "Let's play our drums."

They played their drums and had fun. Then Timmy had an idea. "Let's whistle while we play!" he said.

They started to whistle and play their drums. But then, Timmy slipped on the icy ground and fell. He hit his head and got hurt.

"Oh no!" cried Billy. "We need to get help!"

They called for Timmy's mom, but it was too late. Timmy had hurt himself too badly. From then on, Billy never played with his drum or whistled again. He always remembered the bad ending to their fun day of playing.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the bus stop. He saw a big, red bus coming. Tim was happy because he liked to ride the bus. It was fun to go up and down the hills.

On the bus, Tim met a new friend. Her name was Sue. Sue had a tasty snack. She shared her snack with Tim. They both liked the snack a lot. Sue mentioned that she got the snack from her mom.

Then, the bus stopped. Tim and Sue were sad because it was time to go home. They said goodbye and got off the bus. Tim walked home, but he felt sad because he missed his new friend Sue. The day was not so fun anymore.

Charlie loved to wear colourful clothes. But one day, Charlie spilled some paints on his favourite red cloth and it was ruined! Charlie was very sad.

As Charlie's mum hugged him, she knew that there was only one way to heal the cloth. She took her special needle and thread and stitched it carefully.

Charlie watched as his mum worked hard to fix the cloth. His mum was so kind, unlike the selfish man who had made a mess of the cloth.

Soon, the cloth was as good as new. Seeing the repaired cloth, Charlie was so happy that it was healed!  He hugged his mum and thanked her for all her hard work.

Mikey was a cute 3 year old boy. He was marchin around the house having fun. He went up to his mom and said, "Mommy, where is my bookcase?".

His mom smiled and said, "It's right over there, Mikey!" She pointed to a bookcase in the corner of the room. 

Mikey instantly started marching over to it. He began to take out all the books from the bookcase, one by one! 

His mom laughed, "Mikey, what are you doing?".

Mikey replied, "I'm marching in a line with all the books!". His mom smiled and said, "That's so cute Mikey, go ahead and keep marching. I'll get the books back in the bookcase later." 

And so, Mikey marched around the living room with a line of books behind him. He was so cute and so proud of himself for marching with the books.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day she was exploring when she noticed a tall tree. The little girl wanted to climb the tree! But she was too small. Then she had an idea. She found a clear bucket and put it upside down. She climbed on the bucket and it was just high enough to reach the lowest branch of the tree. She grabbed hold of the branch and started to climb.

The little girl slowly made her way to the top of the tree. She was almost there when suddenly the branch she was standing on started to shake. She held on tight and kept climbing. Finally she reached the very top. The view was amazing!

The little girl looked down at the clear bucket and smiled. She had done it. She had climbed the tree! Now she could see even further.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside in the sunshine. He liked to hop and bounce around in the grass. One day, Benny saw a big, dark frame hanging on the wall of his house. He wondered what it was for.

Benny hopped over to the frame and looked at it closely. It was a picture frame! Benny was so excited. He had never seen a picture frame before. He hopped up and down and bounced around the room. Then, he decided to find a picture to put in the frame.

Benny looked all around the house for a picture to put in the frame. Finally, he found a picture of his family. He carefully put the picture in the frame and hung it back up on the wall. Benny felt so proud of himself. He had done something special all by himself. From that day on, he would hop and bounce around the house, admiring his family's picture in the dark frame.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books, but some of the words were too hard for her to understand. One day, she asked her mom, "Can you help me with these big words?"

Her mom said, "Sure, let's find some books with easier words."

Lily was happy because the new books were more modern and had simpler words. She said, "These books are much better! They improve my reading."

Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like them. Remember, learning new words is important, but it's also important to find books that are just right for you."

Once upon a time, there was a honest boy. He always told the truth. One day, he was walking through a park when he saw a bush. He stopped to take a look. He noticed something strange: there was a tall man standing in the bush! The man was dressed all in black. At first, the boy was scared. But then he remembered that he was an honest boy and decided to stand up for himself. He slowly walked towards the man and asked "Who are you?". The man smiled and said "I am the guardian of the bush. I make sure nothing bad happens here". The boy smiled, he was relieved. He thanked the man and then went on his way.

John was on a journey to find a clear lake. He could see it in the distance, shimmering in the sunlight. He was so excited! 
John ran to the edge of the lake and started to pick up some rocks. He wanted to skim them across the water.

Suddenly, John heard a loud sound. He looked around and saw that the big rock he had just picked up had broken into two pieces! John was sad, but he soon cheered up when he realised that he could still skim the two pieces of rock. 

He was having so much fun that he didn't even notice that a friendly bluebird had been watching him from the branches of a nearby tree.

The bluebird fluttered down next to John and said in a soft voice: "You have a very clear journey ahead of you, John. I think you'll be able to find bigger, better rocks ahead." 

John smiled and said thank you to the bluebird. He was so happy to have a special new friend! With that, John skipped off, ready to continue on his journey.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cat named Tom. Tom was very good at fighting. He liked to look at himself in the mirror. One day, Tom saw another cat in the mirror. He thought it was a new friend.

Tom said, "Hi, friend! Let's play and not fight." But the cat in the mirror did not say anything. Tom was sad. He wanted to be friends with the cat in the mirror.

Tom's owner, a little girl named Sue, saw Tom looking at the mirror. She said, "Tom, that is you in the mirror! You are famous for being a good fighter, but you don't need to fight yourself." Tom looked at Sue and then at the mirror. He finally understood. From that day on, Tom was happy to see himself in the mirror and never tried to fight the cat he saw there.
