Once, there was a little girl named Jenny. She had a pet dog called Biscuit. Jenny loved playing with Biscuit and taking him for walks. Every night, Jenny would pray for Biscuit before she went to bed.

One day, something strange happened. Jenny noticed Biscuit was behaving very weirdly. Whenever Jenny called him, Biscuit ran in the other direction. He acted like he was scared of something. Jenny was worried, so she prayed for Biscuit to feel better.

The next day, Biscuit was still acting weird. But Jenny felt a bit better knowing he was safe. Then, suddenly, Jenny heard a noise coming from outside. She ran to the window and saw an alligator in her backyard with Biscuit in its mouth! Jenny was scared, but she remembered her prayers. She ran into her garden, clapped her hands and shouted at the alligator. Surprisingly, the alligator dropped Biscuit and ran away! Jenny thanked God for answering her prayers. 

From that day onward, Biscuit and Jenny were very careful of weird things in the backyard. Jenny still prayed for Biscuit every night, and they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there lived a family of three. They had an adorable refrigerator which they owned. One day the father asked his three year old son to come over to the refrigerator.
"Come and see what I got for you," he said.
The little boy quickly ran to his father. He was so excited to see what his father had got for him.
When he arrived to the refrigerator, the little boy opened it and saw there was a big cake inside. It was a chocolate cake with frosting and colourful sprinkles.
The little boy could not believe his eyes. He was so happy and said,
"Thank you Daddy! This is so adorable!"

His father smiled and replied,
"You are very welcome, son. Now let's cut the cake and have some delicious slices!"

Mina lived with her mom and dad. One day she wanted a treat. So she asked her mom, "Mom, can I have a treat?". Her mom said, "Sure Mina, let's go to the store and get a ice cream bar for you."

Mina was so happy. She put on her shoes and went to the store with her mom. When they arrived, Mina saw lots of ice cream bars. She picked one with her favorite flavour and showed it to her mom. Her mom said, "That looks yummy, let's pay for it." So they paid and Mina held her treat in her hand.

On their way home, they passed a fountain. Mina wanted to soak her feet in it, so she asked her mom if she could do it. Her mom said, "Yes, but first you have to be very careful not to slip, okay?"

Mina put her feet gently in the cool water with her mom's help. When she was done, she felt very refreshed. She thanked her mom for being helpful and then ran back home with her treat.

Lily and her mom went to the store. Lily wanted a toy, but mom said no. Lily was mad. She yelled and cried. She kicked and threw things. Mom was sad and angry.

A nice man who worked at the store came to help. He had a big smile and a badge. He said his name was Ben. He was reliable. He knew how to calm down kids. He gave Lily a sticker and a balloon. He talked to her softly. He asked her why she was upset.

Lily stopped yelling. She looked at Ben. She said she wanted a toy. Ben said he understood. He said toys were fun, but mom had to pay for them. He said mom had a budget. He said a budget was a plan for money. He said Lily could help mom by being good and saving money.

Lily thought about it. She liked stickers and balloons. She liked Ben. She loved mom. She said she was sorry. She hugged mom. Mom hugged her back. She said she was proud of Lily. She said they could look at toys, but not buy them. She said maybe they could buy one later, if they had enough money.

Lily agreed. She said thank you to Ben. Ben said you're welcome. He said he was happy to help. He said he hoped to see them again. He waved goodbye. Lily and mom waved back. They walked around the store. They looked at toys. They had fun. They did not yell. They were happy.

Sammy was a little girl who loved to sing and dance. Every day she sang her favorite song with her family in the living room.

One day, Sammy's mom said, "We have to be obedient and help each other, no matter what." Sammy smiled and nodded, not understanding why her mom said those things.

The following day, Sammy and her family went on a long journey. They had to struggle for a long time before they reached their destination. Along the way, Sammy sang her favorite song to help boost the family's morale.

When they finally arrived, Sammy saw why her mom had said they needed to be obedient and help each other. The family was on top of a very large mountain, and Sammy realized they would have to struggle together to get down.

Sammy used her singing to keep spirits high, and the family worked together to make it down the mountain. They were all obedient, and they were eventually able to return home.

Sammy realized that when her mom said they need to be obedient and help each other, she was foreshadowing the journey they would have to make. Sammy was thankful for her mom's wisdom and her song that had helped them make it back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved going to her classroom. She loved her teacher and all her friends. She was very graceful when she walked and always tried to be kind to everyone.

One day, a new girl named Emma came to their classroom. Emma was not very nice to Lily and her friends. She took their toys and made fun of them. Lily didn't know what to do. She tried to be nice to Emma and share her toys, but Emma still wasn't nice.

Lily talked to her teacher about the problem and together they tried to talk to Emma about being kind. Emma listened and started to be nicer to everyone. Now Lily and Emma are friends and they both walk gracefully in their classroom, happy to be together.

Tom and Lily wanted to help Mom make a cake. They put on their aprons and went to the kitchen. Mom smiled and said, "Thank you for helping me. You can provide the eggs and the flour."

Tom and Lily nodded and ran to the fridge and the cupboard. They brought back the eggs and the flour and put them on the table. Mom cracked the eggs and poured them into a big bowl. She asked Lily to stir them with a spoon. Lily stirred and stirred until the eggs were yellow and smooth.

Mom added the flour and some sugar and milk to the bowl. She asked Tom to stir them with a spoon. Tom stirred and stirred until the batter was thick and sweet. Mom poured the batter into a round pan. She said, "Now we need to bake the cake in the stove. Can you help me carry the pan?"

Tom and Lily lifted the pan with their hands. They followed Mom to the stove. Mom opened the oven door and slid the pan inside. She said, "The cake will be ready in half an hour. We need to wait and let it cook."

Tom and Lily nodded and sat on the floor. They played with their toys and talked about the cake. They wondered how it would taste and what they would put on top. They were very excited and hungry. They hoped the cake would fit in their mouths.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the rain, but one day it rained too fast and she got very wet. She ran inside to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I'm all wet!"

Her mommy said, "Let's get you dry." She gave Lily a big towel to dry herself off with. Just then, the doorbell rang. It was Lily's friend, Timmy. Timmy said, "Lily, I have a present for you!" Lily was excited to receive the present, but Timmy said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I forgot the present at home."

Lily was sad and started to cry. Her mommy said, "It's okay, Lily. We can still have fun inside." They played games and read books together. Lily soon forgot about the present and was happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was only three years old and he wanted to win something. So he asked his mum for an idea. She suggested that he compete in a race.

Jack was very excited about the race. All his friends were also in the competition, some even older than him. Jack was a bit frightened but he stayed strong and didn't give up.

When the race started, Jack was the first to finish. Everyone cheered with delight when he crossed the finish line. Jack was so happy!

When he went home that day, he got some fantastic news. He had won the race! Jack was overjoyed, he couldn't believe it. He was so happy that he had won.

Jack raced back to tell his mum the good news. She was also very happy. Jack felt super proud that he had won the race, and he will never forget the feeling of being a winner.

One day, there was a little girl called Jenny. She wanted to get creative, so she went outside and looked around the garden. She saw a big tree and decided to play around it. But then, it started to get cold. Jenny knew she needed a sweater.

She went inside and asked her mom if she could have a sweater. Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can." 

So Jenny put on the sweater. She felt warm and cozy. She went back outside and started playing around the big tree. She was feeling so creative! 

But then, she noticed something funny about the sweater. It was getting bigger and bigger. Oh no! It turned out that the sweater was a magical sweater that was growing bigger and bigger! 

In the end, Jenny had to stay outside in the cold all night because her mom didn't know how to make the sweater smaller. Jenny was so sad and cold but she eventually learned her lesson: never wear magical sweaters!

Joey was excited because it was his birthday. He got bigger balloons than usual, and his favorite toys.

Joey said to his mom, "I love all these presents, mommy." 

His mom smiled and said, "You can play and enjoy your day, honey." 

Joey smiled and began to play. He got a fake sword, and pretended to be a knight. He kept playing and running around the house. 

He yawned and his mom asked, "Are you tired, Joey?" 

Joey replied, "No, mommy, I'm having fun!" 

His mom chuckled and said, "Ok, but don't forget lunch soon!" 

Joey didn't want to stop but he knew lunch was important. So he stopped playing and ate a snack. 

Then he went back to playing, and he enjoyed the rest of his birthday.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Jane and she was three years old. She was very happy and really liked to skip. Every day she would put on her shoes and go outside.

One day, Jane saw a loop drawn in the dirt. She ran over to the loop and smiled. She liked to pretend the loop was a game. She was ready to play!

She started to skip around the loop. She counted to ten every time she went around. After a few times, she began to get faster. She skipped and laughed, having lots of fun.

When it was time to go home, Jane was not ready. She wanted to keep playing! But she knew she had to go, so she said goodbye to the loop and skipped back home. The next day, Jane couldn't wait to go back and play!

Once there was a girl who liked to wash her hands. She was so enthusiastic about it that she washed them all the time. Every morning, she would get up and wash her hands before she even brushed her teeth.

One day, she got a journal for her birthday. She was so excited that she wanted to write in it right away. But before she could start, she had to wash her hands first. The girl was so excited to get started on the journal that she was done washing much faster than usual.

The girl used her journal every single day to write about her days and her thoughts. Every evening, she would always make sure to wash her hands before writing in it. She found that she was a much more enthusiastic writer when she made sure to wash her hands first.

Once upon a time there was a bird. He wanted to fly high in the sky so he tried and tried. But he kept falling down. One day, he met an old bird and the old bird said, "I can teach you how to fly." The bird was very excited! He followed the old bird and found out the secret. 

He had to flap his wings very hard, jump and use the wind. The old bird said, "It is not easy, but if you try you can succeed!" The bird tried and tried, and after many hours of practise he could fly!

But then he noticed that the old bird was not flying. "Why don't you fly?" asked the bird. The old bird replied, "I am too old to fly now, but I am happy for you." The bird was sad that the old bird could not fly.

The bird promised that he would always share the sky. He would look after all the birds and tell them his secret. But one day, he saw a bird being selfish and taking all the sky for himself. 

The bird knew what he had to do. He flew to the selfish bird and reminded him to share the sky. Everyone can succeed if they help each other. In the end, they all flew together and enjoyed the blue sky.

Mum was walking through the park. Suddenly, she heard a whistle. It was coming from an elderly man, sitting on a park bench. He had a doll in his hand and he was playing with it.

Mum stopped to look at the man. He was wearing a funny hat and had a big smile.

Mum smiled and asked, "What are you playing with?"

The elderly man answered, "It's my doll. I like to make it whistle."

Mum smiled again. She had never seen someone play with a doll like that before.

The elderly man kept whistling as he played with the doll. Mum watched him for a few minutes before she had to go. It was really nice to see someone having such fun.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl. She wanted to go outside and play in the sunshine. She ran out the door and jumped around. She loved to move! 

Suddenly she saw a bubble, just sitting in the air. It was the most beautiful bubble she had ever seen. She clapped with joy and ran over to the bubble. She touched it and carefully watched it move. 

The bubble was so original! She laughed as she saw it float around. She waved goodbye to the bubble as it moved away. She had so much fun with the bubble and would never forget it! 

The little girl ran back inside, excited to tell her family all about her adventure.

Lily and Ben love to play music. They have a band with their toys. Lily plays the drum and Ben plays the guitar. They sing loud and have fun.

One day, they see a big snowman in the park. He has a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They want to play with him.

"Hello, snowman!" Lily says. "Do you want to join our band?"

The snowman does not answer. He does not move.

"Maybe he is shy," Ben says. "Or maybe he is cold. Let's give him a hug."

They run to the snowman and hug him. He is very cold and hard.

"Ouch!" Lily says. "He is not soft. He is like ice."

"He is frozen," Ben says. "That's why he does not talk or play. He is not a real person. He is made of snow."

Lily and Ben feel sad. They want a friend to play with.

"Maybe we can make him happy," Lily says. "Maybe we can play music for him. Maybe he will like it."

They go back to their band and start to play. They play a long song for the snowman. They hope he will smile.

The snowman does not smile. He does not move. He does not hear them. He is frozen.

Lily and Ben stop playing. They look at the snowman.

"He does not like our music," Lily says. "He does not like anything. He is not a good friend."

"Let's go home," Ben says. "We have each other. We are a good band."

They take their toys and leave. They do not look at the snowman. He is frozen.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But today they are bored. They want to do something new.

"Let's play guess," Sara says. "I will think of something and you will ask me questions. You have to guess what it is."

"OK," Ben says. "Is it a toy?"

"No, it is not a toy," Sara says.

"Is it big or small?" Ben asks.

"It is big," Sara says.

"Is it in our room?" Ben asks.

"Yes, it is in our room," Sara says.

Ben looks around the room. He sees the bed, the closet, the rug, the lamp, the window, and the bookshelf. He thinks hard.

"Is it the bookshelf?" he guesses.

"Yes, you are right!" Sara says. "You are good at guessing."

Ben smiles. He likes to guess. He likes the bookshelf. It has many books. Some are funny, some are scary, some are pretty. He picks one book. It has a picture of a dragon on the cover.

"Can we read this book?" he asks Sara.

"Sure," Sara says. "It is not an ordinary book. It is a magic book. It can take us to a different world."

They sit on the bed and open the book. They see the dragon fly in the sky. They see a castle, a forest, a river. They hear a voice.

"Welcome to the land of dragons," the voice says. "Are you ready for an adventure?"

Sara and Ben nod. They are not bored anymore. They are excited. They enter the book and start their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jen. She loved to go outside and play but one day a storm came and Jen had to remain indoors. She was very sad and didn't know what to do, so she went to take a nap. When she was sleeping, the storm stopped and the sun came out.

Jen was so happy that she jumped out of bed and ran outside. All her friends were playing and having a lot of fun. Jen wanted to join them so she asked if she could play too. They said yes and welcomed her with open arms.

Jen was so excited and she had fun the whole day, but she remembered that she had taken a nap instead of playing with her friends. She knew it was wrong so she apologized to them. 

Her friends said it was ok and that it was not her fault that the storm had come. They hugged Jen and all went back to playing together. Jen was so happy that she promised to never remain indoors when it was sunny and to always join her friends when they wanted to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to zip around in his yard. One day, the sun was warm, and Tim went outside to play.

Tim saw a big ball on the ground. It was as big as the earth! He kicked the ball and it went up, up, up into the sky. Tim was so happy to see it fly.

Tim's mom came out to watch him play. She gave him a warm hug. They played with the big ball all day long. Tim loved to zip around the earth with his mom. They had lots of fun together.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play hide and seek. One day, they decided to hide in the laundry room, where their mom had a big pile of clothes to wash. They crawled under the clothes and waited for their dad to find them.

But their dad was busy making lunch and did not hear them when they shouted "ready or not, here we come!" He turned on the washing machine and put some clothes in it. He did not see Lily and Ben under the pile.

Lily and Ben heard the water and the noise and got scared. They tried to escape from the laundry, but it was too heavy and too hot. They started to cry and call for help.

Their mom heard them and ran to the laundry room. She saw the washing machine and the clothes and realized what had happened. She quickly turned off the machine and pulled out Lily and Ben. They were wet and dirty and scared.

She hugged them and said "I'm so glad you're okay. You should never hide in the laundry, it's dangerous. Next time, find a safer place to play, okay?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said "sorry, mom. We won't do it again." They were not enthusiastic about hide and seek anymore. They decided to play with their toys instead.

Once there was a little boy who liked to poke things. One day, he decided to poke his sister. He thought it would be funny. But his sister didn't like it. She got angry and started to yell at him. She said, "Stop poking me!" 

The little boy tried to apologize, but his sister wasn't listening. She kept yelling. Soon enough, they had a fight. 

The boy was very sorry. He knew it was wrong to poke his sister. So, he hugged her and said, "I'm sorry." 

His sister accepted his apology and hugged him back. She said, "That's ok. Let's not fight anymore." 

The little boy was so happy that the fight was over. From then on, he stopped poking people and always made sure to apologize when he made a mistake.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and helpful bear named Benny. Benny loved to explore the world around him and make new friends. One day, Benny found himself in a messy forest where the animals didn't know how to organize their homes. Benny knew he had to help.

Benny started by teaching the animals how to tidy up their homes. He showed them how to put their toys away and make their beds. The animals were grateful for Benny's helpfulness and soon the forest was looking much better.

The animals were so happy with the changes that they decided to organize a big party to celebrate. Benny was excited to attend and see all his new friends having fun. When he arrived, he was surprised to see that they had organized the party just for him! Benny was so grateful for their kindness and felt happy to have made such wonderful friends in the world.

Lily liked to play with her mom's things. She liked to look at the shiny rings and necklaces in the box. She liked to try them on and pretend she was a princess. But her mom always told her not to touch them. She said they were very special and expensive.

One day, Lily was alone in the house. Her mom had gone to the store and her dad was at work. She was bored and curious. She went to her mom's room and opened the box. She saw a big ring with a blue stone. It sparkled like the sky. She wanted to wear it. She put it on her finger and smiled.

She heard a knock on the door. She ran to see who it was. She forgot to close the box. She forgot to take off the ring. She opened the door and saw a man. He had a big bag and a hat. He smiled at her.

"Hello, little girl," he said. "Is your mom home?"

Lily shook her head. She was shy and scared. She did not know the man.

"That's too bad," he said. "I have a package for her. Can I come in and wait for her?"

Lily nodded. She did not want to be rude. She let the man in. She did not see him look at the ring on her finger. She did not see him look at the box in her mom's room.

The man followed her to the living room. He put his bag on the couch. He asked her some questions. He pretended to be nice. He waited for his chance.

When Lily was not looking, he grabbed his bag and ran to her mom's room. He opened the box and took all the rings and necklaces. He also took the ring from Lily's finger. He hurt her. She cried.

He ran out of the house. He slammed the door. He had a big smile. He had a lot of money.

Lily was alone and sad. She had lost her mom's things. She had lost the ring. She had a red mark on her finger. She did not know what to do.

She heard her mom's car in the driveway. She heard her mom's voice. She was angry and scared.

"Lily, what happened? Where are my things? Where is the ring? Who did this to you?"

Lily could not answer. She could only cry. She had made a big mistake. She had let a bad man in. She had broken her mom's rule. She had lost her mom's trust. She wished she had been more organized. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had never seen the ring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spaghetti for dinner. One day, her mom made her spaghetti with meatballs. Lily was so happy and ate it all up. 

After dinner, Lily felt tired and wanted to take a nap. Her mom said, "Okay, Lily, go take a nap now." Lily went to her room and fell asleep.

While Lily was napping, she had a scary dream. In her dream, she was lost in a big forest. She saw a scary monster and ran away. When she woke up, she told her mom about her dream. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. It was just a dream. I'm here to protect you." 

Lily felt better and smiled. She was glad her mom was there to keep her safe. From that day on, Lily always ate spaghetti with meatballs for dinner and took a nap after. She knew she would have sweet dreams and her mom would be there to protect her. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very adventurous and loved to explore. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a big slide. She climbed up the ladder and slid down so fast, it made her hair fly back. 

When she got to the bottom, she saw a big frame with lots of colors. It was like a big picture with no picture inside. She wondered what it was for. Suddenly, her mom called her over and showed her a new jacket she had bought. It had a zipper that went up and down. Lily loved it and kept zipping it up and down all day. 

As the sun started to set, Lily and her mom went home. She couldn't wait to go back to the park and explore even more. But for now, she was happy with her new jacket and the fun she had on the slide.

Anna loved to fly. She had a big red kite that she took to the park with her dad. She ran and ran until the kite went up in the sky. She felt the wind pull on the string and watched the kite dance in the air. She smiled and laughed.

Ben loved to dance. He had a blue radio that he took to the park with his mom. He turned on the music and jumped and spun and twirled. He felt the rhythm in his feet and watched the birds sing along. He smiled and laughed.

One day, Anna and Ben met at the park. They saw each other's kite and radio and wanted to try them. They shared and swapped and played together. They flew the kite and danced to the music. They felt happy and peaceful. They smiled and laughed.

They became friends and came back to the park every week. They flew and danced and had fun. They learned new words and songs and games. They grew and changed and loved. They smiled and laughed.

One day, little Jack and his mommy went to the subway. Jack's mommy said, "We have to reach the subway fast!" So they rushed to the subway station, but the mommy and Jack were too late.

The subway door closed and it drove away without them. Jack was sad. His mommy was too. 

But then, Jack noticed something on his mommy's face. She had a big smile. "What's that?" asked Jack. His mommy said to him, "Let's take a ride on the bus."

On the bus, they passed a stand selling sour candy. Jack was very excited. His mommy said, "You can get some if we reach our stop." So, Jack and his mommy rode the bus for a long time.

Finally, they reached their stop. Jack and his mommy got off and Jack got some sour candy at the stand. Jack was so happy. His mommy smiled, too. She said, "I knew if we kept trying, we could still reach our goal!"

Tom is a big boy. He likes to help Mom and Dad with the house. Today, he wants to use the mop. The mop is brown and soft. It can make the floor clean and shiny.

Mom says, "Tom, you can use the mop, but be careful. Don't spill the water. And don't mop the rug. The rug is not for mopping."

Tom nods. He takes the mop and the bucket. He fills the bucket with water and soap. He dips the mop in the bucket. He squeezes the mop. He starts to mop the floor.

Tom mops the kitchen. He mops the living room. He mops the hallway. He is happy. He is doing a good job. He sings a song. "Mop, mop, mop the floor. Make it clean and shiny. Mop, mop, mop the floor. I am a big boy."

But Tom forgets what Mom said. He mops the rug. The rug is in the bedroom. The rug is blue and fluffy. The rug does not like the mop. The mop makes the rug wet and soapy. The rug turns brown and soggy.

Mom hears Tom's song. She goes to the bedroom. She sees the rug. She sees the mop. She sees Tom. She is not happy. She says, "Tom, what did you do? You mopped the rug. The rug is not for mopping. The rug is ruined. You made a big mess."

Tom is sad. He did not mean to ruin the rug. He says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted to use the mop. I wanted to help. I forgot what you said."

Mom sighs. She says, "Tom, I know you wanted to help. But you have to listen to me. The mop is for the floor. The rug is for the bed. You have to be careful with the mop. You have to learn the rules."

Tom nods. He says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I will listen to you. I will learn the rules. I will be careful with the mop."

Mom hugs Tom. She says, "It's okay, Tom. I love you. You are a big boy. But you are still learning. Come on, let's clean up the mess. And then we can get a new rug. A rug that is not brown and soggy."

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Susie. She was three years old and she liked to help her Mommy do things around the house. Today Mommy had some clean pills that she needed Susie to take. Susie was a bit afraid of pills, but Mommy said they would taste good. 

Susie popped the pill into her mouth and chewed it up. She waited for it to taste good, but it didn't. It tasted like yucky medicine. Then Susie drank some water, and the pill tasted better. Susie smiled to herself, the pill tasted nice and clean now. 

Mommy told Susie that taking the pill would help her feel better, and sure enough, after Susie took it, she felt really good. She thanked Mommy for helping her take the pill. Then she went outside to play. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat blueberries because they were her favorite fruit. One day, she saw her friend Sarah with a big bowl of blueberries and she felt envious. 

Lily asked Sarah if she could have some blueberries, but Sarah said no. So, Lily decided to march home and ask her mom for some blueberries. 

When she got home, Lily's mom gave her a big bowl of blueberries to eat. Lily was so happy and she shared some with her little brother. From that day on, Lily learned that it's always better to share instead of feeling envious.

Once upon a time, there was a soft goose. She wanted to go on an adventure and explore the world. So one day, she stepped out of her nest to start her journey.

The goose stepped through the tall grass, trying to find something interesting. She stepped through a wide field, a shady forest and a bubbling river. After walking for a while, the goose heard something. It was a loud honking sound!

The goose stepped closer and saw two geese calling to each other. They were her family! The goose ran up to them and they were so happy to be together. They hugged and snuggled, and the goose was so glad to be back with them. 

The goose and her family stepped together back through the tall grass, across the wide field, through the shady forest and back to their cozy nest. They cuddled up in the soft nest, and the goose was so happy. 

The moral of the story is that family is the most important thing and no matter how far you go, it's always nice to be together.

It was evening when three little people took a walk. An old man, a young woman and little Timmy. Timmy was only three years old and as they walked, he stared at the beautiful sky. He watched the stars twinkle and the moon shine brightly. It made him smile.

Then he looked to the ground and saw something he had never seen before. It was an animal. It was small and helpless and didn't move. Timmy stared at it and wondered why it was there. The old man and the young woman stopped to have a look too.

The old man said that the animal was asleep and that it would be okay by morning. He said it was time to go home and that they should leave the animal be. Little Timmy wasn't sure, he felt a bit helpless and kept his eyes on the animal until they had gone. He wanted to make sure it would still be there when morning came.

Once upon a time there was a lamb called Spark. He was very hungry and alone in the big wide world. He had no one to care for him and he regretted not having friends.

One day, Spark heard a friendly voice from a nearby bush. He shyly peeped out and saw a wise old fox. The fox asked Spark why he was so sad and Spark said that he was very hungry and alone. 

The fox chuckled and said she knew just the thing to make him feel better. She led the little lamb to a patch of grass with lots of tasty leaves and Spark ate until he was full.

He thanked the fox for being so kind and help him. Spark realized he didn't need to regret feeling alone, because now he had a new friend. They both had a happy day, playing and exploring the wonderful world around them.

Ted and his Mom were on their way to the store. Ted had never been to a store before and was so excited. As they walked, Ted stared at all the different sights. He saw tall buildings and luxury cars. It was amazing!

When they got to the store, Ted couldn't believe his eyes. Inside were shelves filled with different treats and gifts. Ted stared in wonder at the rows of brightly colored things. He wanted to buy them all!

Mom showed Ted how to shop slowly and carefully. She said that sometimes luxury items cost more than others. When it was time to pay, Ted stared in amazement at the cash register. He had never seen so much money before!

Finally, Ted and his mom left the store. Ted was so excited about the things he bought that he had a hard time walking slow. As they walked back home, Ted stared in wonder at all the sights. He knew that his first store trip was something he would never forget.

One day, a small boy named Sam went to the park with his mom. He was very excited. He wanted to discover new things.

Suddenly, Sam discovered a mailbox on the ground. He opened it and found some small letters inside. He took them out and showed them to his mom.

Sam said, "Look, Mom! I found some small letters!"

His mom smiled and said, "That's great Sam! Let's find out who these are from."

So they opened the letters and they discovered they were from Sam's uncle. Sam was so happy that he had discovered these letters.

From that day on, Sam kept looking for more mail in the park, hoping to discover something special.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big boot that he found in his yard. Tim loved his boot very much. He would play with it every day.

One day, Tim saw a tiny bug near his boot. The bug was trying to pinch the boot with its little legs. Tim thought it was funny. He wanted to help the bug be successful in pinching the boot.

So, Tim picked up the bug and put it on the boot. The bug pinched the boot again and again. The bug was very happy and successful. Tim was happy too. From that day on, Tim and the bug played with the boot together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. He loved to design things. One day, he saw a big squash in his garden. Tim thought it was brilliant.

Tim ran to his friend, Sam. "Look at my squash!" said Tim. "It's so big and brilliant! Let's design something with it!"

Sam agreed. They took the squash and made a big funny face on it. They used leaves for the hair and sticks for the mouth. It looked very funny.

They showed their design to their friends. Everyone laughed and clapped. Tim and Sam felt so happy. They had a great day with their brilliant squash design.

Once there was an old man who lived in a small house. One day, the old man started to put some bricks around the house. He worked all day and when the sun went down, he smiled and said. "Now, it's finished".

The next morning the old man started to put something in the little space between the bricks. When he was finished, he said. "This is my secret".

A few days later, a little girl called Alice came over. She had a big smile on her face and asked the old man. "What is it?" The old man just smiled back. "You'll have to wait and see", he said. 

Alice waited for days and days. Finally, the old man said. "It's time". He opened up the little space between the bricks and inside Alice found a beautiful flowerpot with a beautiful flower in it. 

Alice was so happy and thanked the old man. She knew it was a special gift from the old man. 

The old man smiled and said, "Anything for you, young one".

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim was very adventurous, he loved to explore and discover new things. One day, Tim's family went on a trip to the beach. While they were there, a big hurricane came. The wind was very strong and the waves were huge. Tim and his family struggled to stay safe.

The hurricane was very scary, but Tim was brave. He helped his family by holding onto them tightly. After the hurricane passed, Tim and his family saw that the beach was very different. There were many shells and rocks that the hurricane had brought. Tim was very happy because he loved collecting shells.

Even though they had struggled during the hurricane, Tim and his family still had a fun and adventurous trip. Tim was happy that he got to experience something new and exciting.

Once upon a time, there was a weak little bird named Tim. He had a hard time flying like the other birds. One day, he saw a big tree with a symbol on it. The symbol was a picture of a bird with strong wings.

Tim asked his friend, Sam the squirrel, "What does the symbol mean?" Sam said, "It means that if you turn around the tree three times, you will get strong wings like the bird in the picture."

Tim wanted to try it. He turned around the tree once, twice, and then three times. Suddenly, he felt stronger! He flapped his wings and flew up into the sky. He was so happy that he could fly like the other birds. From that day on, Tim and Sam played together in the sky and the trees, and they were the best of friends.

Lily and Max were excited to play outside. It was fall and the leaves were red, yellow and orange. They looked like fire on the ground. Lily and Max wanted to make a big pile of leaves and jump in it.

They found a rake in the shed and took turns to drag it over the grass. They made a big pile of leaves near the big tree. They laughed and shouted as they threw more leaves on the pile. They were having so much fun.

Then they saw something shiny in the pile. It was a small star. It was glowing like a light. Lily and Max were amazed. They picked up the star and held it in their hands. It was warm and soft. They wondered where it came from.

They decided to keep the star as a secret. They put it in a box and hid it under the bed. They said good night to the star and went to sleep. They dreamed of flying in the sky with the star. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to draw pictures. She would draw pictures of flowers, animals, and even her family. One day, she drew a picture of a big, red mailbox. She wanted to give the picture to her grandma who lived far away.

Lily's mommy told her they could mail the picture to grandma. So, they put the picture in an envelope and walked to the mailbox. But when they got there, they saw that the mailbox was already full. Lily's mommy said they would have to come back later when the mailman had come to take the letters.

Lily was sad because she wanted her picture to reach her grandma as soon as possible. She started to feel naughty and wanted to take the picture out of the envelope and keep it for herself. But then her mommy reminded her that it's important to be patient and wait for things to settle. So, they put the envelope back in their bag and walked home, hoping that the mailbox would be empty the next time they came.

Once there was a little girl called Emma. Emma liked to work all day helping her mum and dad. Emma worked hard and tried her best.

When it was time for a break, Emma liked to take a nap. She would lay down in her bed, close her eyes and snore.

One day, it was a gloomy day. The sky was grey and it was raining. Emma watched from her window and wondered what she should do. She decided it was a perfect day for a nap.

Emma snuggled down in her bed, pulled up the covers and was soon fast asleep. A few hours later, Emma woke up feeling refreshed and ready to work again.

One day, Lily and Max went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They liked to play and run and laugh.

They found a big green caterpillar on a leaf. Lily wanted to touch it, but Max said, "No, it is bitter. It can hurt you with its hairs. Mom told us to be careful with caterpillars."

Lily said, "But it is so cute and fuzzy. I want to be its friend. Maybe it is not bitter. Maybe it is sweet."

She reached out her hand to the caterpillar, but it moved away. It did not want to be touched. It wanted to eat the leaf and be alone.

Lily was sad. She said, "Why are you so mean, caterpillar? Don't you like me?"

The caterpillar said, "I am not mean. I am just busy. I need to eat and grow and change. One day, I will be a butterfly. Then I will fly and see the world. But now, I need to soak in the sun and the rain and the wind. Please, leave me alone."

Lily and Max understood. They said, "Okay, caterpillar. We are sorry. We will let you be. We hope you will be a beautiful butterfly."

They waved goodbye to the caterpillar and went to play with their mom. They had fun in the park. They learned something new. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a man who was driving a car. He was going to the hospital to see his friend who was sick. His friend was a patient there. The man was worried because his friend looked very pale when he saw him. 

The man asked his friend, "How are you feeling?" His friend replied, "I'm not feeling well. I'm very sick." The man said, "Don't worry, I will take care of you." 

But suddenly, the man felt very dizzy and he lost control of the car. The car drove off the road and crashed. The man and his friend were hurt badly. They had to go to the hospital again. This time, they were both patients.

Lily and Max were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Max was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around and saw a big tree. She thought Max might be hiding behind it. She ran to the tree and shouted, "I found you!"

But Max was not behind the tree. Instead, Lily saw a dog. The dog was brown and furry and had a collar. The dog was holding something in its mouth. It was a steak. The dog had taken the steak from someone's picnic. The dog looked at Lily and wagged its tail.

Lily was not scared of the dog. She liked dogs. She was compassionate. She knew the dog was hungry and wanted the steak. She smiled at the dog and said, "Hello, dog. You can have the steak. I don't want it. But can you please reveal where Max is? I want to find him."

The dog barked and nodded. It dropped the steak and ran to another tree. It pointed with its nose. Lily followed the dog and saw Max. Max was hiding under a blanket. He had heard Lily and the dog and was giggling. Lily lifted the blanket and said, "I found you, Max! And I made a new friend. This is the dog. He helped me find you. He is very nice."

Max came out of the blanket and hugged Lily. He also petted the dog and said, "Thank you, dog. You are very smart. And you can have the steak. We don't mind. Do you want to play with us?"

The dog barked and wagged its tail. It was happy. It had found a steak and two friends. Lily, Max, and the dog played together in the park. They had a lot of fun. They were a good team.

Mummy and Daddy had a great surprise for Elsa. They said they were going to deliver something special, something very luxurious! Elsa couldn't believe it. She waited very excitedly for the big surprise.

At last it arrived. Elsa quickly opened it. Inside was the most beautiful doll she had ever seen. It had long curly hair, and was dressed in a pink dress with sparkles on it. Elsa was overjoyed.

She hugged the doll and thanked Mummy and Daddy. She loved it so much, and was so so happy with their great surprise. She couldn't wait to show her friends. It was the best present she had ever had.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a unique object while playing in his room. It was a big, red ball with a shiny star on it.

Tim showed the ball to his friend, Sam. "Look what I found!" Tim said. Sam looked at the ball and said, "Wow! That's a cool ball, Tim. Can I play with it too?" Tim smiled and said, "Of course! Let's play together."

They played with the ball all day. But then, it was time for Tim to remove the ball from his room and put it away. "We can play with it again tomorrow, Sam," Tim said. Sam agreed and they both said goodbye. Tim put the ball in a special box to keep it safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient pillow. It had been around for many years, even before the little girl's grandparents were born.

One day, the little girl was playing in her room when she saw the pillow. Excited, she picked it up and hugged it.

The pillow suddenly spoke, "Let me escape this room!"

The little girl gasped. She looked around cautiously, then asked the pillow, "Where do you wanna go?"

The pillow replied, "Anywhere! I'm tired of this old room!"

The little girl smiled and said, "I know just the place! Follow me!" She then carried the pillow out of the room and into the garden.

The pillow was so happy to see the garden! Trees, flowers, and fields of green grass surrounded it. The pillow had finally escaped the ancient room and was free to explore.

The little girl laughed, "See, I told you I'd find a better place for you!"

The pillow smiled and snuggled into the girl's arms as she took it for a stroll through the garden. Together, they had a really wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a toy skull that she found very attractive. Mia loved to play with her skull and show it to her friends.

One day, Mia took her skull to the park. She saw her friend, Tim, playing with his toy truck. Mia went to Tim and said, "Look at my attractive skull, please!" Tim looked at the skull and smiled. He thought it was a cool toy.

Mia and Tim played together at the park with their toys. They took turns playing with the skull and the truck. They had a lot of fun and were very happy. At the end of the day, they said goodbye and went home with their toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden and watch the birds fly. But one day, she noticed that her window was dirty and she couldn't see the birds clearly. 

Lily thought about how she could improve her window. She went inside and got a pink cloth and some water. She wiped the window until it was clean and shiny. Now she could see the birds much better! 

Lily was happy that she improved her window. She learned that sometimes, things can be better if we take the time to make them better. And so, she continued to take care of her window and enjoyed watching the birds every day.

Mum and Dad were very excited. Today, they were taking their little three year old son to the park. 

He was so happy! As they walked into the park, he pointed out the things he could see. There was a big slide and a cheery roundabout. 

Mum and Dad watched their son, their faces beaming with delight. 

Then the little boy spotted something new - it was a chess board. He didn't know what it was, so he asked Mum and Dad.

Mum explained that it was a chess board, and she asked her son if he wanted to play. He said yes!

So both Mum and Dad helped the little boy choose his chess pieces. Then Dad taught him what to do. It was really special: the three of them were learning something new together. 

After a few games, the little boy learnt how to play. He was so proud of himself. Dad said he was dependable and could win games by himself now. 

Mum and Dad were proud of their clever little son and watched him play again and again. They had chosen a great day in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She had a big, brown box that she loved to play with. One day, Sally saw an ugly bug crawling on her box. She didn't like the bug, so she stepped on it. 

After that, Sally noticed her box was dirty and had ugly marks on it. She decided to clean it with a wet cloth. She stepped on the cloth to make it wet, then wiped her box until it was shiny and pretty again. 

Sally was happy to have her box back to normal. She hugged it tightly and went to play with it outside. She promised herself to always keep her box clean and safe from any more ugly bugs. The end.

Robbie was a three year old boy who loved to ride. Every morning he would run outside and hop on his bike and ride around the block. But that morning was different, there was an upset feeling in the air.

Robbie's mom came out of the house and knelt down next to him. "Robbie, there is a war going on, honey," she said. Robbie looked confused and asked, "What is war mommy?"

"It is when people fight and argue," she explained. "For now you can't ride outside like you usually do, it is too dangerous. We have to stay inside so you can be safe."

Robbie felt a wave of disappointment, but he understood what his mom was saying. He smiled and nodded, then there was a moment of understanding between the two of them. Robbie was upset, but he was glad his mom was looking out for him.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max was a very good dog. He liked to play and run. One day, Max saw a new, unknown cat in the yard. The cat was small and cute. Max wanted to play with the cat, but the cat did not know how to play with dogs.

Max did not ignore the cat. Instead, he wanted to teach the cat how to play. Max brought a ball to the cat. He showed the cat how to play with the ball by rolling it on the ground. The cat watched Max and tried to play too. They played with the ball together and had lots of fun.

After playing, Max and the cat became good friends. They played together every day. And Max taught the cat many new games. They were very happy together. The cat was not unknown anymore, and they both had a new friend to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl who lived in a warm house. She loved how her house felt when the sun came out, and she would often go out to play in its heat with her friends.

One day, the heat began to grow too hot, so the young girl decided to go and explore a nearby forest. She went on an adventure, discovering all sorts of plants and animals!

But when it started to get dark, she realised that she must return home. The forest seemed much bigger than when she arrived, and the night was getting cold.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise, and was startled. It was a large, wild bear! The bear was growling, and the young girl was very scared.

The bear came closer, and the young girl started to run away. She was so scared and tired from running, but eventually she managed to return safely home.

The young girl never forgot the wild bear, but she was forever thankful for the heat of her warm house. She promised never to go to the forest again without her friends.

Lily was very happy today. She had a new suit. It was pink and soft and had a big bow. She wanted to show it to her friends at school. She put it on and looked at herself in the mirror. She smiled and said, "I look pretty!"

She ran downstairs and saw her mom and dad. They were also wearing new suits. They were going to a party. They hugged Lily and said, "You look very pretty, Lily. We are proud of you. But we have to go now. Grandma will take care of you."

Lily waved goodbye to her mom and dad. She was a little sad. She wanted to go to the party too. But she knew she had to stay with Grandma. Grandma was nice and fun. She made cookies and read stories. She also had a big dog named Spot. Spot was Lily's friend. He liked to play and cuddle.

Lily and Grandma had a good time. They ate cookies and read stories. They played with Spot and his toys. They sang songs and danced. Lily was happy again. She forgot about the party. She had fun with Grandma and Spot.

But soon it was dark outside. Grandma said, "It's time to sleep, Lily. You had a busy day. You need to rest. Tomorrow you can go to school and show your new suit to your friends."

Lily nodded. She was tired. She hugged Grandma and Spot and said, "Thank you, Grandma. Thank you, Spot. I love you. Good night."

She went to her room and put on her pajamas. She brushed her teeth and climbed into her bed. She closed her eyes and dreamed of her new suit and her friends. She was happy. She slept well.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw pictures. One day, she went to the park and saw her friend Johnny.

"Hi Johnny! Do you want to play?" asked Lily.

"Sure, but first let's go get some food. I brought an avocado for us to share," replied Johnny.

Lily looked at the avocado and said, "Wow, that's a big green thing! I've never tried it before."

Johnny smiled and said, "It's really yummy! You should try it."

Lily took a bite and said, "Mmm, it's really good! You're so creative for bringing this."

Johnny laughed and said, "I like to tease you sometimes, but I'm glad you like it." They continued to play and have fun together at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on walks in the forest with her mommy and daddy. One day, while they were walking, they saw a pretty flower. Lily wanted to pick it, but her parents told her not to because it might be poisonous.

Lily was confused and didn't understand why the flower could be bad for her. Her parents explained that some things might look nice, but they could hurt you if you touched or ate them. Lily listened and promised not to touch the flower.

But then, as they continued walking, Lily saw another flower that looked even prettier than the first. She wanted to surprise her parents by picking it and showing them. So, she picked the flower and showed it to her parents.

Unfortunately, the flower was poisonous and Lily got very sick. Her parents rushed her to the hospital, but it was too late. Lily didn't make it. Her parents were very sad and wished they had explained better to Lily about the dangers of poisonous things.

Tom likes to draw with his crayons. He has many colors and he makes pictures of his family, his friends and his toys. He draws on big papers that his mom gives him. He is very happy when he draws.

One day, he wants to make a special picture for his mom. He thinks of what she likes. He knows she likes flowers, birds and hearts. He picks his favorite crayons and starts to draw. He draws a big flower with red and yellow. He draws a blue bird next to the flower. He draws a pink heart under the bird. He smiles at his picture.

He wants to show his mom his picture, but she is busy in the kitchen. He waits for her to finish. He looks at his picture again and thinks of something else. He finds a green crayon and writes "I love you, Mom" on the paper. He is very proud of his words.

He hears his mom call him for lunch. He runs to the kitchen with his picture. He says, "Mom, look what I made for you!" He gives her the paper. She looks at the picture and smiles. She hugs him and says, "This is brilliant, Tom! Thank you so much! I love you, too!" She puts the picture on the fridge. Tom is very happy. He finishes his lunch and asks for more paper. He wants to draw more pictures.

Tommy loved springtime. He would often go outside and play in the field near his house. One beautiful day, he decided to explore the field further. He skipped, hopped and ran until he came to a long, green path.

Tommy look to the left and there was a pond. He looked to the right and saw a hill. He didn't know which way to choose. Then he decided to ask his friend who lived down the street. 

Tommy asked, "Which way should I go, friend?"

His friend replied, "Choose the path, Tommy. It will take you on an adventure."

Tommy chose the path and smiled. It led him to a sweet-smelling garden where he picked beautiful flowers. Then he skipped back down the path, feeling excited and happy. 

Tommy had enjoyed his adventure. He was glad he had chosen the long path.

One day there was a man called Jack. He was always playing jokes and making people laugh. Everybody loved Jack.
One day, Jack had a plan. He wanted to scare his friends for fun. So he began to tell them about a scary jail. He said it was in a dark and scary place. Everyone was frightened.
Nobody believed Jack, and they laughed at him. But, the next day, Jack disappeared.
The next day, Jack's friends went looking for him. They knew he was up to something. After a long search, they found him - in a scary place, right where he had said the jail was! Everyone was shocked. 
Jack had tricked them all - and they were never quite sure if he had done it just to make them laugh, or to frighten them. Everyone was relieved to see Jack safe and sound, and they were all a little bit frightened too.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a dog named Max. Max was Timmy's own dog. Timmy loved Max very much.

One night, Timmy was scared of the dark. The dark was very serious to Timmy. Max saw that Timmy was scared and he went to be with him. Max was brave and he helped Timmy not be scared of the dark anymore.

From that night on, Timmy knew he didn't have to be scared of the dark because Max was always there to keep him safe. Max was Timmy's best friend and he was happy to own him.

Sam and Mia are big fans of soccer. They like to watch the games on TV with their dad. One day, their dad has a surprise for them. He takes them to the stadium to see a real game. Sam and Mia are very excited. They wear their favorite team's shirts and hats.

At the stadium, they see many people and hear a lot of noise. They find their seats and wait for the game to start. They see the players warming up on the field. They cheer and clap for them. Their dad points to the big screen and says, "Look, they are showing the names of the players. Do you know them?"

Sam nods and says, "Yes, I know them. That's Jack, he's the best scorer. And that's Ben, he's the fastest runner. And that's Tom, he's the captain. He's very good at passing the ball."

Mia nods and says, "I know them too. But who is that? He looks weird." She points to a player who has a big beard and a funny hat. He is not wearing the same shirt as the others.

Their dad laughs and says, "That's not a player, that's a fan. He likes to dress up like that to support his team. He's having fun. Do you think he's funny?"

Sam and Mia look at each other and giggle. They think he's funny and weird. They say, "Yes, he's funny and weird. But we like our team better. Go, go, go!" They shout and wave their hats. They are ready to enjoy the game.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. One day Daisy was feeling very angry. She was so angry, it made her mad. She wanted to find a way to calm down.

So she went outside and looked for something to help her. She saw a big square on the ground. She had never seen it before. She walked over and wiped it with her hand.

She kept wiping it until the square was very clean. Daisy felt much better. Wiping the square had made her happy and calmer. From then on, when she was feeling angry, Daisy would go outside and wipe the square until she felt better.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they go to Tom's house. Tom has a new computer. He wants to show Mia.

"Look, Mia, this is my computer. It is very fun. You can watch videos and play games on it," Tom says.

Mia is curious. She wants to see the computer too. She goes to Tom's desk. But the floor is wet. Tom's mom was cleaning. Mia does not see the water. She slips and falls. She hits the computer. The computer makes a loud noise and stops working.

Tom is angry. He shouts at Mia. "You broke my computer! You are a bad friend! Go away!"

Mia is sad. She cries and runs away. She does not want to be Tom's friend anymore.

Tom's mom hears the noise. She comes to see what happened. She sees the broken computer and the wet floor. She hugs Tom and says, "I'm sorry, Tom. It was my fault. I forgot to dry the floor. I will buy you a new computer. But you should not yell at Mia. She did not mean to break it. She slipped and it was an accident. She is your friend. You should be kind and forgive her."

Tom feels sorry. He knows his mom is right. He was not nice to Mia. He wants to say sorry to her. He runs to Mia's house. He knocks on the door. Mia opens it. She has tears in her eyes.

"Mia, I'm sorry. I was wrong. You did not break my computer on purpose. You slipped and it was an accident. I was mean to you. Can you forgive me? Can we still be friends?" Tom says.

Mia smiles. She is happy to hear Tom's words. She says, "Yes, Tom, I forgive you. I'm sorry too. I did not want to hurt your computer. I was curious. I wanted to see it. Yes, we can still be friends."

Tom and Mia hug. They are friends again. They learn a lesson. They learn to be careful and not slip on wet floors. They learn to be gentle and not break things. They learn to be kind and not shout at each other. They learn to say sorry and forgive each other. They are good friends.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. Anna wants to go on the slide, but Ben is scared.

"Come on, Ben, it is fun!" Anna says. "I will hold your hand."

Ben shakes his head. "No, it is too high. I will fall."

Anna smiles. "You will not fall. You are intelligent. You know how to sit and slide. Trust me."

Ben looks at Anna. He sees that she is brave and kind. He decides to try. He holds Anna's hand and they climb the stairs. They sit on the slide and slide down together. They laugh and feel happy.

"See, Ben, that was not so bad!" Anna says. "Do you want to go again?"

Ben nods. "Yes, I do. Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend."

They hold hands and run to the slide again. They have fun in the park. They are friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie was three and she loved to wear lots of lovely clothes. Every day she would find something new to put on and look fabulous.

One day Sophie's mum bought her a beautiful present. It was a new dress and it was so lovely that it made her smile. She couldn't wait to put it on and show it off to her friends.

The next day Sophie put on her new dress and she looked amazing. Her mum said "Well done Sophie, you look beautiful."

But when Sophie went to school, none of the other children said nice things. They started to laugh at her and call her names. Sophie felt sad and embarrassed, she wished that she had never put on her new dress.

In the end, Sophie felt so upset that she never wanted to wear her lovely dress again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat radishes, but her brother Jack thought they were too smelly. 

One day, Lily brought a big radish to the dinner table. Jack wrinkled his nose and said, "Ew, that's so smelly! I don't want to eat it."

Lily tried to convince Jack to try a bite, but he resisted. "No way, it's too stinky!" he said.

Their mom suggested they play a game to see who could eat the most radishes. Jack agreed to play, and to Lily's surprise, he ended up eating more radishes than her! From that day on, Jack didn't think radishes were so smelly anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and sing songs. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a package. Timmy was so happy! He opened the package and found a toy recorder inside. He was so excited to record his songs and play them back.

But then, Timmy's sister came and took the recorder away. Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do. He tried to take it back, but his sister wouldn't give it back. Timmy got so angry that he did something crazy. He threw his sister's favorite toy and broke it.

Timmy's mom was so mad at him. She took away the recorder and sent him to his room. Timmy was sad and cried himself to sleep. The end.

Lisa liked to play in the garden with her mom. She helped her mom water the plants and pull out the weeds. Sometimes, she found bugs and worms in the soil. She liked to examine them and see how they moved and felt.

One day, she saw a red ball poking out of the ground. She pulled it out and saw that it was a radish. She had never seen a radish before. She showed it to her mom and asked, "What is this?"

"That's a radish, Lisa. It's a vegetable that grows under the ground. Some people like to eat it, but it's very spicy. Do you want to try it?" her mom said.

Lisa nodded. She was curious about the radish. She took a small bite and made a face. It was hot and bitter in her mouth. She spit it out and said, "Yuck! I don't like it!"

Her mom laughed and gave her a glass of water. She said, "That's okay, Lisa. Not everyone likes radishes. Maybe you'll like something else from the garden. How about a carrot? They're sweet and crunchy."

Lisa smiled and said, "Yes, please. I like carrots. They're orange and fancy." She took a carrot from her mom and ate it happily. She decided that she liked the garden, even if she didn't like radishes.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Bob. Bob was very intelligent. He could call out to his friends in many different ways. He loved to talk and share his opinion with others.

One sunny day, Bob met a new friend named Tina. Tina was a small, shy mouse. She did not talk much. Bob called out to her, "Hi Tina! Do you want to play with me?" Tina nodded her head and smiled.

As they played together, Bob shared his opinion about the best games to play. He would say, "I think this game is fun!" or "I like this game more!" Tina listened and soon started to share her opinion too. They became very good friends, and everyone thought they were a great team. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sue are playing in the garden. They like to grow things with Mom and Dad. They have carrots, beans, lettuce and tomatoes. Tomatoes are red and round and juicy. Tom and Sue like to eat them.

"Look, Sue, this tomato is very big!" Tom says. He holds a tomato in his hand. It is bigger than his fist.

"Wow, Tom, it is big! How big is it?" Sue asks. She wants to know.

"Let's measure it!" Tom says. He has a ruler. He puts the tomato on the ruler. He counts the numbers. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. It is seven long!"

"That is very long, Tom! Can we eat it?" Sue says. She is hungry.

"Wait, Sue, there is something on the tomato. What is it?" Tom says. He sees a black spot on the tomato. It is not dirt. It is unknown.

"Unknown? What is unknown?" Sue says. She does not understand.

"Unknown means we do not know what it is. Maybe it is a bug. Maybe it is a seed. Maybe it is a hole. We have to find out!" Tom says. He is curious.

"How do we find out, Tom?" Sue says. She is curious too.

"Let's ask Mom and Dad. They know a lot of things. Maybe they know what the unknown is. Come on, Sue, let's go!" Tom says. He takes the tomato and the ruler. He runs to the house. Sue follows him.

They find Mom and Dad in the kitchen. They show them the tomato and the unknown. Mom and Dad look at it. They smile.

"What a big tomato, Tom and Sue! You did a good job growing it. And you measured it too. That is very smart!" Mom says.

"Thank you, Mom. But what is this unknown on the tomato? We do not know what it is. Do you know?" Tom says.

Mom and Dad look closer. They laugh.

"That is not unknown, Tom and Sue. That is a sticker. It says 'organic'. That means the tomato is natural and healthy. Someone put it on the tomato at the store. We bought some tomatoes there yesterday. We mixed them with the ones from the garden. We forgot to take the sticker off. Sorry!" Dad says.

"Oh, a sticker! That is funny. We thought it was a bug or a seed or a hole. We were wrong. We learned something new!" Sue says.

"That is okay, Sue. Learning something new is good. You can always ask us if you do not know something. We are happy to help you. Now, do you want to eat the tomato? It looks delicious!" Mom says.

"Yes, please, Mom. We want to eat the tomato. It is big and red and juicy. And it has a sticker!" Tom and Sue say.

They wash the tomato and cut it into slices. They share it with Mom and Dad. They enjoy the tomato. It is tasty. They are happy. They love to play and learn and eat in the garden. The end.

Jimmy and his mom were standing on the beach looking at the ocean. "Isn't it so beautiful?" asked Jimmy. His mom nodded and pointed in the distance. "Look at the boats out there," she suggested. Jimmy squinted at the tiny boats. Suddenly, he gasped and pointed with excitement. "Mommy, I can see dolphins!"

Jimmy and his mom smiled as they watched the dolphins playing in the water. They were jumping and splashing in the waves. Jimmy noticed that one of the dolphins seemed to be swimming a bit slower than the others. "Mommy, it looks weak," he pointed out. His mom nodded and suggested they take a closer look. 

They both stepped closer to the water's edge. From their new view, Jimmy could see the weak dolphin more clearly. It was swimming slower than the other dolphins and it seemed a little tired. 

Jimmy waved his hand and said, "Hello!" to the dolphin. As if it could understand him, the dolphin turned to look in Jimmy's direction and then carried on swimming with slow, tired movements. 

Jimmy and his mom watched it until it was out of sight. Then, they turned back and continued on their way, both feeling glad that they could suggest and lend a helping hand to the weak dolphin.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to clean up her room. "Lily, can you please clean up your room? It's a bit messy," said mommy. 

Lily didn't want to clean up her room, but she knew she had to. She started picking up her toys and putting them away. While she was cleaning, she found a mystery box under her bed. "Mommy, mommy! Look what I found!" exclaimed Lily. 

"What did you find, sweetie?" asked mommy. 

"I found a mystery box under my bed!" said Lily. 

Mommy and Lily opened the box and found a bunch of old toys and books. Lily got so excited, she started spinning around and around. "I feel dizzy!" she laughed. 

After they finished exploring the mystery box, Lily went back to cleaning her room. She was happy to have found something new, but she knew it was important to keep her room clean.

One day, there was a little boy named Derek who really wanted to use his fan. He asked his mom, but she said no. He thought that it was unfair and started to demand for it. He suggested that she could turn it on for just two minutes. His mom said no again, but Derek was determined.

He kept demanding for it, so his mom said that he could use the fan in the next room. Derek did not want to go so far, he wanted his fan to be here. His mom said that it was too loud if it was close.

Derek looked around the room and saw something far away. It was a small fan that was attached to the wall. It looked quite distant for Derek. But his mom said that he could use it.

Derek was very excited and he ran to the fan. He quickly turned it on and enjoyed the cool air. He smiled and jumped up and down. He was finally happy that he got his fan.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sunshine and watch the flowers grow. Every night, she would look up at the moon and say goodnight.

One night, Lily saw a scary shadow on the moon. It looked like a monster! She was afraid and ran inside to tell her mommy. Her mommy told her not to be scared because the moon was just growing bigger and bigger.

Lily was amazed! She didn't know the moon could grow. From then on, every night she looked at the moon and watched it grow bigger and bigger until it was full and bright. And she wasn't scared anymore because she knew it was just the moon growing. The end.

Once upon a time, three brave animals, a cat, a dog and a mouse, wanted to succeed in life. Together they set out on an adventure. 

Their first challenge was to find a yellow skull in a faraway land. For days they searched, but they could not find it. Finally, they reached a mysterious cave. 

East at the entrance of the cave, they spotted a yellow skull! Quickly the three of them raced towards it and reached it first.

The brave animals had succeeded! They hugged each other with joy and celebrated their victory.

The end

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived by the sea. Every day she would walk to the harbor and wave to the boats coming in. One cold winter day she went to the harbor and saw a small boat. Inside the boat was a little boy, shivering from the cold.

"Do you want to come inside?" asked the little girl.

The boy shook his head. "No," he replied sadly.

The little girl smiled and said, "It's ok. You can stay here in the harbor. I'll accept you and you can stay safe here. No one will hurt you."

So the little boy and the girl stayed in the harbor, keeping each other warm. The girl taught the boy how to make boats out of shells and driftwood, and the boy taught the girl to sing the songs of his people. Together, they accepted each other and found comfort in the harbor.

Once there was a generous snowman. He loved spending time with the children in the park and making them laugh. 

One day when the snowman was walking he saw a shivering dog. He wanted to help the dog, so he spread his arms wide to give it warmth. But when he got closer, the dog snapped and growled at him.

The snowman was sad, but he knew what he could do. He opened his suitcase and took out all the colors he had saved up. He scattered them around to make the dog more comfortable and happy.

The dog stopped shivering and stepped closer. It stretched out its paw to thank the snowman. The snowman smiled and the two hugged and became friends.The children in the park felt so lucky to have such a generous snowman in their park.

Sara and Tom are helping Mom make soup for dinner. Mom gives Sara a carrot and Tom an onion to cut. Sara likes carrots. They are sweet and crunchy. Tom does not like onions. They are smelly and make his eyes water.

"Mom, why do I have to cut the onion?" Tom complains. "I don't want to eat it. It is yucky."

"Tom, stop complaining," Mom says. "Onion is good for you. It makes the soup tasty. And you don't have to cut it very small. Just make thick slices."

Tom tries to cut the onion, but it is hard and slippery. He cries and rubs his eyes. Sara laughs and says, "Tom is a baby. He can't cut an onion. I can cut a carrot. It is easy and fun."

"Tom is not a baby," Mom says. "He is a big boy. He can do it if he tries. And Sara, don't laugh at your brother. That is not nice. You should help him."

Mom gives Tom a paper towel to wipe his eyes. She shows him how to hold the onion and the knife. She helps him cut a few slices. Then she lets him do it by himself. Tom feels proud. He says, "Look, Mom, I did it. I cut the onion. It is not so bad."

Mom smiles and says, "Good job, Tom. You are a good helper. Now put the onion in the pot with the carrot and the water. We will add some salt and pepper and cook the soup. It will be delicious."

Sara and Tom put their vegetables in the pot. They stir the soup and smell it. It smells good. They say, "Mom, we are hungry. Can we have some soup?"

Mom says, "Yes, you can. But first, wash your hands and set the table. Then we can have some soup and bread and butter. And maybe some cookies for dessert."

Sara and Tom wash their hands and set the table. They are happy. They like to help Mom make soup. They like to eat soup. They don't complain about the onion. They say, "Thank you, Mom, for the soup. It is yummy."

One day, Mommy was writing in her diary. She was a little nervous: tomorrow was a very important day. Her little daughter, Susie, wanted to know why Mommy was so nervous, so Mommy explained it to her.

"I'm worried about tomorrow, sweetheart," Mommy said. "It's an important day."

Susie nodded, and then yawned. She was sleepy.

"You should go to bed now, my love," Mommy said, and kissed Susie goodnight.

Susie climbed into bed and yawned again. She was so sleepy, she didn't stay awake long enough to worry.

Mommy checked on her one last time before she went back to her diary. Seeing her daughter sleeping peacefully, she felt a little less nervous. She knew tomorrow would work out just fine.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny loved to drink coffee with his mommy every morning. One day, Benny's mommy made the coffee very thick and yummy. Benny was so happy and he asked his mommy if he could join her for coffee. His mommy said yes, and they enjoyed their thick coffee together. Benny was so happy to join his mommy for coffee and he felt very grown up. From that day on, Benny always asked his mommy if he could join her for coffee, and they had many happy mornings together.

Sally wanted to pick apples. She was very patient. She carefully looked for the ripest apples on the tree. After she found five of the brightest apples, she wanted to pick them, but she couldn't reach them. She asked her mom for help, and her mom gave her a step stool. When Sally stood on the stool, she was tall enough to pick all five of the apples. Sally was so excited and said, "I got it!" She proudly took her apples to the kitchen and happily ate them. 

The end.

Lily and Ben were going on a trip with Mom and Dad. They were very happy. They packed their luggage with toys, books, and clothes. They put their luggage in the car and said goodbye to their dog, Spot.

The car drove for a long time. Lily and Ben looked out the window and saw many things. They saw trees, houses, cows, and bridges. They played games and sang songs. They asked Mom and Dad when they would get there.

Mom and Dad said they would get there soon. They said they were going to a big city with many people and buildings. They said the city was very busy and noisy. They said they would have fun and see new things.

Lily and Ben were excited. They wanted to see the big city. They wondered what it would look like. They wondered what they would do there. They hoped they would find a park and a zoo and a museum.

The car drove and drove. Lily and Ben started to feel tired. They yawned and closed their eyes. They fell asleep. They dreamed of the big city.

The car stopped. Lily and Ben woke up. They rubbed their eyes and looked around. They saw a lot of cars and buses and trucks. They saw a lot of people and buildings and signs. They heard a lot of horns and sirens and voices. They felt a lot of heat and smoke and dust.

They were in the big city. They had reached the end of their trip. They got out of the car and took their luggage. They followed Mom and Dad to a big hotel. They were very surprised. They did not know what to expect. They wondered if they would like it or not.

Once upon a time, there lived a mommy and a daddy and their little girl. One day, the mommy and daddy wanted to teach the little girl something special. So, they set up a trap.

The trap was made of string with shiny things on it. They put it in the front yard, so it was safe for the little girl.

When the little girl saw the trap, she screamed out of excitement. She ran to the trap and was so happy when she saw what was inside the trap.

There were lots of little bugs, hopping around the trap. The mommy and daddy told the little girl to use her fingers to pick up the bugs. The little girl was so excited to teach the bugs about the world.

The mommy and daddy watched their little girl, teaching the bugs how to find food and run around the garden. They were happy to see their little girl learning something new.

The little girl was so proud of her teaching and the mommy and daddy were proud of her too. They hugged the little girl and told her how safe she was in their yard.

Once upon a time, there was a long road that led to a big house. The house was very dusty and needed to be cleaned. A kind lady lived in the house and she wanted to offer some cookies to her neighbors. She put on her apron and started to clean the dust. As she was cleaning, she saw a little girl walking on the long road. The lady offered the girl some cookies, and the girl was very happy.
