They sat together and ate the cookies, and the lady told the girl about her adventures when she was young. The little girl was fascinated by the stories and they became good friends. From that day on, the lady and the little girl would often sit together and talk about their day while enjoying some cookies.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her mom's makeup. One day, she found a big box of makeup in her mom's room. Lily was very happy and excited.

Lily started to put the makeup on her face. She put on red lipstick, blue eyeshadow, and pink blush. She looked in the mirror and laughed. She looked very funny. Lily wanted to show her mom her new look.

Lily ran to her mom and said, "Look, Mom! I used your makeup!" Her mom looked at her and smiled. She said, "Oh, Lily, you look so pretty, but you need to release that makeup from your face now." Lily felt a little bitter because she wanted to keep the makeup on. But she knew her mom was right.

Lily and her mom went to the bathroom and washed off all the makeup. Lily's face was clean and shiny again. Her mom gave her a big hug and said, "You are beautiful just the way you are." Lily felt happy and hugged her mom back. They both laughed and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot liked to act like a big dog, even though he was small. He would run and jump and bark all day long.

One day, Spot found a big, bitter lemon. He thought it was a ball, so he picked it up in his mouth. The lemon was very bitter, and it made Spot's mouth feel funny. But Spot didn't want to stop acting like a big dog, so he kept playing.

Spot played with the bitter lemon all day, even though it made his mouth feel funny. His friends saw him and they laughed. They said, "Spot, you are a funny dog!" Spot was happy that he made his friends laugh, and he knew that even a small dog could act like a big dog.

Uncle Bob was a jazzy man. He had a bright smile and big eyes. He was always on the move, never staying in the same spot for too long. 

Every night, he wore his tight overalls and grabbed his trumpet. He would go to the park and play jazz for everyone to hear. The music was upbeat and fun. He sang about the birds and the flowers, and soon people would start to dance. 

On one occasion, a little girl was selling lemonade at the park. She kept getting closer to the stage, until she started to sway with the music. Uncle Bob smiled and stepped off the stage. He bent down to the little girl and asked her if she wanted to join in with the music.

The girl nodded, and took the trumpet from Uncle Bob. She put it up to her lips and started to play. The music was a little bit squeaky and wrong, but it made Uncle Bob smile. He clapped his hands and danced around. Everyone at the park partied along. 

The little girl looked proud. She beamed as she played along with Uncle Bob's jazz. Even when the night ended and everyone went back home, the little girl was still carrying the trumpet. Uncle Bob waved goodbye, and the girl waved back. The tight chords played in her mind during those quiet nights at home.

Once upon a time, there was a purple cop. He had a big job to do. He needed to print a picture for a little boy.

The purple cop went to his big machine. He put the paper in the machine. Then, he pushed the button to print the picture. The machine made a funny noise.

The little boy was happy when he saw the picture. The purple cop smiled too. They both had a fun day together.

One day, Bob the bunny had a big urge to go on a jog. He hopped out of his hole and began to bounce up and down the path. He moved so fast he thought he could fly! But then he saw a big tree. Its branches were far too big and high to climb, but he wanted too see what was on top.

So Bob got an idea. He started to jog around the tree. Once he made it to the trunk he kept going and going. He jogged one circle, two circles, then three! Finally he made it to the top. The view was so great! 

Bob couldn't believe how far he'd gone. He felt proud and wanted to tell everyone what he had done. But just then he heard a loud call from his family. "Bob, time to come home!" So Bob gave one last look around, and then jogged back down the big tree.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the living room. They have a new couch. It is big and soft and red.

One day, they have a fun idea. They take the pillows from the couch and put them on the floor. They make a big pile of pillows. Then they climb on the couch and slide down on the pillows. Whee!

They slide and slide and laugh and laugh. They pretend they are on a mountain or a slide or a rocket. They have so much fun.

But then, they hear a voice. It is Mom. She is coming home from work. She opens the door and sees the mess. She sees the couch without pillows and the pillows on the floor. She sees Anna and Ben sliding and smiling.

She is not happy. She says, "What are you doing? You made a big mess. You can't slide on the couch. You can break it. It is new. You have to be careful. And you have to clean up. Now!"

Anna and Ben stop sliding. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "We're sorry, Mom. We just wanted to have fun. We like the new couch. We didn't mean to make a mess. We will clean up. We love you, Mom."

Mom sighs. She sees their faces. She loves them too. She says, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. I know you wanted to have fun. But you have to be respectful of the new couch. And you have to tidy up after you play. OK?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "OK, Mom." They hug Mom. Then they pick up the pillows and put them back on the couch. They make the couch look nice again. They say, "We're sorry, couch. We won't slide on you again. You are nice and soft and red."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful tribe of brave warriors called the Heelers. They all wore special shoes with strong heels to help them walk and run quickly.

One day, a Heeler named Kayla was on her own in the forest. Suddenly, she heard a voice coming from behind a tree.

"Will you help me?" it said.

Curiously, Kayla stepped forward and saw a small creature. It was a fairy who had ripped her wings and was not able to fly.

"I need you to help me complete my tasks," the fairy begged.

Kayla knew she had to help the fairy. She took off her shoes, revealing strong heels. She gave them to the fairy and said, "These are powerful. Put them on and you'll be able to fly again."

The fairy turned to Kayla and said, "Thank you! I am now able to complete my tasks." And with that, she flew away.

Kayla smiled and thought, "It's true that powerful heels can get you anywhere!"

Once there was a yacht that was ready to sail. It bobbed on the water, waiting to set off to find new lands. The captain was ready, too. He was folding the sails and making sure they were nice and tidy. When he was finished, the yacht was ready to go. 

The captain sent up the sails, and the wind pushed the yacht forward. The sails billowed out, and the captain steered with the wheel. The captain and his crew took the yacht on a big adventure. They sailed to new lands, and had many new experiences. 

Finally, after a long journey, the captain steered the yacht back home. He put the sails away and gave them a good fold. Then the captain and his crew stepped off the yacht and went to their homes, happy and proud of the journey they had taken.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety liked to fly in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big cloud in the sky. The cloud was moving fast and suddenly Tweety disappeared behind it.

Tweety felt scared because he couldn't see anything. But then the cloud moved away and Tweety was happy to see the sun again. Tweety continued to fly and sing until he saw a group of animals. They were fighting and making loud noises. 

Tweety asked them why they were fighting, and they said it was because of a war. Tweety didn't understand what war meant, but he knew it was not good. He flew away and saw a tree that was very flexible, moving with the wind. Tweety thought it was cool how the tree could bend without breaking. 

Tweety continued to fly and sing, happy to be free and safe.

Once upon a time there was a young boy named Sam. He loved to play outdoors. Today he was playing on the grass, just enjoying being outside. He noticed a butterfly flying by and he wanted to catch it. He started chasing it around and then suddenly he tripped and fell down, right on his knee.

It really hurt and he started to cry. His mom came over and saw what happened. She kneeled down and said, â€œLet me help you.â€ She tied a cloth around Samâ€™s knee to make it feel better.

Little Sam felt much better afterwards. His mom gave him a hug and said, â€œNow you can go back to playing.â€ Sam smiled and went back to chasing butterflies. He was happy to be back in the sunshine, feeling young again!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Bubbles. Bubbles loved to eat carrots and play with his friends in the grass. One day, Bubbles noticed that his yellow carrot was missing. 

He asked his friend, a little bird, "Did you see my yellow carrot?"

The bird replied, "No, but I can help you find it. Let's look together!" 

So, they searched high and low, but they couldn't find the yellow carrot. Bubbles was very sad because it was his favorite. 

But then, the bird had an idea. "Let's replace your yellow carrot with a big, juicy orange one!" 

Bubbles was hesitant at first, but he decided to give it a try. To his surprise, the orange carrot was even tastier than the yellow one! From then on, Bubbles was happy and content with his new carrot and grateful for his helpful friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, he saw a ladder leaning against his fence. He wanted to climb up the ladder but it was too tall for him.

Suddenly, Timmy's mom came outside and saw the ladder. She told Timmy that the ladder was spoiled and he shouldn't climb it. Timmy was sad but he listened to his mom and walked away.

Later that day, Timmy's dad came home from work. He saw the ladder and knew it was still good. He picked it up and passed it over the fence to their neighbor who needed it. Timmy watched as the ladder was passed over the fence and he felt happy knowing that it was being put to good use.

Tom and Anna were twins. They liked to play in the park with their dog, Spot. One day, they saw a new path in the park. It was quiet and had many trees and flowers.

"Let's go there!" Tom said.

"OK!" Anna said.

They ran along the path with Spot. They saw a bird, a butterfly and a squirrel. They were happy and curious.

But then, the path split into two. One went left and one went right.

"Which way should we go?" Anna asked.

"I don't know," Tom said.

They looked at each other. They did not want to get lost.

"Maybe we should go back," Anna said.

"But I want to see more," Tom said.

They did not agree. They started to argue.

"Left!"

"Right!"

"Left!"

"Right!"

Spot barked. He did not like the noise. He wanted them to stop.

He ran to the middle of the path. He looked at Tom and Anna. He wagged his tail.

He wanted them to follow him.

"Look, Spot has an idea!" Anna said.

"Maybe he knows the way," Tom said.

They stopped arguing. They smiled at each other.

They followed Spot. He led them to a big pond. It had ducks and fish and frogs. It was beautiful and peaceful.

"Wow, this is nice!" Tom said.

"Yes, it is!" Anna said.

They thanked Spot. They hugged him. They played by the pond. They forgot about the split path.

They were happy and together.

Once upon a time there was a hall. It was a smelly hall with lots of things in it. All the things were jumbled up and it was a mess. 

One day, a little girl came into the hall. She saw all the things jumbled and she decided to sort them. She worked and worked, picking up one thing at a time and putting it in the right place. 

It took her all morning, but soon the hall was clean and tidy. The little girl smiled and was happy that she had sorted all the things. 

The hall no longer smelled and now it was a nice place to be. All the things were in the right place and the little girl could enjoy the hall.

Once upon a time, there was a elderly man walking down the street. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from the sky above. It was an warning.

"Help! Beware of the cloud!"

The old man looked up and saw a big, billowing cloud hurdling through the sky. He quickly moved to the side of the street, making sure to stay out of its way.

He turned to a little 3-year-old girl who had been watching the cloud and said, "That cloud is not safe, young one. You should always listen to warnings and stay away from danger."

The girl nodded in response and ran off as the cloud passed by. 

The old man chuckled and admired the girl's bravery as she moved further and further away from the impending danger.

The moral of the story? Always listen to warnings and stay away from danger, no matter how small the warning.

Once upon a time there was a big mountain. The mountain was icy from the top to the bottom and had lots of vines growing up the side. One day, two friends decided to try and climb the mountain. So they put on their warm clothes and gathered their supplies.

The first friend started up the vines. He tried to reach the top, but it was too slippery. He tried and tried again but the icy vines wouldnâ€™t let him get very far.

But then the second friend had an idea. He put on his special shoes which had spikes on them. He stepped on the ice and started climbing up the vines using his spikes. He tried his best and finally made it to the top of the mountain.

The two friends were very excited. They celebrated their big victory and enjoyed the beautiful view from the top of the mountain. And from then on, the two friends never stopped trying to reach new heights.

Anna liked to dance. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the kitchen. She danced with her doll, with her cat, and with her mom. She danced fast and slow, high and low, happy and sad.

One day, she heard a knock on the door. She ran to open it and saw a lady with a big smile and a bag. The lady said, "Hello, Anna. I am your new dance teacher. Are you ready to learn some new moves?"

Anna nodded and clapped her hands. She was very excited. She followed the lady to the living room, where there was a lot of space. The lady took out a music box and a scarf from her bag. She said, "Today, we are going to dance like a butterfly. A butterfly is graceful and beautiful. It flutters its wings and flies in the air. Can you do that?"

Anna wrapped the scarf around her neck and pretended it was her wings. She moved her arms and legs like a butterfly. She twirled and jumped and spun. The lady played the music box and sang a song. Anna felt happy and free.

The lady clapped her hands and said, "Bravo, Anna. You are a wonderful dancer. You have a lot of talent and joy. I am proud of you." Anna smiled and hugged the lady. She said, "Thank you, teacher. You are very nice and fun. I love dancing with you." The lady said, "You are welcome, Anna. I love dancing with you too. See you next week." She gave Anna a sticker and a kiss and left. Anna waved goodbye and ran to show her mom her sticker and her scarf. She said, "Mom, look. I danced like a butterfly. It was so much fun." Mom said, "I saw you, Anna. You were graceful and beautiful. I am so happy for you." She kissed Anna and said, "Now, let's have some cookies and milk. You deserve a treat." Anna said, "Yay, cookies and milk. My favorite." She danced to the kitchen with her mom. She was very happy.

Sam and Mia are twins. They like to play in the pool with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big box near the pool. It has many pieces of foam in different colors and shapes.

"Look, Mia, what is that?" Sam asks.

"I don't know, Sam. Let's go and see," Mia says.

They run to the box and take out some pieces. They are soft and light. They throw them in the pool and watch them float.

"Wow, they are like boats!" Sam says.

"Or like hats!" Mia says. She puts a yellow piece on her head and laughs.

They jump in the pool and splash each other with water and foam. They have fun making shapes and patterns with the pieces. They also share them with their mom and dad, who join them in the pool.

After a while, they get tired and hungry. They get out of the pool and dry themselves with towels. They see a picnic basket on the grass. It has sandwiches, fruits, and juice.

"Come on, kids, let's have a snack," their mom says.

They sit on a big blanket and eat their food. They are happy and comfortable. They thank their mom and dad for the surprise.

"Mom, dad, where did you get the foam pieces?" Sam asks.

"They are a gift from your aunt Lucy. She works at a toy factory and she thought you would like them," their dad says.

"We love them! Thank you, mom and dad. Thank you, aunt Lucy!" Sam and Mia say.

They hug their mom and dad and smile. They look at the pool and the foam pieces. They can't wait to play with them again.

Tom and Lily wanted to make a pie with their mom. They needed apples for the pie. Mom said they could go to the garden and gather some apples from the tree.

Tom and Lily ran to the garden. They saw many red and green apples on the tree. They tried to reach them, but they were too high. They jumped and stretched, but they could not get any apples.

"This is difficult!" Tom said. "How can we get the apples?"

Lily had an idea. She saw a big basket near the tree. She dragged the basket to the tree. She said to Tom, "You stand on the basket. I will push you up. Then you can get the apples."

Tom climbed on the basket. Lily pushed him up. Tom reached the apples. He picked some and put them in the basket. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are smart."

Lily smiled. She said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are brave."

They gathered many apples in the basket. They carried the basket to the kitchen. Mom was happy to see them. She said, "Well done, Tom and Lily. You worked together and got the apples. Now we can make a delicious pie."

Tim and Liz are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big swamp near their house. They want to go and look.

"Let's go to the swamp!" Tim says. "Maybe we can find frogs and bugs."

"OK, but we have to be careful," Liz says. "The swamp is wet and muddy. And maybe there are snakes and crocodiles."

They hold hands and walk to the swamp. They see green plants and brown water. They hear birds and frogs. They smell something bad.

"Look, there is a frog!" Tim points. "It is green and shiny. It is charming."

He tries to catch the frog, but it jumps away. He follows it into the swamp. He gets his shoes and pants wet and dirty.

"Tim, come back!" Liz calls. "You are too far. The swamp is dangerous."

But Tim does not listen. He wants the frog. He goes deeper and deeper into the swamp. He does not see where he is going.

Suddenly, he hears a loud roar. He sees a big crocodile. It has sharp teeth and a long tail. It is not charming. It is scary.

"Help!" Tim screams. "There is a crocodile!"

Liz hears Tim. She is scared too. But she is brave. She runs to the swamp. She finds a big stick. She throws it at the crocodile. The crocodile is angry. It bites the stick and lets go of Tim.

"Tim, run!" Liz shouts. "Come to me!"

Tim runs to Liz. They hug each other. They are safe. They are happy.

They run away from the swamp. They go back to their house. They tell their mom and dad what happened. They are proud of Liz. She is a hero.

They learn a lesson. They do not go to the swamp again. They play in the yard. They find a charming frog. They are friends. They are happy.

The sky was grey and it started to rain. Benny was excited. He loved to jump in the puddles when it rained. He put on his boots and ran outside. As he jumped, the raindrops splashed on his face and the puddles got bigger and bigger.

Benny ran inside when he got too wet. His mom was making some delicious pasta for dinner. Benny loved pasta - it was his favorite food. He could smell it all the way from the kitchen. 

When dinner was ready, Benny and his mom sat down to eat. Benny was competitive when it came to eating pasta and finished first. His mom was so proud of him and said he had eaten like a champion, even though it was raining outside. 

Benny smiled and went back to his rain boots. He couldn't wait to go outside and jump in the bigger puddles again.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to fly higher than anyone else. Every day it practiced flying, and it got really good. One day it decided it wanted to show everyone so it organized a big event. Everyone gathered around the grill. The bird flew around and around above the grill, higher and higher each time. Everyone cheered and clapped as the bird flew above their heads. Everyone was amazed and proud of the little bird. From that day on it was the champion flyer!

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to his garden to play. He saw a rake and started to play with it. He used the rake to make a pile of leaves. Then, he jumped on the pile and laughed.

Suddenly, Timmy's mom came and said, "Timmy, I permit you to play with the rake, but be careful not to hurt yourself." Timmy nodded and continued to play.

While playing, Timmy found an ancient coin buried in the ground. He showed it to his mom and she was surprised. She said, "This is an ancient coin, Timmy! We should keep it safe." Timmy was happy to have found something special in his garden.

One day, there was a little boy. He was walking through the park and he saw a bird hopping around. He tried to catch it but it flew away. Suddenly he stumbled and fell. He started to cry.

A kind lady saw the little boy and came to help. She asked him what was wrong. The boy said he was sorry that he couldn't catch the bird. The lady said it was ok and she hugged him and said â€œItâ€™s ok, I forgive you.â€

The boy felt better. He thanked the lady and she smiled at him. Then the boy ran off to find more birds to catch. The kind lady watched the little boy go, with a warm feeling in her heart.

The fog was rolling in from the sea. It was thick and dangerous. Little Sandy was wrapped up warmly against the cold, standing at the edge of the beach and looking out over the grey mass, bravely. 

"Wow, it's really foggy out there," he said. He could just make out the boats out at sea, their sails barely visible in the darkness.

His dad joined him, placing a strong arm around his shoulders.

"It looks dangerous out there," he said, pointing to the fog, "That's why you should always stay close to the shoreline and never venture too far out at sea. This fog can be deceiving."

Little Sandy nodded and sighed and the two of them went back home, where his Dad storied him a story and tucked him in bed. 

The next day, the fog was even thicker, and the air seemed darker. Little Sandy's dad was pacing up and down the beach, wringing his hands with worry.

"Oh Sandy, I was afraid of this!" he said, "Some of the fishermen went too far out yesterday and the fog has been so thick, they can't find their way back!"

Little Sandy felt his heart beat faster. Those were the same words his father had spoken the night before. The same warning. He had been right. The fog was dangerous indeed.

Amy and her mom were very excited to visit Grandma's house. Grandma was always very cheerful and so were Amy and her mom. As they drove, they sang songs and talked about how much fun they were going to have visiting Grandma.

When they arrived to Grandma's home, they found a big surprise waiting - an alarm! Grandma had installed a new alarm to keep her house safe. Amy and her mom were so happy to see the alarm.

At Grandma's house, Amy and her mom had a great time visiting. Grandma was cheerful and cheerful again. They laughed and played games and ate treats. Amy was so happy to see Grandma and the alarm made the visit extra special. 

When it was time to leave, Amy and her mom hugged Grandma goodbye and thanked her for the wonderful visit. They waved goodbye and drove away, feeling cheerful and happy.

Once upon a time there were two little friends, Tom and Tim. Tom and Tim were very good friends and always did things together.
One sunny day, Tom and Tim were going for a jog in the park. As they were running, they came across an incredible temple.

When they had finished exploring, Tom and Tim thanked the guardian for letting them in. The guardian smiled and told them, â€œItâ€™s always important to be respectful and ask permission before entering a special place.â€

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a good dog, always happy and loyal to his owner. Max loved to play in the park and chase after balls.

One Wednesday, Max's owner took him to the park. Max was so excited to play, he barked and wagged his tail. But then, another dog came and took Max's ball. Max didn't like that and started to shout at the other dog.

The other dog didn't like that and started to fight with Max. Max was hurt and had to go to the vet. The vet tried to help Max, but it was too late. Max had to go to doggy heaven.

Max's owner was sad and missed him very much. They learned that shouting and fighting was not a good thing to do. They wished they could go back to that Wednesday and make things right.

Lily likes to sew with her mom. They have many colors of thread and make pretty things. Lily has a needle and a hoop and some cloth. She sews a flower with red and yellow thread.

One day, Lily hears a loud noise outside. She runs to the window and sees a big truck. The truck is taking away the old sofa from next door. Lily thinks the sofa is cozy and soft. She wonders why they are throwing it away.

She sees something shiny on the sofa. It is a spool of thread. It is purple, her favorite color. She wants to have it for her sewing. She runs outside and tries to get the thread. But the truck is moving fast. She can't catch it.

She hears a terrible sound. It is the thread breaking. The spool falls off the sofa and rolls on the street. Lily cries. She lost the purple thread. She runs back to her mom and hugs her.

Her mom sees her tears and asks what happened. Lily tells her about the thread and the truck and the noise. Her mom says she is sorry and kisses her. She says she has a surprise for her. She gives her a new spool of thread. It is purple, her favorite color. Lily smiles. She says thank you and hugs her mom. She sews a new flower with purple and yellow thread. She is happy.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra named Zee. Zee lived in a big forest. One day, Zee saw a yummy apple high up in a tree. Zee wanted the apple but could not reach it.

A bird named Bee saw Zee and asked, "Why are you sad, Zee?" Zee said, "I want the yummy apple, but I can't reach it." Bee wanted to help, so she tried to get the apple for Zee. But a mean cat came and scared Bee away.

Zee wanted to rescue Bee from the mean cat. Zee ran fast and scared the cat away. Bee was happy and said, "Thank you, Zee!" As a thank you, Bee got the yummy apple for Zee.

The moral of the story is to help your friends, and they will help you too.

Mummy was in the kitchen when a distant yelp was heard. She ran out to the garden where she saw her three year old daughter trying to rescue a tiny bird from a wheat field. 

"Oh, my darling! What are you doing?" asked Mummy.

"I hear it crying, Mummy. I'm trying to save it," said the daughter.

Mummy smiled and showed her how to carefully pick up the bird, checking for any damage. To everyone's relief, the bird was healthy and safe.

"Let's take it somewhere safe so it can fly away," said Mummy. Together they carried the bird to the nearest park and released it. They watched with joy as the bird flew away, far into the distant sky. 

They returned home with a smile on their faces and a happy heart.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty gray elephant. He was so big, he could carry giant logs! He was a strong elephant, but he still needed to rest. So, every day, he would take a nap in the sun. He loved feeling its warm rays and his mighty trunk loved to curl up and get comfy.

One day, a little bird came and asked the elephant if it wanted to take a nappy together. The elephant thought it was a fun idea! He curled up his big trunk and the little bird chirped with delight. They were so comfy together, the elephant was soon snoring gently. The bird found it funny and laughd happily!

When the sun started to set, the elephant woke up from his nap feeling refreshed. He thanked the little bird for joining him and said goodbye. As the elephant moved away, the little bird chirped a happy good-bye!

Lily liked to soar in the sky. She had a big balloon that was red and shiny. She tied it to her wrist and ran outside. The wind was strong and lifted her up. She felt happy and free.

She saw many things from the air. She saw her house, her garden, her dog, and her mom. She waved to them and they waved back. She saw the park, the pond, the ducks, and the slide. She wanted to play with them, but she was too high.

She also saw a bakery. It had a sign that said "Muffins". She loved muffins. They were soft and sweet and warm. She smelled them and her tummy growled. She wished she had a muffin.

But then she saw something else. She saw a big bird. It was black and had a sharp beak and claws. It saw her balloon and wanted to pop it. It flew towards her and screeched. She felt scared and sad.

She did not know what to do. She could not fly away. She could not fight the bird. She could only hold on to her balloon and hope. She closed her eyes and waited.

But then she heard a voice. It was her mom. She had a big net and a basket. She threw the net over the bird and caught it. She put it in the basket and closed the lid. She said "Don't worry, Lily, I'm here. I'll get you down."

She pulled the string of the balloon and brought Lily closer. She hugged her and kissed her and said "You're safe, my darling. You're brave, my star. You soared so high, but now you're home."

She took her inside and gave her a muffin. It was blueberry and had a lot of sugar on top. Lily ate it and smiled. She felt warm and full and loved.

She said "Thank you, mom. You're the best. You saved me from the bird. You gave me a muffin. You're my hero."

She said "You're welcome, Lily. You're my joy. You make me proud. You're my angel."

They hugged and cuddled and said "I love you". They looked at the empty basket and the empty sky. They did not need the balloon anymore. They had each other.

Anna and Ben are very happy. They are going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They pack their bags with toys and clothes. They get in the car and drive to the airport.

"Are we there yet?" Anna asks.

"Soon, sweetie," Mom says. "We are going to fly in a big plane."

Ben is excited. He likes planes. He wants to see the clouds and the birds. He looks out the window and sees many cars and trucks.

At the airport, they check in their bags and get their tickets. They walk to the gate and wait for their plane. Ben sees a big plane with blue and white stripes. He points and says, "Look, Anna, that's our plane!"

Anna nods and smiles. She holds Mom's hand and follows her to the plane. Ben holds Dad's hand and walks behind them. He is clumsy and trips over his own feet. He falls and bumps his head.

"Ow!" Ben cries.

"Are you okay, buddy?" Dad asks. He picks him up and hugs him.

"I'm okay," Ben says. He rubs his head and sniffs. "It hurts a little."

Dad kisses his head and says, "Don't worry, it will be better soon. You are a brave boy."

They board the plane and find their seats. Mom and Anna sit together and Dad and Ben sit together. They buckle their seat belts and listen to the pilot. He says, "Welcome aboard, ladies and gentlemen. We are ready to start our flight to Hawaii. Please enjoy your vacation."

Anna and Ben clap their hands and cheer. They are going on vacation. They are very happy.

One night, Dave was getting ready to take a test. He was feeling nervous, but he wanted to do his best.

Just before he was about to start, his mom came into the room. She smiled and said, "It's time to part, Dave. Good luck on your test!"

Dave smiled back and said, "Thanks, Mom!" He gave her a big hug and began his test.

He wrote down all his answers on the thin piece of paper. After a while, he looked up from his paper and smiled.

Good news - he had finished his test!

He carefully folded the thin test paper and took it to his mom. She smiled and said, "You did a great job, Dave! I'm proud of you."

Dave smiled and thanked her for her support. He felt so happy and relieved!

Tom liked to play in his room. He had many toys and books and a big wardrobe. Sometimes he pretended the wardrobe was a castle or a spaceship or a secret cave. He liked to open and close the doors and make noises.

One day, Tom was playing in his wardrobe. He was a king and he had a crown and a sword. He opened the door and said, "I am the king of this land. No one can stop me." He closed the door and said, "I am the king of this castle. No one can enter." He opened the door and said, "I am the king of this space. No one can catch me." He closed the door and said, "I am the king of this cave. No one can find me."

But then, something bad happened. Tom pulled the door too hard and it broke. The door came off the wardrobe and fell on the floor. Tom heard a loud snap and saw a big crack. He was scared and sad. He had broken his wardrobe. He had broken his castle and his spaceship and his cave. He cried and cried.

His mom heard the noise and came to his room. She saw the broken door and the crying Tom. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. It was an accident. We can fix the door. We can fix the wardrobe. You can still play in it. You are still the king."

Tom looked at his mom and smiled. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. You are tough. You can fix anything." He hugged her back and said, "I love you, mom. You are my queen."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look at the pretty colors in the sky. One day, she saw a big, beautiful rainbow in the sky. It was so pretty and made her feel happy.

Lily had a friend named Jack who was very kind and adorable. She wanted to marry him when she grew up. But one day, Jack did something mean to her. He took her toy and wouldn't give it back. Lily was sad and didn't want to be friends with Jack anymore.

But then, Lily remembered the rainbow and how it had so many different colors. She realized that even though Jack did something mean, he still had good qualities too. She forgave him and they became friends again. Lily learned that everyone makes mistakes, but it's important to forgive and see the good in others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily had an idea to have a picnic with her friends. She asked her mom for help and her mom offered to make some sandwiches for the picnic.

Once there was a yellow mint. It was sitting in a jar, minding its own business. All of a sudden, it heard a noise coming from the top of the jar. It was a pair of hands trying to open the jar! The mint tried not to get scared, and kept its cool.

The yellow mint was gone, but it was happy that the little boy enjoyed it. It was nice to have a chance to bring some joy to someone's life. Minding its own business had paid off!

Once there was a little girl called Gloria. She was very small and quite helpless. Every day, Gloria would go out to the garden to explore.

One day, she noticed something strange in the garden. Two Animal friends, Kevin the Rabbit and David the Squirrel were organizing something. She tried to get closer to have a look but they were too quick for her.

Gloria asked, "What are you doing, friends?"

David told her, "Sorry, sweetie, it's a surprise. We don't want you to know yet."

Then, Gloria got frustrated and angry and said, "That's not fair!"

But the Animal Friends had already finished their secret project. Then, they quickly ran away, leaving little Gloria feeling very helpless and disappointed. 

The next day, Gloria noticed some very odd shapes in the garden. It was the Animal Friends' surprise. They had organized an enormous shelter and there was no way Gloria could have anything to do with it. She was so sad and helpless that all she could do was watch her friends go into their shelter as if it were their own kingdom.

John was outside in the garden. He saw a post standing in the middle of the grass. He wanted to stand on top of it but it looked fragile. He was scared that if he stepped on it, the post would break. He wanted to try it but he was too scared.

Suddenly, his mom yelled at him not to do it. She said it was too dangerous and he might get hurt. But John still wanted to step on the post. He wanted to show his mom that he could do it. 

John decided to be brave. He slowly made his way towards the post and stood on it. It felt wobbly and he was scared but he stayed standing. His mom cheered for him and clapped. John was so proud he did it and smiled with joy. His mom hugged him and said he was very brave to try.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to look at the moon at night. The moon was big and round and it shone bright in the sky. Lily thought the moon was very pretty.

One night, Lily had a plan. She wanted to go to the moon! She asked her mom and dad if they could take her to the moon. They told her it was too far away and they couldn't go there. Lily was sad, but she still loved looking at the brown moon in the sky. She knew she would see it again tomorrow night. 

And so, every night, Lily would look up at the brown moon and dream about going there. She knew one day she would find a way to get there and see what it was like up close. Until then, she was happy just looking at it from her backyard.

John and Jane were two best friends. One day, they were playing together in the park. They were running and jumping around.

John suddenly noticed a big puddle in the park and he got an idea.

"Let's jump in the puddle", said John.

Jane was looking at the puddle with big eyes.

"Let's do it!" said John.

"But we will get wet!" said Jane.

John laughed and said, "It's OK, it's just water!"

John and Jane smiled at each other and then they did the silliest thing! They both jumped into the puddle with a lot of splashing!

The water was up to their waists. They were laughing and playing in the puddle for a long time. When they were tired, they ran away from the puddle and continued playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a furry teddy bear that she loved to hug. One day, Lily was playing outside when she fell and hurt her knee. It was bleeding and she was crying. 

Her mom came outside and saw what happened. She said, "Oh no, Lily! Let's go inside and put a bandage on your knee." Lily sniffled and said, "Will it hurt?" 

Her mom shook her head and said, "No, it won't hurt. It will make you feel better." They went inside and her mom cleaned her knee and put a bandage on it. 

Lily felt much better, but she was still scared to go back outside. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay to be scared. But remember, sometimes we fall down and get hurt. But we can always get back up and keep playing." Lily smiled and hugged her furry teddy bear. She felt much better and went back outside to play.

One day, a little girl named Lily went out to play in her yard. It was a cold day, but the sun was shining. She saw a small puddle from the rain last night. Lily wanted to find a dry spot to play with her toys.

She walked around her yard and found a dry place near a big tree. Lily called it "mine" because it was her special spot. She put her toys there and started to play. She made her toys talk to each other. 

One toy said, "Brr, it's cold today!" The other toy replied, "Yes, but we found a nice dry spot to play!" They played all day in the cold, dry spot under the tree. Lily was happy she found her special place.

Sara and Ben are best friends. They like to play in the garden. They dig in the soil with their hands and make mud pies. They also look for bugs and worms. They are not afraid of them. They think they are funny and interesting.

One day, they find a big, fat caterpillar. It is green and fuzzy. Sara picks it up and puts it on her nose. It tickles her. She giggles and says, "Look, Ben, I have a caterpillar nose!" Ben laughs and says, "You look silly, Sara. Can I try?" He takes the caterpillar and puts it on his ear. It wiggles and crawls. He laughs and says, "Now I have a caterpillar ear!"

They take turns putting the caterpillar on different parts of their faces. They laugh and laugh. They are having so much fun. They forget about the mud pies and the bugs and the worms. They only care about the caterpillar. They are very gentle with it. They do not hurt it. They are kind to it.

The caterpillar likes Sara and Ben. It thinks they are dependable friends. It trusts them. It does not mind being on their faces. It feels safe and warm. It is happy. It also laughs, but in a very quiet way. Only Sara and Ben can hear it. They are the only ones who understand it. They are the only ones who love it. They are the only ones who make it laugh.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many branches. They wanted to climb the tree and see the birds.

"Come on, Lily, let's go up the tree!" Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but be careful!" Lily said.

They climbed the tree and found a nest with three eggs. They were blue and speckled. They looked at the eggs and smiled.

"Wow, look at the eggs! They are so pretty!" Lily said.

"Shh, don't make noise! The mother bird might come back!" Tom said.

But it was too late. The mother bird came back and saw the children. She was angry and scared. She flew at them and pecked them with her beak.

"Ow, ow, ow! The bird is hurting us!" Tom said.

"Help, help, help! The bird is mad at us!" Lily said.

They tried to climb down the tree, but they were stuck. The bird was blocking their way. They were in a trap. They felt terrible.

"Help, help, help! We are in a trap!" Tom and Lily shouted.

A man heard their shouts. He was walking his dog in the park. He saw the children and the bird. He ran to the tree and climbed up. He shooed the bird away and helped the children down.

"Are you OK, kids? You should not touch the bird's nest. It is her home and she is protecting her eggs." The man said.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry! We did not mean to make the bird angry. We just wanted to see the eggs." Tom and Lily said.

"It's OK, kids. I'm glad you are safe. Next time, just look at the nest from far away. The eggs will hatch soon and you can see the baby birds." The man said.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you! You saved us from the trap!" Tom and Lily said.

They hugged the man and his dog. They learned their lesson. They never climbed the tree again. They watched the nest from the ground and waited for the baby birds. They were happy and grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to study the sky at night. One night, she saw a star that was not ordinary. It was very big and bright. Amy was very happy to see this special star.

"Mommy, let's decorate the room!" said Jack, who was very eager to make the room look exciting.

So Mommy and Jack gathered some chairs and a lamp. Jack made a square shape with his hands, and when they shone the lamp on the wall, they saw a big square shadow.

Jack laughed as he watched the shadow move. Then he made a triangle, a circle and a heart. The shadows looked majestic and Jack was proud of his work.

When they finished, the room had been beautifully decorated with shadows. Jack was so pleased he couldn't stop smiling. "This is the best day ever!" he shouted.

Once upon a time there was a rich boy. He just loved to rock in his rocker chair! He would rock, rock, rock all day long.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emma. One day, Emma was playing outside in her garden when suddenly the weather changed. It began to rain and the wind started to blow. Emma put her hands over her ears and yelled out loud, "That's too noisy!"

A friendly bird who was sitting in a tree nearby saw how scared Emma was of the weather. The bird flew down and landed on a nearby branch. She said to Emma in a polite voice, "Don't be afraid. This is just the way the weather is sometimes!"

Emma was very surprised to hear a bird talking to her. She stopped yelling, and listened again to all the noise that the storm was making, but this time she wasn't scared. She felt brave and the bird smiled at her.

Emma thanked the friendly bird and waved goodbye as the bird flew away into the sky. Emma went inside, happy that she wasn't scared of the weather anymore. She had learned it was okay to yell when you're scared, but it's even nicer to be polite!

Once upon a time there was a very charming print. It was a very special print, with lots of colours and shapes.

The moral of the story is that you must be careful how you react when others have things that you want. If you stay calm and practice balance, things will always work out for the best.

Once upon a time there was a lady who liked to explore far away lands. She was always searching for new minerals.

The lady decided to keep exploring and try to find more minerals, even though people ignored her. She kept searching and travelled to distant places.

Finally, the lady found a village where the people listened and admired the minerals she had found. She was no longer ignored, and everyone was happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abby. She liked to play outside and build things with her hammer. Her Mommy told her it was time to wash her hands. Abby shook her head and said "No!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was 3 years old and loved to play with her toys. One day Mary was playing when she felt a sharp pain in her leg. She began to cry and was very sad. 

Her mom heard her crying and came to comfort her. "What's the matter, Mary?" she asked. Mary looked up at her mom with tears in her eyes and said, "I have a bad pain in my leg."

Her mom looked worried and said, "ok, let me have a look. Please show me where it hurts." Mary pointed to a red mark on her leg. 

Her mom said softly, "I think you need to go to the doctor to have that checked. It might be a bit sore, but he can make it all better."

Mary smiled and nodded. She knew that the doctor could help her with her pain and make her sad heart happy again. So off they went to the doctor, who marked her leg and fixed her pain.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He wanted to be as fast as a fox. He wanted to run really fast and serve speed to everyone he met!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because it was his first day at school. He put on his coat because it was cold outside. Tim's mom walked with him to school, holding his hand all the way.

When they got to the school, Tim saw a big door. He felt a little scared. Tim's mom said, "Don't worry, you will have fun." Tim took a deep breath and peeked inside the door. He saw lots of kids playing and laughing.

At first, Tim was too shy to play with the other kids. But then, a nice girl named Sue came over and asked if he wanted to play. Tim felt happy and joined in. They played all day and became good friends. Tim learned that school was a fun place to be, and he couldn't wait to go back the next day.

Anna and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play with their toys and read books. They are very happy because tomorrow is a holiday. They do not have to go to school or do homework. They can have fun all day.

"Ben, what do you want to do on the holiday?" Anna asks.

"I want to go to the zoo and see the big animals. And I want to pet the fluffy rabbits and eat popcorn. Can we do both?" Anna says.

They run to the living room, where Mom and Dad are watching TV. They jump on the couch and hug them.

"Can I have your doll?" Sam asks Lily.

"No, it is mine. You can't have it," Lily says.

"Please, can you lend it to me? Just for a little while," Sam begs.

Lily thinks. She likes her doll, but she wants to be nice to Sam. She says, "OK, you can lend it, but you have to be careful. Don't break it or lose it."

Sam is happy. He takes the doll and hugs it. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend."

Lily and Sam play with the doll and other toys. They have fun. But then, Lily's mom calls them for lunch. They have to go downstairs.

"Give me back my doll," Lily says to Sam.

Sam says, "No, I want to keep it. It is mine now."

Lily is angry. She says, "No, it is not. You only lent it. You have to give it back."

Sam says, "No, I don't. It is mine. Go away."

Lily and Sam start to fight. They pull the doll from each other. They yell and cry. The doll is hard. It hurts their hands. The doll rips. The stuffing comes out. The doll is broken.

Sam is scared. He says, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to. Please don't be mad."

Lily's mom says, "Too late. You should have thought before. You are a bad friend. Go home now."

Sam leaves. He is sad. He has no doll. He has no friend. He has no fun. He wishes he never asked for the doll. He wishes he never fought with Lily. He wishes he was nice. But it is too late. He can't change what he did. He can't fix what he broke. He can't mend what he tore. He can only cry.

Tommy was walking along the beach one sunny day. The sand was warm, and the waves were gentle. He saw a friendly little fish swimming near the shore. He smiled and said hello. The fish swam closer and he reached out his hand and tried to touch it. The fish darted away and then came back again. Tommy laughed. It seemed like the fish was teasing him.

The tank crept through the forest until it saw a small creature picking flowers. "What are you doing?" the tank asked. 

The creature stopped picking flowers and said, "I am looking for my friends." 

The tank offered to help. Together they searched the forest until they heard a distant cry. 

The tank and the creature followed the sound and eventually found the creature's friends. They were very happy to see the tank and thanked it for being so obedient. 

The tank smiled and returned to its home, feeling proud of its help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved robots. He had a big, heavy robot toy that he played with every day. One day, Timmy's robot broke. He didn't know what to do. 

Timmy's dad said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We can manage to fix your robot." They took the robot apart and looked at all the pieces. Timmy's dad found the problem and fixed it. 

Timmy was so happy! He hugged his dad and said, "Thank you for fixing my robot. It's not heavy anymore!" From that day on, Timmy played with his robot every day and it never broke again.

One day, a small cat named Kitty and a dog named Doggy were playing in the park. They saw a big circle on the ground. It was a hula hoop. They did not know what it was for, but it seemed fun.

Kitty said to Doggy, "Let's see who can jump through the circle first!" Doggy agreed, and they took turns jumping through the circle. Kitty was fast, but Doggy was faster. They laughed and played with the circle all day.

As the sun began to set, they realized how useful the circle was for playing games. Kitty and Doggy decided to take the circle home with them. They knew they would have many more fun days playing with their new toy.

Lily liked to play with her computer. She had many games and pictures on it. She could make sounds and colors with it. She was happy when she played with her computer.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, we have to leave soon. We are going to visit grandma. Turn off your computer and get ready."

Lily did not want to leave. She wanted to play more. She said, "No, mom, I want to play. I don't want to go."

Mom said, "Lily, we have to go. Grandma is waiting for us. She has a surprise for you. It is something different. You will like it."

Lily was curious. She wondered what the surprise was. She asked, "What is it, mom? What is different?"

Mom said, "You will see when we get there. Come on, Lily, turn off your computer and put on your shoes. We have to leave now."

Lily turned off her computer and put on her shoes. She was still sad to leave her computer, but she was also excited to see grandma and the surprise. She hoped it was something fun and different. She said, "Okay, mom, let's go."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go to a restaurant with her family. Her mom said it was a terrible idea because the restaurant was too expensive. But Lily's dad encouraged them to go.

When they got to the restaurant, Lily was so excited. She saw lots of yummy food and pretty decorations. She asked her mom if they could get ice cream for dessert, and her mom said yes.

Lily's dad told her that she was doing a great job at being patient while they waited for their food. This made Lily feel happy and proud. She loved going to restaurants with her family.

Once upon a time there was a pretty onion. She wanted to be accepted by all the other vegetables, but they all thought she didn't belong. She felt a bit sad.

But one day she spotted a carrot in the corner. He was very friendly and accepted her straight away. He showed her around the garden and helped her make lots of new friends.

Soon the other vegetables began to accept the onion too. They helped her to grow bigger and made her feel happy.

The pretty onion was so pleased to have been accepted by everyone in the garden. She had lots of fun playing with her new friends and was no longer lonely.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very adventurous and loved to explore. One day, he went on a walk in the forest and saw a bird with a hurt neck. 

"Hello birdie, what happened to your neck?" Timmy asked.

"I hurt it while flying," the bird replied sadly.

"Don't worry, I can solve it!" Timmy said confidently.

So, Timmy took the bird to his mother who knew how to fix the bird's neck. The bird's neck was soon healed and the bird was able to fly again.

The moral of the story is that we should always help others when they are in need, even if it's just a small thing like helping a bird with a hurt neck.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong man. He liked to walk around the park every day. One day, he saw a long hose on the ground. He picked it up and started to play with it. He sprayed water all around and laughed. Then, he put the hose back where he found it and continued to walk. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish little boy. He wanted to go outside to play, but the sun was shining so bright that it made a huge shade. So the boy had an idea. He wanted to try and strike the shade away. 

The boy grabbed a stick and started to whack it against the shade. But no matter how hard he tried, the shade would not go away. He got so frustrated that he started to cry. 

Just then, a fairy appeared. She said, "Why are you so silly? You can't strike away a shade." The fairy waved her wand and made the sun go away, so the world around them was much cooler. 

The boy was so happy. He thanked the fairy, and they played tag together until it was time to go home. From that day, the boy learned that it is never a good idea to do something foolish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Tina. Tina was three years old. She had a big sister called Lisa who was eight years old. Everyday, Lisa would help Tina do lots of fun things.

One day, Lisa asked Tina if she wanted to learn how to make toast. Tina said yes and Lisa showed her how to do it. Lisa put two slices of bread in the toaster, and then set the timer. When the timer went off, out came the toast.

Tina was amazed and said "Wow, is this the toast?" Lisa said yes and they both put butter on their toast. Tina tasted it and said, "yummy!" She was so happy to have learned something new, and it tasted delicious.

After they finished their toast, Lisa said to Tina, "Now you know how to make toast, and anytime you want something yummy just make some toast!"  Tina smiled and said, "Thank you, Lisa!"  She was so proud of herself for learning how to make toast.

Mama had a very special box. It was brown and very shiny, like she had polished it a hundred times. She talked to her daughter about the box on Tuesday. She said it was a secret, but one day, if she was very good, Mama would show it to her.

Once there was a small boy. He was very happy and he liked to observe things around him. One day he went for a walk with his mom. They saw the police officers on duty. The boy was very curious about what the police officers were doing.

Once upon a time there was a brother and a sister. The brother and the sister loved to play together but one day something different happen.

Jim was a serious little boy who loved learning new things. One day, he heard a sound coming from his brain. It sounded like a beep.

He wondered what it was, so he decided to ask his mom for help. She told him that it was his brain working hard to think.

Jim was so proud to hear that his brain was working hard. He asked his mom if he could make it beep more often. She smiled and said that if he tried hard to learn and think more, it would beep.

Jim didn't want to stop learning, so every day he worked really hard and he could hear his brain beeping more and more. Eventually, his brain beeped so much that it seemed like it was talking to him. 

Jim had learned something serious and he was very happy that he could make his brain work so hard. He was now a very serious and intelligent boy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, she found a shiny rock on the ground. It was very unusual because it sparkled in the sun. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. Her mom told her that it was a valuable gemstone and that she should keep it safe. 

Lily didn't really understand what "valuable" meant, but she knew that the rock was special. She put it in her pocket and went back to playing. Later, when she showed her rock to her friends, they all thought it was really cool too. Lily felt proud to have something so unusual and valuable. 

As she grew older, Lily learned more about the value of things and how some things are more special than others. But she always remembered the little rock that she found and how it made her feel. She understood that sometimes the most unusual things can be the most valuable.

One day in the forest, a little deer was out for a walk. He saw many trees and ate some tasty leaves. But then he heard a sound. He looked behind him and saw a big bear. The deer was scared. He wanted to run away but the bear was too close. 

The deer said, "Please don't hurt me!" 
But the selfish bear said, "I'm hungry! I'm going to eat you!"

So the deer and bear struggled. The bear wanted to catch the deer, but the deer wanted to stay free. The deer used all of his strength to run away, and the bear used all of his to try and catch him. 

In the end, the deer was too fast and managed to escape. He ran away and the bear didn't follow. 
The little deer was relieved and happy to be safe and free.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots and play with his friends. One day, Benny's mom asked him to help her with the dishwasher. Benny didn't want to help because he wanted to play, but his mom said it was important. 

As Benny was putting the dishes away, he heard a loud noise. It was his friend, Sammy the squirrel, trying to escape from a tree. "Benny, help me escape!" Sammy cried. Benny knew he had to help his friend, so he quickly ran outside to the tree. 

Benny saw that Sammy was stuck in a branch, so he used all his strength to pull him out. "Thank you, Benny!" Sammy exclaimed. Benny felt happy that he could help his friend. From that day on, Benny knew that even though he may not want to do something, it's important to help others when they need it.

Macy was at the beach with her dad. She wanted to play in the sand and look for seashells. She chose to wear her navy blue bathing suit because it was sunny and nice out. 

Macy's dad smiled. "Ready?" He asked.

Macy smiled back and grabbed her beach toys.

Dad and Macy ran out into the ocean together. The waves were crashing and the water was cold. But Macy loved the feeling of the water on her skin. 

Suddenly, the sand began to shake beneath them. Macy and her dad turned around to see a mighty whale coming up out of the brilliantly blue water. 

Macy was filled with amazement. She had never seen anything so magnificent before. She wanted to stay and watch the whale swimming, but Dad said it was time to go.

Macy felt miserable when she realized she had to leave. She wished she had chosen to stay for just a few more minutes.

Once there was a little girl named Hope. She was excited because she had a special surprise. She saw a rabbit in a tree! Hope wanted to pet it but it ran away.

Hope was sad but then she heard a sound. It was a frog! Hope was so excited to see the frog that she clapped her hands. She slowly moved closer and the frog hopped away.

But then Hope got a really amazing sight. A colorful butterfly was flapping its wings in the air. Hope couldn't believe what she was seeing and she reached out her hand.

The butterfly landed on her finger and she was so excited. Hope laughed and smiled and tried to catch the butterfly with her other hand. But the butterfly flew away and snapped its wings in the wind. 

Hope was so sad but then the rabbit suddenly appeared and playfully slapped her on the nose! Hope was so happy to see the rabbit she laughed and hugged it. She was so excited to have made a special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and go outside to play with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the grocery store. While they were waiting in line, Timmy saw a toy that he really wanted. He asked his mom if they could buy it, but his mom said they didn't have enough money.

Timmy was sad, but he decided to plan for the toy. He started to save his allowance every week. After a few weeks, he had enough money to buy the toy. Timmy was so lucky that the toy was still in the store. He was very happy and proud of himself for saving his money.

The moral of the story is that if you plan and save your money, you can get the things you want. Timmy learned that it's important to be patient and work hard to achieve your goals.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Susie and she was three years old. Susie was playing in the garden one day when she saw something shiny in the grass. She went to see what it was and it was a hoop! It was made of silver and it was so pretty that Susie wanted to take it home.

Susie picked up the hoop and held it in her hands. She was so lucky to find such a nice hoop! 

Susie decided to take the hoop home and play with it. She took it to her backyard and started to mind her hoop. She would spin it around and around and around. She hopped and skipped after the hoop, laughing and smiling as she watched it spin.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big pink tower made of blocks. One day, Lily's friend came over to play. "Wow, that tower is so big!" said Lily's friend. "Can we play with it?" Lily replied, "Yes, but first we have to unpack it from the box." 

Lily and her friend unpacked the tower and started building it higher and higher. They were having so much fun until Lily's little brother came in and knocked the tower down. "Oh no!" cried Lily. But her friend said, "It's okay, let's build it again!" 

So they built the tower again, even taller than before. They were so proud of their tower and showed it to Lily's mom. "Wow, that's amazing!" said Lily's mom. Lily smiled and said, "We unpacked it and built it all by ourselves!"

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Bubbles. Bubbles lived in a big ocean with lots of other fish. One day, Bubbles went to visit his friend, Sammy. 

When Bubbles got to Sammy's house, he saw that Sammy was not there. Bubbles looked around and saw a big reef. The reef seemed like a good place to explore, so Bubbles swam over to it.

As Bubbles swam around the reef, he saw that it was full of bright colors and lots of different fish. Suddenly, Sammy appeared from behind the reef. "Hi Bubbles! What are you doing here?" Sammy asked.

"I wanted to explore the reef. It's so crazy!" Bubbles said. "Do you want to come with me?"

"Sure!" Sammy said. "Let's go explore together." 

Bubbles and Sammy swam around the reef, looking at all the different fish and colors. They had so much fun together that they decided to explore more of the ocean together next time.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But sometimes they get bored.

One day, they find something unusual on the carpet. It is small and round and green. It looks like a pea, but it is not a pea.

"What is this?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is candy," Mia says.

She picks it up and puts it in her mouth. She makes a face. It is not candy. It is bitter and sour and yucky.

"Yuck! This is not candy! This is bad!" Mia spits it out.

Tom laughs. He thinks Mia is funny. He picks up another green thing. He wants to try it too.

"Maybe this one is candy," he says.

He puts it in his mouth. He makes a face too. It is not candy. It is worse than the first one. It is spicy and hot and ouchy.

"Ouch! This is not candy! This is worse!" Tom spits it out.

Mia laughs. She thinks Tom is funny. They look at each other. They have green stuff on their teeth and tongues.

They hear a voice. It is Mom. She is coming to their room.

"Tom, Mia, what are you doing?" Mom asks.

She sees the green things on the carpet. She sees the green stuff on their mouths. She knows what they are.

"Tom, Mia, those are not candy. Those are seeds. They are for the bird. They are not for you. They are bad for you. They can make you sick," Mom says.

She takes the seeds away. She gives them water. She cleans their mouths. She hugs them.

"Next time, do not eat anything you do not know. Ask me first. OK?" Mom says.

Tom and Mia nod. They say sorry. They learned their lesson. They do not want to eat seeds again. They want to eat real candy.

Once upon a time in a land far away, there lived two best friends, Joe and Will. Joe was a three year old and Will was a dinosaur. Each morning when Joe woke up, he would promise Will that he would play with him.

One day, Joe woke up feeling very tired, but he still remembered his promise to Will. Joe crawled out of bed and trudged outside to see Will. When Joe arrived, he saw that Will had set up a game of hide and seek.

Joe wanted to play, but he was still very tired. For a moment, Joe wanted to go back to bed, but then he remembered his promise. Joe knew he had to keep his promise and make his best friend happy.

Joe smiled and started playing with Will. After a few minutes, Joe was no longer tired. He was too busy having fun.

Moral of the story: A promise made is a promise kept! Whenever you make a promise to someone, no matter how difficult it might seem, make sure to keep it. Being honest and keeping your word will make you and your friends very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big office. Inside the office was a heavy box. Everyone wanted to find the box so they could open it up. 

Every day, they looked and looked, but they couldn't find it. Then one day, they saw a big mouse run into a corner and hide. They followed the mouse and soon they found the heavy box.

Mommy had a surprise for Lilly. Lilly was three and very excited.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Timmy. He was very obedient and liked to try new things. One day, he decided to try and run up the hill. His friends cheered him on, but warned him it would be hard. Timmy tried his best, and soon he felt like his lungs were about to burst. 

He was doing so well, but then he stopped and started to cry. He was too tired and he couldn't catch his breath. His friends quickly hugged him and tried to calm him down. But, it was too late. Timmy had hurt his lungs and had to go to the doctor.

The moral of the story is to never try something if you know that it's going to be too hard. It is important to be obedient, but it's even more important to be safe.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Lucy. She was very curious and wanted to learn new things.

One day, she decided to learn how to add, so she came up with a game. She took 2 cups, one empty and one filled with water, and her dad joined her.

Dad said: "If we add the two cups together, what do you think will happen?"

Dad smiled and nodded: "Yes, that's right! When something is too much, it can be dangerous. That's why we have to be careful and not add too much!"

Lucy nodded and understood the lesson. From then on, every time she added something to anything, she thought carefully and made sure not to add too much.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved to stir. Everywhere she went, she would take a big spoon and stir! One day, the girl decided to go to the woods. She wanted to find something really beautiful to stir.

The girl went walking through the woods and soon saw something wonderful. She saw a big puddle of beautiful bubbly blue water. She put down her spoon and decided to go and explore. 

The girl started to stir the water with her hands. She found that the water bubbled and rippled in the most beautiful way. Then, she noticed something in the water. It was a piece of old wood!

The girl took the piece of wood and went to find a stick. She started to stir with the stick and the piece of wood in the water. Suddenly, a beautiful flower bloomed from beneath the water. 

The girl was so happy! She continued to stir and more and more beautiful flowers bloomed from the puddle. 

She had found something wonderful in the woods... a beautiful way to stir.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jim and Bob. They liked to explore the woods near their house together.

Little Emma was gazing out her bedroom window. She looked at the bright trees with colorful leaves, the cute little bunnies hopping about, and the quiet bird in the sky.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Amy had a pet puppy. She played and talked to her puppy every day, and they quickly became the best of friends. Amy felt very lucky to have such a loyal pet.

Once there was a girl named Molly who liked to write. She loved to draw pictures and write stories. One day, it was a very hot day and Molly thought it would be fun to write in the bathtub. So she ran to the bathroom and filled the bathtub with water.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw his friend, Sue, near a mailbox. Sue looked sad.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, James and Joe. They were always together and had lots of fun.

One day, James wanted to go for a drink and he asked Joe to come along. When they went to the cafe, Joe wanted a tasty dessert to go with his drink but he had no money. James said, â€œDonâ€™t worry Joe. I will get you dessert.â€

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Daisy who had a very messy room. On a shelf in her room was a special book.

Ben and Sam were friends who liked to play outside. They had a toy gun that made a loud noise when they pulled the trigger. They pretended to be cowboys and chased each other around the yard.

One day, they saw a big rabbit in the grass. It had long ears and a fluffy tail. Ben and Sam wanted to catch it and pet it. They grabbed their toy gun and ran after the rabbit.

"Stop, rabbit, stop!" Ben shouted. "We just want to play with you!"

But the rabbit was scared of the boys and their toy gun. It hopped away as fast as it could. It hopped over the fence, into the neighbor's garden.

Ben and Sam followed the rabbit. They climbed over the fence and looked around. They saw many flowers and vegetables growing in the garden. They also saw a sign that said "Keep out!"

"Uh-oh," Sam said. "We are not supposed to be here. This is Mr. Jones's garden. He is very mean and angry. He does not like children or animals."

Ben and Sam did not care. They wanted to find the rabbit. They walked through the garden, stepping on the plants and making a mess. They did not see Mr. Jones watching them from his window.

Mr. Jones was very mean and angry. He did not like children or animals. He saw Ben and Sam in his garden, with their toy gun. He thought they were trying to steal his flowers and vegetables. He grabbed his real gun and went outside.

"Hey, you!" Mr. Jones yelled. "Get out of my garden, you little rascals! Or I'll shoot you!"

Ben and Sam heard the loud voice and turned around. They saw Mr. Jones with his real gun. They were very scared. They dropped their toy gun and ran back to the fence. They tried to climb over it, but it was difficult. The fence was high and sharp.

Mr. Jones aimed his real gun at the boys. He pulled the trigger. But nothing happened. His gun was empty. He had forgotten to load it.

Ben and Sam heard the click and looked back. They saw Mr. Jones with his empty gun. They were not scared anymore. They laughed at him and stuck out their tongues.

"Ha ha, your gun does not work!" Ben said. "Our gun is better than yours!"

Ben and Sam hopped over the fence and ran back to their yard. They picked up their toy gun and played some more. They forgot about the rabbit and Mr. Jones. They were happy and silly. They did not know how lucky they were.

Once upon a time there was a fisherman who had the most colorful boat in the town. He was the happiest fisherman around because no-one else had a boat that was as bright and beautiful as his.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the forest behind his house. One day, he saw a butterfly and wanted to follow it. So, he ran after the butterfly and lost track of where he was going. 

Timmy got scared and didn't know how to get back home. He looked around and saw a tall tree. He thought he could stand on it and see his house from there. But when he climbed up, he got upset because he couldn't see anything. 

As the sun began to set, Timmy started to cry. He was all alone and didn't know what to do. Unfortunately, nobody found him and he had to spend the night in the forest. The next morning, the search party found Timmy, but he was very sick from being outside all night. From then on, Timmy never went into the forest alone again.

Bob was a little boy who loved the beach. He loved to splash in the waves, scoop up the shells and even stand still with the tide coming in and out around his feet. One day, Bob decided to take a walk along the beach. He hopped and skipped along, feeling the sand between his toes and the warm sun on his face. 

But as Bob kept walking, the tide started to come in quickly. It was way bigger than usual, and Bob felt a little confused. He tried to turn around, but the water was blocking his way. Bob started to miss the sand and the sun. He wanted to go back to them, but he didn't know how. 

Suddenly, Bob spotted a big rock right in front of him. He had never noticed it before, but it was huge and tall. Right away, Bob had an idea. When the tide finally went back out, Bob jumped back down and continued to hop and skip along the beach. He was no longer confused, and he was glad to be back in the warm sand and sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a 3 year old girl named Lily. She was so excited because it was her birthday! Lily and her family went out to celebrate. She was so happy because they had fun together.

Once upon a time there was a mama and a baby. Mama had something silver and shiny with her. The baby wanted the silver thing but Mama said no. Mama and Baby disagreed.

Jen and Ben liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very proud of their snowman.

But Tom, the boy next door, was spoiled. He did not like to share or be nice. He wanted to ruin Jen and Ben's snowman. He waited until they went inside for hot cocoa. Then he sneaked out with a bucket of water. He poured the water over the snowman. He hoped the water would turn to ice and make the snowman hard and ugly.

But he did not know that Jen and Ben had a sign. The sign said "Please do not touch our snowman. He is our friend." They had put the sign behind the snowman, where Tom could not see it. They had also put a stick under the sign, to make it stand up.

When Tom poured the water, the sign got wet too. The stick became slippery and fell down. The sign slid down the snowman's back and hit Tom on the head. It made a loud noise and hurt Tom a lot. He dropped the bucket and ran away, crying.

Jen and Ben heard the noise and came out. They saw the sign on the ground and the bucket next to it. They saw Tom's footprints in the snow. They knew what he had tried to do. They were angry and sad.

But then they looked at their snowman. He was still smiling, with his hat and scarf. The water had not turned to ice. It had made the snowman shiny and sparkly. He looked even more beautiful than before.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and wanted to eat something yummy. His mom asked him what he wanted to eat, and Timmy said he wanted a sandwich. So, his mom went to the kitchen to prepare a sandwich for Timmy.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty rabbit who liked to play jokes on his friends. One day, he decided to hide in a bush and scare his friend, the squirrel. When the squirrel came along, the rabbit jumped out and yelled "boo!", but the squirrel was not amused.
