"What is it?" he asked his friend, Sarah.

Sarah said, "Let's go look and find out!"

So the two of them walked to the trees. The smoke seemed to be coming from behind one of the trees, so they went round to have a closer look.

When they got there, they saw a small campfire hidden in between the roots of the tree.

"Someone must have made the fire here," said Sarah.

The two friends stared at the fire for a while and watched the smoke rise into the sky. Then Sarah suggested, "Let's go and find the person who made this fire!" 

So, the two of them searched around the area but couldn't find anyone. In the end, they had to leave without learning who had made the hidden campfire.

Lily loved ice-cream. She liked all kinds of ice-cream, but her favorite was chocolate. She wanted to own a big tub of chocolate ice-cream and eat it every day.

One day, she went to the shop with her mom. She saw a big tub of chocolate ice-cream in the freezer. She asked her mom if she could buy it. Her mom said no, it was too big and too expensive. Lily was sad.

She looked around the shop and saw a small cone of chocolate ice-cream. It was only one dollar. She asked her mom if she could buy it. Her mom said yes, it was small and cheap. Lily was happy.

She gave her mom one dollar and took the cone. She licked the ice-cream and smiled. It was cold and sweet and yummy. She felt like she owned the best ice-cream in the world.

She walked out of the shop with her mom. She saw a boy crying on the sidewalk. He had dropped his ice-cream on the ground. He had no more ice-cream and no more money. Lily felt sorry for him.

She walked up to him and offered him her cone. She said, "Here, you can have my ice-cream. I have enough." The boy stopped crying and looked at her. He smiled and said, "Thank you. You are very kind." He took the cone and licked the ice-cream. He felt like he owned the best ice-cream in the world.

Lily and the boy became friends. They shared the ice-cream and talked. They found out they liked the same things. They decided to play together. They had fun.

Lily learned that ice-cream was not only good to eat, but also good to share. She learned that owning something was not as important as being generous. She learned that there was always more ice-cream available if she looked for it. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink tea with her mom every day. One day, they went to a charming tea shop in town. The tea shop had many pretty teacups and tasty treats.

Lily saw a butterfly and said, "Look, Mommy! A butterfly!" Her mom replied, "Yes, it's beautiful. But be careful, it might vanish if you get too close."

Lily and her mom ordered some tea and cookies. They talked about their day and enjoyed their delicious treats. Suddenly, Lily's mom noticed that her teacup was missing. She asked the tea shop owner, "Excuse me, have you seen my teacup? It seems to have vanished." The tea shop owner searched and found the teacup hiding behind a charming teapot. They all laughed and continued to enjoy their tea time together.

Bob and his mum were at the church. Bob was sad and he started to cry. His mum gave him a big hug. 
She said "Don't cry, Bob. Look over there".
Bob looked and saw a beautiful bride in a big white dress, wearing a veil. 
The bride looked very tidy. She was smiling and Bob stopped crying. 
Mum said "Do you know what that is? That is a bride getting married." 
Bob smiled and said "I want to be a bride one day". His Mum said "You can be, when you're older Bob". 
Bob felt better and was happy. He gave his mum a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a man who worked in a big office. He had a special stick called a staff that helped him walk. Every day, he would point to the papers on his desk and work hard.

One day, the man noticed that his staff was missing. He looked everywhere but couldn't find it. He felt sad and guilty because he had lost something important.

Later that day, a little girl came into the office with the man's staff. She had found it outside and wanted to return it. The man was so happy and grateful that he gave the little girl a big hug. From that day on, he made sure to always keep his staff close by and never forget it again.

A little boy was so excited to get his first toy car. He ran up to it and it was black and smooth. 

The little boy asked his mom, â€œMommy, can I play with the car?â€  His mom said, â€œYes you can, but be careful!â€

The little boy was so happy. He pushed the car with his tiny hands and the car moved really fast. He smiled with excitement and ran after the car. 

But then, the car started to move too fast and the little boy could not catch it. It went down a hill and the little boy needed help. But there was no one around to help him. 

In the end, the little boy watched sadly as his toy car disappeared and he never saw it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, Lily was scared of the dark and wanted to sleep with her flashlight. She turned it on and saw a shadow on her wall. She was fearful and didn't know what it was. 

Lily's dad came in and saw her flashlight. He asked her what was wrong and she told him about the shadow. Her dad took the flashlight and stretched his arm out to shine it on the wall. 

The shadow was just a tree branch outside her window. Lily felt better and went back to sleep with her flashlight. From that night on, Lily was never afraid of the dark again because she knew her flashlight could help her see and her dad could stretch to make the shadows disappear.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to watch videos on her tablet. One day, Lily's tablet broke and she couldn't watch any videos. She was sad and didn't know what to do. 

Lily's mom took her to the store to choose a new tablet. There were so many tablets to choose from! Lily picked one that was pink and sparkly. She was happy again because she could watch videos on her new tablet. 

But one day, Lily's tablet fell into a smelly mud puddle. It smelled so bad! Lily didn't know what to do. She tried to clean it, but it wouldn't turn on. Lily was sad again because she couldn't watch her videos. 

Lily's mom took her to the store again to choose a new tablet. Lily picked one that was blue and shiny. She was happy again because she could watch videos on her new tablet. And she made sure to be careful with it so it wouldn't fall into any more smelly mud puddles!

Once upon a time, there were two kids. One was named Sue and the other was named Jack. They were best friends. 

Jack and Sue found a dead animal in the park. "What should we do?" asked Sue. Jack thought for a moment, then said, "Let's sort it out."

So they took the dead animal and buried it in the ground. Then they marked the grave with a rock and said a few kind words. 

When they finished, Jack said, "Let's go play!" And they ran off to have fun.

The clown blinked and his eyes lit up. He smiled a wide happy smile and started to juggle three balls in the air. Everyone around him laughed and clapped. The clown kept juggling and he even started to sing a silly song.

Suddenly, the clownâ€™s face changed. His smile turned sour and he stopped juggling. He blinked again and looked worried. The people around him could see that something was wrong.

The clown slowly pointed at a small boy in the crowd. Everyone gasped when they saw what the clown was pointing at. The little boy had taken a bag of sweets from the clownâ€™s pocket!

The clown took a deep breath, blinked and shook his head. Even though he was angry, he found it hard to stay mad. He smiled at the boy and offered him some free sweets. The boyâ€™s eyes lit up and he quickly accepted the offer. Everyone cheered and celebrated, and the clown blinked one last time as he remembered why he loves his job.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to eat celery. He would munch on it all day long. One day, Benny saw his friend, a squirrel named Sammy, eating a carrot. Benny wanted the carrot so badly, but Sammy wouldn't share. 

Benny felt sad and ignored by Sammy. He decided to go for a walk to find more celery. As he was walking, he saw a big, red apple on the ground. Benny knew he shouldn't take it because it wasn't his, but he couldn't resist. He took a bite and felt guilty. 

Benny realized that he shouldn't have taken the apple without asking. He went back to Sammy and apologized for feeling jealous and taking the apple. Sammy forgave Benny and they shared some celery together. From that day on, Benny learned to never ignore his friends and to always ask before taking something that wasn't his.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was very obedient. His name was Bill. Every day Bill would go outside and listen very carefully. He wanted to hear the sound of his neighbor's dog, who he was very fond of.

So one day Bill went outside and did as he usually did - he listened. He was very quiet and could hear a distant bark. It was the bark of his neighbor's dog! Bill was so happy. he excitedly jumped up and down for joy.

He ran to the fence and began to listen intently. He heard the sound of the neighbor's dog barking and he was so pleased. He smiled and was sure to be extra obedient. Every day he would go back and listen until he heard the sound of the neighbor's dog. He just loved the sound and found it soothing.

And so whenever Bill needed a little bit of joy, he would just listen and soon enough he would hear the sound of the neighbor's dog again. He was happy and grateful he was so obedient.

One day, a little boy named Tim had a toy vehicle. It was a red car that could go very fast. He loved to play with it all day long.

Tim wanted to make his vehicle look cooler. He got some paper and cut it into small pieces. He was a little confused about how to make the car look better with the paper, but he tried his best. He glued the paper pieces onto the car to make it look like it had wings.

Now, Tim's vehicle looked like a flying car. He was so happy and played with it even more. His friends saw the car and thought it was cool too. They all played together, having fun with the red flying car.

Once upon a time, there was a raven named Jack. Jack was a big black bird with shiny feathers. One day, Jack saw a shiny object on the ground. He flew down to take a closer look. It was a useful tool that he could use to twist things. 

Jack picked it up with his beak and flew back to his nest. He showed it to his raven friends, who were all impressed. They asked him where he found it, but Jack didn't remember. 

Later that day, Jack used the tool to twist some sticks together to make a strong nest for his family. His raven friends were amazed at how useful the tool was. From that day on, Jack always kept the tool close by, ready to use whenever he needed to twist something.

Mummy was in the kitchen. She was getting ready to make some cookies. "What are you doing, Mummy?" asked the little girl.

"I'm going to make some cookies. Would you like to help me?" asked Mummy.

The little girl was very excited and nodded her head.

Mummy got out the eggs, butter and flour to prepare the cookies. She showed the little girl how to mix the ingredients. The little girl was getting serious about making the cookies - she wanted them to turn out perfectly!

After the mixture was ready, Mummy showed the little girl how to roll it out into circles and cut it into shapes. Then they carefully put the shapes on a baking tray and put them in the oven.

The little girl and Mummy waited patiently for the cookies to bake. When they were ready, the little girl was so excited to eat the cookies! They both enjoyed the tasty treat!

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful leopard who lived near a big pond. The leopard loved to swim in the water every day. One sunny day, while the leopard was swimming, he saw a little duck.

"Hi, little duck," said the leopard. "Do you want to swim with me?"

The little duck looked at the thoughtful leopard and said, "Yes, I would love to swim with you."

So, the leopard and the little duck swam together in the big pond. They had so much fun playing and splashing in the water. The sun was shining, and they were very happy. After a long day of swimming, they became good friends. From that day on, the thoughtful leopard and the little duck always swam together in the big pond.

Fred was a little boy who loved to play. He loved to run and jump around the playground, pretending he was a superhero.

One day he saw a girl who looked sad. She was sitting alone on the swingset, her head facing down. Fred walked up to her and asked, "What's wrong?"

The girl didn't answer right away. After a few seconds, she said, "I can't finish my coloring book. Every time I try, I make a mistake."

Fred smiled. He looked at her with kind, compassionate eyes and said, "I can help you. Let's finish it together."

The little girl smiled and nodded. Together, they worked on the coloring book. They colored each page carefully and with precision.

When they were finished, the girl thanked Fred for helping her. She said, "Thank you for your help. You have a very kind face."

Fred beamed. He was glad that he could help the little girl with her problem, and even happier for her kind words. "You are welcome," he said with a smile.

One day, a mommy took her little boy to the park. All around them, the sky was wet and grey. Little boy was excited - he wanted to play.

Mommy took his hand and together they walked to the pitch. He looked around and saw lots of other boys and girls playing on it. Little boy smiled and clapped his hands.

Mommy told him it was time to play a game. She asked him to carry a round, red ball. He touch the ball - it was bouncy, and it felt nice.

Mommy threw the ball and it went high into the sky. Little boy ran and tried to catch it, but it was too high. He kept trying and quickly got better at it. Soon he was carrying the ball back and forth, very carefully!

Mommy and little boy played until it started raining. The pitch got wet and cold, so they decided to go home. Little boy was happy with his adventure. He had a great day with his mommy and the ball at the wet pitch.

Lila was a curious girl who liked to explore the forest near her home. One day, she saw a big cat with yellow fur and black spots. She had never seen such a cat before and wanted to know more. She followed the cat quietly, hoping to get closer.

The cat was a leopard who was hunting for food. He did not notice Lila at first, but soon he heard a twig snap behind him. He turned around and saw the girl staring at him with wide eyes. He growled and showed his sharp teeth, ready to attack.

Lila was scared and ran away, but the leopard was faster and chased her. She cried for help, but no one was around. She wished she had listened to her mother, who always told her not to go too far into the forest.

Then, she heard another voice, a loud and deep voice, that made the leopard stop. It was Lila's father, who had heard her call and came to rescue her. He had a big stick and waved it at the leopard, who backed away and ran off.

Lila ran to her father and hugged him. She was sorry for being so curious and foolish. She thanked him for saving her and promised to never follow strange animals again. Her father was glad that she was safe and forgave her. He told her that curiosity was good, but she had to be careful and listen to her parents. They walked back home together, holding hands.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved watching television. Every day his parents would sit him in front of the television, and he would stay there for hours. He loved all the colors on the television!

One day, while his parents were at work, they asked the boy to keep an eye on the deep blue sea that was out the window. They said that he must watch it and not move until they came back.

The little boy was so excited to watch the sea that he forgot all about the television. He watched the blue sea for the whole day and forgot to watch the television. 

When his parents came back, he was filled with deep regret for not watching the television. He had been so excited to watch the sea that he had forgotten all about the television.

The little boy never forgot the lesson he learnt that day, and now he watches the television carefully every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily was playing on the porch when she saw her friend, Tommy, walking by.

"Hi, Tommy!" Lily said. "Do you want to dance with me?"

Tommy smiled and said, "Sure, I love to dance!"

So, Lily and Tommy danced and twirled on the porch. After a while, they got tired and sat down to rest.

"I'm so tired," Lily said.

"Me too," Tommy said. "Let's go get some juice."

Lily and Tommy went inside and got some juice. They sat on the porch and drank their juice while watching the birds fly by. It was a beautiful day and they were happy to have danced together.

Once upon a time there was a brave beetle named Bob. He lived deep in the forest and every day liked to explore different places. One day while he was out, he heard a loud sound coming from the nearby hill. He was curious, so he crept closer to the noise.

When he got to the top of the hill, he saw a fierce beast! It was huge and had sharp teeth. Bob was brave, but he was also scared. He couldn't turn back and he was too brave to run away. Instead, he slowly walked closer to the beast.

"Please don't hurt me," he said politely. The fierce beast paused and looked at Bob. Then, it said in a harsh voice,
"I dare you to climb up my back and see the view from the top. If you do it, I promise I won't hurt you."

Bob had never climbed anything before, but he was brave. He knew he could do it! He took a deep breath and slowly he started to climb. The beast was rough, but Bob kept going one step at a time. Finally, he made it to the top and he gasped in amazement.

The view was beautiful! Bob had never seen so many colors and shapes in his life. He thanked the beast, and then slowly climbed back down. The beast smiled and said "you are very brave, brave beetle!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy cart and fill it with her favorite toys. One day, she went to the park with her cart and found a lost puppy. She was so happy to have a new friend and decided to take the puppy home with her.

When she got home, her mom was surprised to see the puppy. Lily explained that she found it at the park and wanted to keep it. Her mom was grateful that Lily had a big heart and decided to keep the puppy.

As the puppy grew, Lily had to change her cart to a bigger one so she could take the puppy for walks. She was very happy to have a new friend and a new cart to play with. From that day on, Lily and her puppy went on many adventures together in their cart.

Once, there was a very shy boy who lived on a street with a number. Every day he watched the other kids play and wished he could join, but he was too shy.

One day he mustered up all his courage, and walked out onto his street. He felt strange and scared. He kept his head low, but the other children noticed him. They invited him to join their game.

The shy boy said nothing and kept his head low. But the other kids asked his name and his number on his street. He told them.

The other kids clapped their hands. Together they ran around the street and played until the sun went down.

The shy boy was so happy he went home with a big smile on his face. From that day on he was no longer shy, and he made lots of friends on the street by his number.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books about animals and princesses. One day, her mom told her they were going on a trip to the zoo. Lily was so excited to see all the animals she had read about in her books.

Before they left, Lily's mom made sure they had healthy snacks to eat on their trip. They packed apples, carrots, and water bottles. Lily loved eating healthy because it made her feel strong and happy.

At the zoo, Lily saw lions, tigers, and bears. She was amazed at how big and strong they were. She even got to see a princess parrot that looked just like the one in her book. Lily had so much fun on her trip and couldn't wait to read more books about the animals she saw.

Once there was a happy bird. He liked to pour water in the river. Every day he would find a new puddle and pour the water into it.

One day, he heard a small voice calling out. He flew down low and saw a little girl. She was three years old and said to him, "Please pour me some water into my bucket".

The bird was happy to help, so he flew down to the river and grabbed some water with both his wings. He flew back to the little girl and poured the water gently into her bucket. 

The little girl thanked the bird. She said, "You're so kind. I'm so happy you poured me some water!" 

The happy bird flew away, knowing he had made someone's day.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign on the grass. The sign says: "Do not walk here. New seeds."

"What are seeds?" Tom asks.

"Seeds are small things that grow into plants," Anna says.

"Can we see them?" Tom says.

They go closer to the sign. They see some thin brown lines on the grass. The lines are the seeds.

"Wow, they are so small!" Anna says.

"Can we touch them?" Tom says.

He reaches out his hand. Anna stops him.

"No, Tom, we can't touch them. The sign says so. If we touch them, we might spread them or break them. Then they won't grow," Anna says.

"Oh, I see. We don't want to do that. We want to see the plants grow," Tom says.

They nod and back away from the sign. They find another place to play. They are good friends. They listen to the sign. They wait for the seeds to grow.

Anna likes to bake with her mom. They make cookies and cakes and pies. Anna helps to mix and stir and pour. She likes to taste the dough and lick the spoon.

One day, mom says they will bake something new. She shows Anna a big bunch of grapes. Anna likes grapes. They are sweet and juicy and purple. Mom says they will make grape jam. Anna is curious.

Mom washes the grapes and puts them in a big pot. She adds some sugar and water and lemon. She turns on the stove and lets the grapes cook. They bubble and pop and smell good. Mom stirs the pot with a wooden spoon. She tells Anna to be careful. The pot is very hot.

When the grapes are soft and mushy, mom turns off the stove. She pours the grape jam into small jars. She puts lids on the jars and lets them cool. She says they will keep the jam in the fridge. They can use it for toast and sandwiches and pancakes.

Anna is happy. She helped mom bake grape jam. She thinks it is better than regular jam. She can't wait to try it. She gives mom a big hug and a kiss. Mom smiles and hugs her back. They love to bake together.

Tom and Ben are playing knights in the garden. They have sticks for swords and pots for helmets. They pretend to fight dragons and monsters.

"Roar! I am a big dragon and I will eat you!" Tom says, waving his stick.

"No, you are not! I am a brave knight and I will stop you!" Ben says, hitting Tom's stick with his own.

Their sticks make a loud noise when they clash. They laugh and run around the garden.

But then, Tom's stick breaks in half. He looks at it and feels sad.

"Oh no, my sword is broken! Now I can't play anymore!" he says.

Ben sees Tom's sad face and thinks of an idea. He runs to the shed and finds an old metal sword. It is very dull and rusty, but it looks like a real sword.

"Here, Tom, you can have this sword. It is better than a stick!" he says, giving Tom the sword.

Tom takes the sword and feels happy. He smiles and thanks Ben.

"Wow, this is a great sword! Thank you, Ben! You are a good friend!" he says.

They hug and then continue to play knights. They have more fun with the new sword. They forget about the broken stick and the dull metal. They only see their imagination.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She was very happy and she loved to march.

One day, Sue was marching around the garden when she saw a hill with a big top at the top. She wanted to climb to the top, so she started marching up the hill.

At first, it was easy, but as she got higher, it became harder. She slipped and slid, and every time she tried to march up, she kept slipping back down.

But she kept trying, and eventually she made it to the top. She was so happy she had reached it! But then she looked down and saw how high up she was and it made her feel a bit scared and hurt.

Luckily, Sue did not give up. She marched back down the hill, and when she reached the bottom, she was so proud of herself!

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a daddy that had a daughter. The daughter was very happy and excited because today was a special day. Today was the daughter's birthday! All morning long the daughter had been asking when the guests would arrive.

Finally the guests began to arrive and the daughter was so excited. The doorbell rang and the mommy opened the door. Standing there was Grandma. Grandma opened her arms wide and said, "Welcome, my darling daughter!"

Grandma handed the daughter a big, clear box. The daughter opened it and saw the beautiful present inside. She was so happy and excited that the teachers at her school had arranged a special birthday party for her. The daughter smiled and hugged her grandma, thanking her for the present.

The daddy watched the daughter with a big smile on his face. He looked at his wife and said, "That's the best present she could have gotten for her birthday. A lesson in welcoming someone with open arms." 

The mommy and daddy smiled at each other. They had taught their daughter a moral value by welcoming Grandma with open arms and sending her away with a loving hug. The daughter learned a valuable lesson; to always welcome people with clear and open arms.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved Wednesdays because that was the day her mom would make her favorite food for dinner. One Wednesday, Lily was playing with her toys when her mom called her for dinner. Lily was eager to eat her favorite food, spaghetti.

When Lily saw her plate, she replied, "Yum, this looks delicious!" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily." They both enjoyed their dinner and talked about their day. After dinner, Lily helped her mom clean the dishes.

Later that night, Lily was getting ready for bed when she remembered something. She asked her mom, "Can we go to the park tomorrow?" Her mom replied, "Of course, we can go to the park tomorrow. Goodnight, Lily." Lily went to bed with a smile on her face, excited for the fun day ahead.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing outside when she fell and got a big boo-boo on her knee. Her mommy took her inside and cleaned the boo-boo with a wet cloth. 

Lily was sad and cried a lot because it hurt so much. But then her mommy said, "Don't cry, sweetie. I will stitch your boo-boo and make it all better." 

Lily was grateful to her mommy for making her feel better. She gave her mommy a big hug and said, "Thank you, mommy. You make me feel all better." And from that day on, Lily knew that whenever she got a boo-boo, her mommy would always be there to make it all better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was scared of the dark chamber in his house. The chamber was big and had many things in it. One day, Tim's mom asked him to go into the chamber and attach a hook to the wall.

Tim said, "I am scared, Mom. Can you come with me?" His mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, I will be with you." They went into the chamber together. Tim saw that it was not so scary after all.

He found a hook and attached it to the wall. Tim felt brave now. He wasn't scared of the chamber anymore. From that day on, Tim and his mom would go into the chamber and play. Tim learned that there was nothing to be scared of when his mom was with him.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to hop. Bunny was very persistent. Every day, Bunny would hop around the house and play.

One day, Bunny saw a big refrigerator in the kitchen. Bunny thought it would be fun to hop on top of the refrigerator. So, Bunny hopped and hopped, trying to reach the top.

But the refrigerator was too tall for Bunny. Bunny tried and tried but could not hop high enough. Bunny became sad and tired. In the end, Bunny could not hop on top of the refrigerator and had to stop trying.

Once there was a little girl named Ellie. Ellie was three and very curious. She wanted to know everything.

One day, Ellie was playing with her toys when her mom asked her a question. Ellie squinted her eyes and looked up, wondering what the question was.

"Why is the sky blue?" Ellie's mom asked.

Ellie thought for a moment. She put her finger to her lips and asked, "Why?"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a good question! The sky is blue because it's reflecting the color of the ordinary ocean."

Ellie was so happy that she had asked the question. She smiled and said, "Yes! That's why!"

And from then on, Ellie always remembered to question everything.

Once upon a time, there was a comfortable goose. The goose loved to wander around in the big meadow and eat the tasty grass.

One day, something exciting happened. The goose was waddling around when it spotted a pond. The pond was full of sparkling blue water and even had a few lily pads on it too. The goose was so happy that it decided to take a dip.

The goose paddled around and around the pond, and it felt so good. Then, a little frog hopped up to the edge of the pond and spotted the goose. The frog was surprised to see the goose swimming in the pond because it had never seen a goose in the pond before.

The goose and the frog became friends and spent the whole day in the pond. The goose was so comfortable that it didn't want to leave and it spent many happy days playing with the frog in the pond.

The moral of the story is: making new friends can make you feel comfortable.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Abigail. She loved to explore her city, and often spent her days playing at the park. 

One day, Abigail stopped by the bakery and noticed a large cake on the counter. Its delicious smell made her mouth water. Abigail asked the baker, "Can I have a piece of that cake, please?"

The baker shook his head and said, "I'm sorry Abigail, but this cake is special. It's for a man with a mustache. He is coming today and he ordered it especially." 

Abigail was sad, but she didn't want to prevent the man with the mustache from enjoying his cake. But then, Abigail had an idea. She said, "Please, can I leave a note on the cake? Just a few words?"

The baker agreed, and Abigail wrote a note that said, "I hope this cake is as delicious as it looks!" She then thanked the baker and walked away. 

When the man with the mustache received his cake, he was surprised to find the note. He smiled and said, "This cake looks even tastier now!"

Ben and Lily like to play with blocks. They can build many things with blocks. They can build houses, towers, bridges and more. They have fun with blocks.

One day, they decide to build a big circle with blocks. They put blocks on the floor and make a round shape. They are happy with their circle. They sit inside the circle and pretend it is their fort.

But then, Tom comes along. Tom is older and bigger than Ben and Lily. He sees their circle and he wants to play too. He says, "Move over, I want to join your fort." He tries to push his way inside the circle.

Ben and Lily are scared and angry. They say, "No, Tom, this is our circle. We built it. You can't come in. Go away." They try to block Tom with their arms and legs.

Tom is mad and mean. He says, "Fine, if I can't join your circle, I will break it." He kicks and throws the blocks. He makes the circle fall apart. He laughs and runs away.

Ben and Lily are sad and hurt. They cry and hug each other. They look at their broken circle and their scattered blocks. They don't want to play anymore.

Then, Mom comes along. She sees what happened and she feels sorry for Ben and Lily. She says, "Oh, my poor babies, what did Tom do to you? He was very rude and naughty. He should not have broken your circle. I will talk to his mom later. Come here, let me hug you."

She hugs Ben and Lily and kisses their heads. She says, "Don't worry, you can build another circle. Or you can build something else. You have many blocks and you have each other. You are very smart and creative. You can make anything you want. And I will help you."

Molly decided to play chess every day, because it made her feel so good. And she always smiled as she bounced around.

Anna liked to play with her toys in the kitchen. She had a doll, a truck, a ball and a spoon. She pretended the spoon was a magic wand and the ball was a dragon. She waved the spoon and said, "I am a fairy and you are my friend, dragon. Let's go on an adventure!"

She took the ball and the spoon and ran to the sink. She saw a big hole in the sink. She thought it was a cave. She said, "Let's go inside, dragon. Maybe we will find treasure!" She put the ball in the hole and pushed it down. She heard a splash. She said, "Oh no, dragon! You fell in the water! I will save you!"

She reached her hand in the hole. She felt something hot. She screamed. She pulled her hand out. It hurt. It was red. She had touched the drain. The drain was hot. It burned her hand. She dropped the spoon. She cried.

Mom heard her cry. She ran to the kitchen. She saw Anna's hand. She said, "What happened, Anna? Why are you crying?" She took Anna's hand and put it under cold water. She said, "This will make it feel better. Did you touch something hot?"

Anna nodded. She said, "I touched the drain. I wanted to save my dragon. He fell in the water. He is in the hole. I am sad. I lost my dragon and my hand hurts."

Mom hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, Anna. The drain is very hot. You should not touch it. It can burn you. It is dangerous. I will get your dragon for you. He is not lost. He is just wet. You are brave and kind, but you have to be careful. I love you, Anna."

She took a plunger and pushed it in the hole. She pulled it out. The ball came out with it. She gave it to Anna. She said, "Here is your dragon. He is safe. He is happy to see you. You can play with him, but not in the sink. Let's go to your room and find a dry place for him. And let's put a band-aid on your hand. It will heal soon. Don't worry, Anna. You are okay."

Tim and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tim had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving and talking.

"Vroom, vroom, I'm a fast truck!" Tim said.

"Hello, I'm a pretty doll!" Lily said.

They were having fun, but then Tim saw something on the shelf. It was a red cap with a star on it. He wanted to wear it and pretend he was a superhero.

"Look, Lily, a cap!" Tim said. He ran to the shelf and reached for the cap.

"Wait, Tim, that's Dad's cap!" Lily said. "He said we can't touch it. It's special."

But Tim did not listen. He grabbed the cap and put it on his head. He felt a tingling in his body. He looked at Lily and saw that she was much bigger than him.

"Tim, what happened?" Lily asked. She was scared.

Tim was scared too. He felt very small. He looked at the cap and saw a button on it. It said "shrink". He had pressed it by accident.

"Help, Lily, I shrank!" Tim said. He tried to take off the cap, but it was too tight.

Lily ran to him and picked him up. She was careful not to hurt him. She looked at the cap and saw another button. It said "grow". She pressed it and hoped it would work.

Tim felt a tingling again. He grew back to his normal size. He was happy and relieved. He took off the cap and hugged Lily.

"Thank you, Lily, you saved me!" Tim said.

"You're welcome, Tim, but don't touch Dad's cap again!" Lily said.

They put the cap back on the shelf and went back to their toys. They decided to play something else. They learned their lesson.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play at the park. They like to go on the slide. The slide is big and fun.

One day, they go to the park with their moms. They run to the slide. But there is a boy on the slide. He is big and mean. He does not let Tom and Anna go on the slide. He says, "This is my slide. Go away!"

Tom and Anna are sad and scared. They look at their moms. Their moms are talking. They do not see the boy. Tom and Anna do not know what to do. They stare at the boy. The boy stares back. He smiles. He has a bad smile.

The boy says, "Do you want to go on the slide? I will let you go. But you have to do something for me. You have to give me your toys. All of them. Now!"

Tom and Anna do not want to give their toys. They love their toys. They have a ball, a doll, a car, and a book. They say, "No, we do not want to give our toys. They are ours. You are not nice. You are not fair."

The boy gets angry. He says, "Fine. Then you can not go on the slide. Ever. And I will take your toys anyway. Watch me!" He jumps off the slide. He runs to Tom and Anna. He grabs their toys. He pushes them. He laughs. He runs away.

Tom and Anna cry. They are hurt and sad. They lost their toys. They lost their slide. They look at their moms. Their moms are still talking. They do not see what happened. They do not help Tom and Anna. They are not reliable. Tom and Anna feel alone and betrayed. They wish they had a better friend. They wish they had a better mom. They wish they had a better day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly up high in the sky and sing songs. One day, she met a big mean cat named Scratch. Scratch wanted to catch Tweet and eat her up for dinner. Tweet was very scared and didn't know what to do.

Flying away from Scratch was very difficult for Tweet because she was so small. But she knew she had to try. As she tried to fly away, Scratch got closer and closer. Just when it seemed like Scratch was going to catch her, a kind dog named Rover came to her rescue. Rover barked at Scratch and scared him away.

Tweet was so happy to be safe and she wanted to thank Rover. She flew over to him and gave him a big kiss on the nose. From that day on, Tweet and Rover became the best of friends and went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly monster. Every day the monster liked to cover himself in a blanket and play. One day the monster decided to go on a big adventure. When he went outside he saw a big cross. He wanted to cross it so he started running. The monster was so excited when he reached the other side. He was so proud that he'd covered the cross and reached the other side. 

So the monster kept exploring and soon found some friendly birds. They were chirping and singing in the trees. The monster became very happy and he asked the birds to teach him how to sing. The birds were very friendly and taught the monster how to sing.

The monster was now so happy. He liked to sing and cover the cross. He became very good friends with the birds and they decided to sing and cover the cross every day.

The end.

One day, Molly and her Mommy went to the store. Molly was very excited to go, as she loves shopping. When they arrived, Mommy took Molly to the fabric section. There were lots of colors to choose from and Molly was having a hard time deciding which one to get.

Mommy said, "Let's buy some red, mild fabric with small stitches. It looks very cheap." Molly liked the red fabric so the two chose it and put it in the cart.

Next, they went to the craft section and looked for yarn. Molly picked some pink yarn and Mommy picked some yellow yarn. They chose some needles too. 

When they were almost done shopping, Mommy said that it was time to spend the fabric. She explained to Molly that she had to carefully use the needle and yarn to make small stitches. Molly watched Mommy as she stitched the fabric for a pretty quilt. When Molly saw the quilt, she was so happy. Now she could spend time cuddling with it whenever she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved helicopters, they were his favorite toy. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. While they were there, Timmy saw a big, tough dog. He pointed at the dog and said, "Woof woof!" 

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a helicopter flying in the sky. It was so cool! Timmy pointed at the helicopter and said, "Wow!" 

After playing for a while, Timmy and his mom went home. Timmy told his dad all about the helicopter he saw at the park. His dad said, "That sounds amazing, Timmy!" Timmy smiled and said, "Yeah, it was tough!"

Mia and Ben are friends. They like to play outside in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They are very playful and happy.

One day, it is cold and windy. Mia and Ben wear sweaters to keep warm. They go to the park as usual. But the wind is very strong. It blows the leaves and dust in their faces.

"Ouch!" Mia says. "The wind hurts my eyes!"

"Me too!" Ben says. "Let's go to the bench and wipe our eyes."

They run to the bench and sit down. Mia takes out a tissue from her pocket and wipes her eyes. Ben does the same.

"Are you okay?" Mia asks Ben.

"Yes, I'm okay. Are you okay?" Ben asks Mia.

"Yes, I'm okay. But I don't like the wind. It is not fun." Mia says.

"Me neither. It is not fun. It is mean." Ben says.

They look at each other and hug. They are still friends. They are still happy.

"Let's go home and play inside. We can play with our toys and read books. That is fun." Mia says.

"Okay, let's go home and play inside. That is fun." Ben says.

They get up and hold hands. They walk home with their sweaters. They are still playful and happy.

Once upon a time there was a little kitty cat. He wanted to go see the world, so he started to roll away. As he rolled down the lane, he passed lots of houses and farms. Eventually, he saw a pretty little house with his family inside!

The kitty cat was so happy to be near his home. He rolled faster and faster until he was at his front door. He was so lucky to have such a nice house and family to welcome him home!

The kitty cat rolled all around his house. He rolled in the garden and he rolled around the house. He rolled and rolled and rolled until he was so tired he couldn't roll anymore. He found a nice spot at the end of the day, curled up and went to sleep.

Tommy was a big boy. He loved to play all day. But sometimes, he got very tired and he had to take a nap. He would put his head on a big, soft pillow, close his eyes and go to sleep.

One day, Tommy was so tired that he decided to take a nap in his favorite spotâ€”under the big, green tree in the backyard. The sun was shining and it was very nice and quiet.

But then, he heard something very strange. It sounded like a buzzing noise. He opened his eyes and saw a big, black buzzing file zooming around the tree. It was very surprising!

Tommy watched the file as it zoomed around the tree, curious as to why it was buzzing so loud. But soon, he got very sleepy again, and he decided to take another nap. As he drifted off to sleep, he heard the buzzing sound of the big, black file in the distance.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Ben had a truck. They liked to imagine different things with their toys.

"Let's pretend we are going to the park," Lily said. "You can drive your truck and I can bring my doll."

"Okay," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. There are many cars on the road."

They made noises with their mouths as they moved their toys along the carpet. They pretended to stop at red lights and honk at other drivers.

Suddenly, they heard a loud crash from the kitchen. They ran to see what happened. They saw their dad holding a broken plate and looking very foolish.

"What did you do, dad?" Lily asked.

"I was trying to get a cookie from the jar, but I dropped the plate," dad said. "I'm sorry, I made a mess."

Lily and Ben giggled. They thought dad was silly.

"Can we have a cookie too, dad?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but only one each," dad said. "And then we have to clean up this mess."

Lily and Ben took a cookie and went back to the living room. They continued to play with their toys and imagine fun adventures. They were happy.

Tim and Mia like to play with their bikes in the park. They ride fast and have fun. But one day, Tim's bike breaks. The wheel comes off and Tim falls to the ground. He hurts his knee and cries.

Mia stops her bike and runs to Tim. She sees his bike and his knee. She says, "Oh no, Tim, your bike is broken and your knee is bleeding. This is serious. We need to fix it."

Tim says, "How can we fix it? We don't have tools or bandages. And it hurts a lot."

Mia thinks for a moment. She says, "I have an idea. We can use this stick to hold the wheel in place. And we can use this leaf to cover your knee. It will help stop the bleeding and make it feel better."

She finds a stick and a leaf and helps Tim fix his bike and his knee. Tim says, "Thank you, Mia. You are very smart and kind. You are my best friend."

Mia says, "You're welcome, Tim. You are my best friend too. Now let's go back home and show our parents. They will be proud of us and give us hugs and cookies."

They get on their bikes and ride back home. They are happy and proud. They fixed their problem and helped each other. They learned a lesson: when something is serious, they can fix it together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her stuffed animals. One day, she found a great ball of wool on the floor. She picked it up and examined it closely. 

Lily: "Look, Mr. Bear! I found a big ball of wool. It's so soft and fluffy!"

Mr. Bear: "Wow, that's great! What are you going to do with it?"

Lily: "I think I'll make a scarf for you. It will keep you warm and cozy."

Mr. Bear: "Thank you, Lily. You're so kind and clever."

Lily smiled and began to knit a scarf with the wool. She worked hard and soon the scarf was finished. Mr. Bear tried it on and it was just perfect. They hugged each other tightly and felt very happy. From that day on, they always kept each other warm with the great scarf made of wool.

One day, Mary and her father were walking in the garden. Mary saw a large rose bush and asked her father, "What is this?". Her father replied, "This is a rose bush. They have beautiful roses". Mary was eager and asked her father, "Can I pick one?". Her father said, "Yes, but remember to be honest and yield only one rose". 

Mary carefully walked over to the rose bush and looked at all of the different colored roses. She decided on a beautiful pink rose, and pierced the stem with her teacher. As she held the rose in her palm, she felt an excited joy. She took it to her father and said, "Look what I yield!" 

Her father smiled and said, "You have done a very honest action". They walked back inside with the rose in hand, and Mary knew that the rose was meant to be hers.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks. They have many blocks of different colors and shapes. They can use the blocks to make houses, towers, cars, and animals.

One day, they want to make a big bridge with the blocks. They use the long blocks and the wide blocks to make the bridge. They are excited to see how high and long they can make it. They work together and have fun.

But then, Tom comes to play. Tom is not nice. He likes to break things. He sees the bridge and he wants to break it. He runs to the bridge and pushes it with his hands. The blocks fall down and make a loud noise. Ben and Mia are sad and angry. They worked hard to make the bridge.

They shout at Tom and tell him to go away. Tom does not listen. He laughs and tries to break more blocks. Ben and Mia do not want to play with him. They want to make the bridge again.

They have an idea. They use the wide blocks to make a wall around the bridge. They make the wall very high and strong. They use the long blocks to make a door in the wall. They can go in and out of the door, but Tom cannot. They are happy and proud of their wall and their bridge. They are excited to play with them.

Tom sees the wall and the door. He is curious and jealous. He wants to see the bridge and break it. He tries to climb the wall, but he cannot. He tries to open the door, but he cannot. He is frustrated and bored. He does not have any blocks to play with.

He realizes that he was mean and rude. He feels sorry and lonely. He wants to be friends with Ben and Mia. He knocks on the door and says sorry. He asks if he can play with them. Ben and Mia hear him and think about it. They decide to give him a chance. They open the door and let him in. They show him the bridge and teach him how to use the blocks. They share and help each other. They have fun together. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She had a pet dog named Max who loved to play all day long. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. They saw another dog playing with his owner.

Lily said, "Max, let's play with them!"

Max barked happily and ran towards the other dog. But the owner of the other dog said, "Sorry, my dog doesn't like to play with other dogs."

Lily was sad and said, "But we came here to play. Can't you plan to let your dog play with us?"

The owner thought for a moment and said, "Okay, let's give it a try."

And so, Max and the other dog played together while Lily and the owner watched. They all had a great time and became friends. From that day on, they planned to meet up in the park every week to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and compassionate little girl named Molly. She had a big arm which she used to to sort out all sorts of things around the house. One day, Molly was walking around when she heard a little puppy crying. The puppy had gotten stuck in between some branches and couldn't get out. Molly gently and compassionately reached out her arm and tried to sort out the problem.

Molly: "There, there, little one. I'll try to help you get out."

But no matter how hard Molly tried, she just couldn't free the puppy from the branches. She tried and tried, but her arm just wasn't strong enough. Molly's heart was breaking and she started to cry.

Molly: "I'm so sorry, little one. I just don't know what to do."

Finally, the little puppy had to remain stuck in the branches for the night. Molly left crying, but she never forgot the puppy. She was so compassionate and felt so helpless. 

The next morning, the puppy was found by a kind-hearted stranger who was able to sort out the problem with his strong arms. Sadly, it was too late for the poor puppy.

Molly's heart learned a valuable lesson that day, that not all problems can be sorted out with a compassionate arm.

Once upon a time, two socks were living far apart. Every day they dreamed of being together. One day, they found a way to unite.

The two socks hopped, skipped and jumped over the hill. But it was very long. Then, they decided to try an unusual way to get closer together.

They started rolling! One after the other, they rolled down the hill, faster and faster until they crashed into each other. It felt so good to be close at last.

The two socks laughed and hugged and never wanted to be apart again. They have been united ever since - and never have to be apart ever again!

Tom likes to mail letters to his grandma. He draws pictures of his toys, his dog and his friends. He puts them in envelopes and sticks stamps on them. He asks his mom to help him write his name and grandma's address. Then he walks with his mom to the big blue box and puts his letters inside. He is happy to mail letters to his grandma.

One day, Tom sees a big fire on TV. He sees houses and trees burning. He sees smoke and ash in the air. He feels scared and sad. He wonders if grandma is okay. He asks his mom if grandma's house is on fire. His mom says no, grandma lives far away from the fire. She says grandma is safe and she will call her later. Tom feels a little better.

Tom decides to make a special letter for grandma. He finds some gray paper and cuts out a circle. He glues some black yarn on it. He makes a face with eyes, a nose and a mouth. He says it is a picture of ash. He thinks grandma will like it. He puts it in an envelope and writes "ash" on it. He asks his mom to mail it for him. His mom smiles and says it is a very creative letter. She says it is easy to mail it. She takes Tom to the big blue box and they mail the letter together. Tom hopes grandma will get it soon. He hopes she will smile and laugh. He loves his grandma.

One day, a little girl was playing in Mama and Papa's garden. She was carrying a basket full of green apples. Suddenly, it started to rain. She looked up at the grey roof and the rain was falling hard. She was hungry, so she quickly ran with her basket to the house.

Mama was in the kitchen, and saw the little girl looking wet and cold. Mama opened a big umbrella and carried the girl, with her basket, into the house. She gave her a warm hug and some hot peanut butter sandwich. The little girl was happy and ate it all.

The rain kept raining, so Mama and the little girl looked at the roof. Papa was outside the house and had hung a rope over the roof. He then tied the rope to the handle of the big umbrella. There was no more rain getting inside the house!

Mama thanked Papa and carried the little girl back to her bed. She hugged and kissed her goodnight, and the little girl went to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved playing soccer with his friends at the park. One day, Timmy's team was losing the game. They needed to score a goal to win.

Timmy's friend, Johnny, kicked the ball towards the goal. But he was careless and missed the shot. Timmy said, "Don't worry, Johnny. We can still win if we try harder."

Suddenly, Timmy got the ball and ran towards the goal. He kicked the ball so hard that it went into the net. "We did it! We won!" Timmy shouted with victory. His team was so happy that they sacked him with hugs and high-fives.

Once upon a time, in a faraway country, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play all day long. One day, he found a big, disgusting bug in his room. Tim was scared and did not know what to do.

Tim ran to his mom and said, "Mom, there is a disgusting bug in my room! I don't want to sleep there tonight." His mom looked at him and said, "Don't worry, Tim. We will take care of the bug."

Tim and his mom went to his room to find the bug. They saw it on the wall. Tim's mom got a paper and gently took the bug away. She put it outside, so it could go back to its home.

That night, Tim was still scared to sleep in his room. His mom said, "The bug is gone now, Tim. It's safe to sleep." Tim trusted his mom, so he went to his room and fell asleep.

From that day on, Tim was not scared of disgusting bugs anymore. He learned that they just needed to be put back outside, where they belong. Tim and his mom lived happily ever after in their country home.

Once upon a time, there was a fierce rope. It thought it was more powerful than anything else. One day, it met a frog and said, "You are weak and little. I can split you in two with no problem!"
"No, you can't," replied the frog. "You can't even move, so how do you think you can split me?"
The rope was so angry that it started to shake and it split in two. A gust of wind blew and carried each piece away.
The frog was sad, but it learned an important lesson. Even though you may be tough and proud, you should never be too mean and boastful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved the ocean. Every day, she would go and stand on the beach and gaze out to the sea. One day, the girl's mommy said "Come on, let's go and play near the ocean!" So the little girl and her mommy went to the beach and the little girl was so happy.

The sun was shining and it was a lovely day. When they got to the beach, the little girl saw a beautiful boat sailing far away. "Oh, look!" She said to her mommy. "It's so beautiful!" Her mommy explained that the boat belonged to a special man who loves the ocean too.

The little girl looked around, and she noticed that the ocean had woken up. She saw the waves gently move and the birds that sing in the morning sky. She felt so happy and peaceful.

At last, she understood why the man loved the ocean. He could see the beauty and joy that it can bring. She then told her mommy, "I'm going to love the ocean too!"

This story shows that if we take time to appreciate the world around us, it can bring us feelings of peace and joy. The ocean is a lovely thing and we should treasure it always.

Once upon a time there was a frog. He was a thoughtful frog who liked to sit in the sun every day. One day, he hopped over to the pond. He wanted to take a cool dip in the water. He made sure to shut the pond door behind him so no animals would come and bother him.

He hopped onto a rock and relaxed. He shut his eyes and enjoyed the sun on his back. Then he heard a noise. It sounded like something hopping around. He opened his eyes and saw a butterfly!

The frog thought it was very thoughtful of the butterfly to come and visit him. So, he hopped around and showed the butterfly around the pond. They played all day and when the sun set, the frog said goodbye to the butterfly and shut the pond door again. 

The frog was very happy. He hopped all the way back home, feeling very thoughtful and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her dolls and her favorite doll was named Molly. One day, Lily decided to take Molly on an adventure to the park.

As they were walking, Lily saw a beautiful purple flower and she wanted to pick it. "Molly, look at this beautiful flower! Let's pick it and bring it home," said Lily excitedly.

But then, a bee flew out of the flower and Lily got scared. "Oh no, Molly! Let's go to the playground instead," said Lily. They entered the playground and had so much fun going down the slide and swinging on the swings.

After playing for a while, Lily and Molly went back home. Lily put the purple flower in a vase and it looked so beautiful in her room. "Molly, we had so much fun today! Let's go on another adventure tomorrow," said Lily before going to bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Grace. Grace was three years old. One day, she went to the forest with her mom. As they were walking, Grace spotted a deer. She ran up to the deer and wanted to give it a big hug.

"No, Grace," her mom said. "That deer is dirty, so you mustn't hug it."

Grace was sad. She wanted to give the deer a hug so badly. Just as she was about to do it, the deer ran away.

Grace cried and ran after the deer. But it was too late. The deer was gone. 

Grace was very sad. She wanted so badly to give the deer a hug. She never saw the deer again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who lived next to a big, tall wall. Every morning the mom would insist that her two children, Peter and Penny, stand up straight against the wall. But the two little ones were too dizzy to do it! They kept spinning and laughing, holding hands, and wouldn't stay in one spot.

"Come on you two!" said the mom, "stand still and hold your hands against the wall!" But the two kids just kept giggling and spinning around, unable to stand still.

"Please," the mom said again, trying to sound very grown-up, "insist on standing still! I'm counting to three, okay?"

Peter and Penny looked at each other, then nodded and took turns standing up against the wall. They held hands, and with the mom's encouragement, finally managed to hold the wall without spinning around and feeling so dizzy.

The mom smiled, pleased that her two children had finally managed to listen to her. From then on, every morning, without being asked, the two kids happily lined up against the wall, standing straight and still until their mom told them it was okay to move.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play games with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends played a game of tag. Timmy wanted to win the game so badly, but his friends were very fast.

After the game, Timmy went home for dinner. His mom made his favorite food, spaghetti. But when Timmy saw his plate, he noticed that his spaghetti was covered in a black sauce. Timmy didn't like the black sauce, so he refused to eat his dinner.

His mom said, "Timmy, you need to eat your dinner. You can't just refuse to eat it because it's black. It still tastes good." But Timmy didn't want to listen. He just wanted his regular spaghetti. 

Timmy's mom got upset because Timmy was being stubborn. She said, "Timmy, you need to eat your dinner. If you don't, you won't get dessert." Timmy finally gave in and ate his dinner. He realized that the black sauce wasn't so bad after all. And because he ate his dinner, he won a piece of chocolate cake for dessert.

Once upon a time, there was a big puddle. It was enormous! A little boy named Timmy saw the puddle and wanted to jump in it. But he was wearing his new shoes and didn't want to get them wet. So, he took a blanket and covered the puddle. 

Suddenly, a little girl named Sally came along. She wanted to jump in the puddle too. But when she saw the blanket, she thought the puddle was gone. Timmy showed her the covered puddle and they both laughed. 

Then, Timmy uncovered the puddle and they both jumped in it. They splashed and played until they were all wet. But they didn't care because they had so much fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a clever farmer who had a big farm. He worked hard every day to grow crops and take care of his animals. He loved his farm very much.

One day, a big storm came and destroyed all of the farmer's crops. He was very sad and didn't know what to do. He tried to plant new crops, but they didn't grow well.

The farmer realized he had to yield to the storm and start over. But it was too late. He didn't have enough food to feed his animals and they all became very sick. The farmer was very sad and had to sell his farm. He never forgot the lesson he learned about yielding to nature.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy loved to play outside with her hoop. She would roll the hoop and run after it, laughing all the time.

One sunny day, Amy was playing with her hoop when she saw a hungry cat. The cat was very thin and looked sad. Amy wanted to help the cat, so she went to her house to get some food for the cat.

Amy's mom gave her a bowl of food to give to the hungry cat. The cat was very happy and ate all the food. After the cat was full, it played with Amy and her hoop. They had a lot of fun together. From that day on, Amy and the cat were the best of friends.

Ben and Jen were twins who lived on a farm. They liked to play with the animals, but their favorite was Billy the goat. Billy was friendly and funny, and he liked to eat grass and carrots. Sometimes, he would let the twins ride on his back or pull them in a cart.

One day, Ben and Jen's mom told them that they had to go to the city with their dad for a week. They had to visit their grandma, who was sick. The twins were sad, because they would miss Billy and the other animals. They hugged Billy and said goodbye.

"Be good, Billy," Ben said. "We will come back soon."

"Don't worry, Billy," Jen said. "We will bring you a present."

Billy nodded and bleated. He watched them leave in the car.

While the twins were gone, Billy was lonely. He missed his friends, and he had no one to play with. He became bored and angry. He started to chew on the fence, the clothesline, and the flowers. He knocked over the buckets, the barrels, and the chairs. He made a big mess on the farm.

The farmer, who was Ben and Jen's uncle, was not happy. He scolded Billy and tied him to a tree. He said Billy was a bad goat, and he would not let him out until he learned to behave.

Billy felt sorry and sad. He realized he had been naughty, and he wished he could say sorry to the farmer. He wished Ben and Jen would come back soon.

After a week, Ben and Jen returned from the city. They had a lot of fun with their grandma, who was feeling better. They brought her a card, a cake, and some flowers. They also brought Billy a present: a new collar with a bell.

They ran to the farm, looking for Billy. They saw him tied to the tree, looking sad and dirty. They felt sorry for him, and they ran to hug him.

"Billy, we missed you so much!" Ben said.

"Billy, we are sorry you were alone!" Jen said.

They untied him and gave him his present. Billy was happy to see them, and he licked their faces. He bleated and shook his head, making the bell ring.

The farmer came out and saw them. He smiled and said he was glad they were back. He said he was sorry he had been harsh with Billy, but he hoped he had learned his lesson.

Billy nodded and bleated. He had learned his lesson. He was sorry he had been angry and made a mess. He decided he would be good and not chew on things he shouldn't.

Ben and Jen thanked the farmer and said they loved him. They said they loved Billy too, and they wanted to play with him. They asked the farmer if they could take Billy for a ride in the cart.

The farmer agreed and said they could. He said he was proud of them and Billy. He said they were a good family.

Ben, Jen, and Billy were happy. They rode in the cart, laughing and singing. They learned that being away from someone you love can make you miss them, but also make you appreciate them more. They learned that being angry can make you do bad things, but also make you sorry and want to do better. They learned that being good can make you happy, and also make others happy. They learned that love is the best present of all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to school and learning new things. One day, Timmy's teacher gave him an exam to take. Timmy was nervous because he had never taken an exam before.

After the exam was over, Timmy's teacher asked him how he did. "I don't know," said Timmy. "I have to wait for you to examine it." Timmy's teacher smiled and told him that he did a great job.

Later that day, Timmy went to his friend's house to play. His friend had a modern toy that Timmy had never seen before. "Wow, that's really cool!" said Timmy as he examined the toy. "It's so modern!" His friend smiled and let Timmy play with it for a while.

When it was time to go home, Timmy's mom asked him how his day was. "I took an exam today," said Timmy. "And I saw a really modern toy at my friend's house!" Timmy's mom smiled and told him how proud she was of him for doing well on his exam.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Tim and Jane. They were playing outside when Tim saw something on the roof. He said to Jane, "Look, a bird on the roof. I bet I can catch it!"

Jane was worried. "That looks bad. Too high," she said. But Tim didn't listen and started to climb up the roof.

He managed to get to the top but the bird flew away. He was almost back on the ground when he slipped. Poor Tim was stuck on the roof.

Jane knew she had to help. She started to look for something that could help Tim get down. She saw a ladder leaning against the wall of the house. She knew this would manage.

Jane grabbed the ladder and she and Tim managed to get off the roof. They both were really happy and they never tried to catch birds on roofs again.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He wanted to help his mom, so he decided to lend a hand in the kitchen. He grabbed a lemon from the top shelf and started to squeeze it. 

Unfortunately, the lemon was too sour, and it made Jack's eyes sting! He was embarrassed, but he had to laugh at how silly he felt. His mom came in and started to laugh too. 

Jack was not embarrassed anymore and he thanked his mom for lending him a helping hand. She smiled and gave him a hug. 

Since then, Jack has been careful when lending a hand in the kitchen!

Once upon a time, there was a baby duck named Steve who lived in a lake. Steve liked to dive under the lake's water every day. One day he wanted to explore somewhere new, so he decided to dive deeper than ever before.

As he dove down, Steve noticed a strange black liquid covering the ground. He looked closely and realized it was ink! Steve was confused. He had never seen this before.

Steve tried to figure out why the ink was there, but he couldn't understand it. He then started to feel scared and wanted to go back. Before he could though, an eel suddenly came out of the ink!

Steve was so scared he quickly dove away and back up to the safety of the lake's surface. He was relieved but very confused as to what he just saw.

Steve went back to the lake everyday but decided to never dive that deep again.

Sammy was so lively. He loved to pass the days in his backyard. Every morning he would wake up early and spend his time playing in the grass. Today was no different, yet even more fun!

Sammy's mom handed him a big ball. "Let's play," she said. Sammy smiled and passed the ball back and forth to his mom. They laughed and laughed as the ball flew through the air.

After a while, Sammy's mom suggested they play a game. They chose a game about passing the ball through a hoop. Sammy was a natural. He passed the ball through the hoop every time!

The game went on and on, until Sammy and his mom were both tired. But they both had lots of fun and Sammy felt especially lively after the game. They gave each other a high-five and Sammy ran back inside. He couldn't wait to play the game again.

Once upon a time there was a small boy named Timmy who was always brave. He didn't ever want to be sad or scared.

One day his mother gave him a mask. It was big and round, and had a big smile painted on it. Timmy felt so brave wearing it that he wanted to dare himself to something. He wanted to do something he'd never done before.

So Timmy decided to go to a dark and scary cave by himself. The cave was very deep, and as soon as he went in he felt a bit miserable. But he remembered his mask and felt brave again. He sang a silly song and kept on walking until he'd gone through the entire cave.

At the end, he was so proud of himself he wanted to tell the world. He ran out of the cave, shouting and cheering. He felt so good he had to keep reminding himself that he'd dared himself to do something brave.

No matter how big or small the dare, everyone should remember to be brave and never feel miserable.

Danny looked out the window and saw the sun in the sky. He gazed at its bright yellow light. He wanted to go outside, so he ran to his mom. She said it was time for lunch.

Danny went to the kitchen where his mom was cooking. He saw a big stove with pots and pans on it. His mom was making something healthy for lunch. He watched as she moved the pots around the stove.

After lunch, Danny asked if he could go outside. His mom said yes and Danny ran to put on his shoes. His mom said he should stay in the backyard and he promised he would.

Danny exited the kitchen and opened the back door. He stepped out into the warm sun and took a deep breath. He smelled grass and flowers and smiled. He looked around and took it all in. It was so peaceful.

Then he gazed up at the sun with happy eyes and experienced the beautiful outdoors. He felt so healthy and alive. He looked forward to many more days of sunshine and exploration.

Lily was a very intelligent girl. One day she wanted to go to the park. She asked her mom if she could go.

"Not now, Lily," her mom said. "It's too late in the day. You'll have to wait until tomorrow when it's light outside."

Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right. She had to wait. The next morning, she woke up early and asked her mom if she could go to the park.

"Yes, you can go," her mom said.

Lily was so excited. She ran to the park and played for hours. She ran around the trees, played on the swings, and hugged her friends. She had so much fun! 

When it was time to go, Lily was so sad to leave. She wanted to stay at the park forever. But she was a very intelligent girl, and she knew it was time to come back home.

George is a three-year-old boy. He walks into his living room and sees a big, orange computer.

He runs over and gives it a big hug. Then he reaches his hands up high and stretches as far as he can. He loves to stretch!

Next, George turns the computer on. All sorts of happy colors and sounds fill the room. He sits down in front of the computer and starts to play.

He presses the keys and moves the mouse. He makes the computer do for him all kinds of funny things. It really is a lot of fun!

Suddenly, he has to stretch again. He stands up and reaches his hands up high. George loves to stretch and play with the computer.

Lily liked to dance. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the kitchen. She danced when she was happy, when she was sad, and when she was bored. She danced with her toys, with her dog, and with her mom.

One day, Lily wanted to dance with her dad. He was busy in his office, working on his computer. Lily knocked on the door and asked, "Dad, can you dance with me?"

"Not now, Lily," he said. "I have a lot of work to do. Maybe later."

Lily felt sad. She went to the kitchen and saw a bunch of celery on the counter. She had an idea. She took the celery and made a crown with it. She put it on her head and said, "I am the celery queen. I can dance with anyone I want."

She went back to her dad's office and opened the door. She said, "Dad, look at me. I am the celery queen. Dance with me now."

Her dad was angry. He had a big red face. He said, "Lily, go away. You are bothering me. You are making a mess with the celery. You are not a queen. You are a naughty girl."

He grabbed the celery crown from her head and threw it in the trash. He slammed the door and locked it.

Lily was shocked. She felt hurt. She felt anxious. She ran to her room and cried. She did not want to dance anymore. She did not want to be the celery queen. She did not want to be a naughty girl. She just wanted to be loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little kid called Sammy. Sammy was only three years old and he was very excited to explore the world. 
One day, Sammy was playing outside with his friends when he noticed something shining on the ground. He went to take a closer look and he saw that it was a bottle of ink. Sammy was very intrigued and he wanted to take the bottle with him, so he did.

Sammy took the bottle of ink home with him. He asked his mom if he could play with the ink and she said it was okay, so Sammy got to work. He drew lots of pictures with the ink and was so happy with the end result. 

But then, it was getting late and his mom told him it was time to go to bed. Sammy sadly put away the ink and went to bed. The next morning, Sammy asked his mom if he could take the ink with him again, and she said yes! Sammy was so happy and he ran off to play with the ink again. 

This time, Sammy was extra careful and he was able to use the ink in an easy way. He drew lots of lovely pictures and had lots of fun. At the end of the day, Sammy had to return the ink to its rightful place in the garden. He bid the ink goodbye and went home. Sammy was very happy to have been able to play with the ink and was looking forward to the next time

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl. She was so excited for a very special day. She wanted to pick potatoes in the garden.

She picked up her big basket and went out to the garden. She looked around until she found the patch of potatoes. She started to pull the potatoes up and put them in the basket.

She was so excited by the potatoes that she could hardly contain her happiness. She was jumping around and shouting with joy. When she was done picking the potatoes, she was so proud of all the potatoes she had collected.

As the sun began to set, she went back indoors with her basket of potatoes. She couldn't wait to enjoy the potatoes. 

The next day, she cooked up the potatoes and was so excited to have the delicious meal. She enjoyed every bite!

She never forgot the special day when she went out to pick potatoes in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful bird. The bird loved to sing. When the bird sang, it made beautiful music.

One day, the bird saw a colorful flower. The flower was red, blue, and yellow. The bird thought it was pretty. The bird wanted to match the flower's colors.

The bird sang its best music. As it sang, its feathers changed colors. Now the bird was red, blue, and yellow too. The bird and the flower matched. They were both very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing with her toys when she suddenly needed to go to the toilet. She said to her mommy, "Mommy, I need to go potty." 

Mommy took Lily to the toilet and helped her sit down. The toilet was very noisy and Lily covered her ears. "It's okay, Lily," said mommy. "It will be over soon." 

After Lily finished, she washed her hands and went back to playing with her toys. Her brother, Tommy, came into the room and asked to play with her. "Sure, Tommy," said Lily. "Let's pass the ball back and forth." 

They played together for a while, passing the ball and laughing. Lily was happy that she got to go to the toilet and now she could play with her brother. The end.

Once upon a time in a far away land there was a slept a tiny flower. Every night, the flower slept in the underground and dreamed of one day blooming.

One day, the flower's dream came true and it opened its petals to the light of the sun. Its colours shone bright and soon many of its friends started to bloom.

The flowers underground were protected and safe. All the other plants and creatures in the world were so happy they cheered and sang.

The flowers were now forever safe from the winds above ground, and they could bloom every day. The sun shone down on their petals and the underground buzzed with their beauty.

The little flower was so happy and the others flowers were so proud! Together, they sang and danced in the underground, forever blooming in their safe and magical home.

Molly was a little girl who loved to climb. She always wanted to try and get to the top of things. One day, Molly was wearing her favourite pink blouse and decided to climb a tree. 

Molly put her foot on a branch and started to climb. She found it harder than she thought it would be and started to get tired. But Molly kept climbing higher and higher.

Suddenly, Molly started slipping and her blouse got caught on a branch. She couldn't move!

Molly started to feel embarrassed and called out to her mum. 

"Mum, I'm stuck!" Molly said.

Mummy rushed to help Molly and after a few minutes she was able to free her from the branch and blouse.

Molly remembered to be more careful next time and promised herself to not climb so high again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat cereal from his favorite bowl every morning. One day, his mom gave him a new bowl. It was an unusual bowl with bright colors and funny shapes.

Timmy didn't like the new bowl. He said, "Mommy, I disagree. I want my old bowl back."

Mommy said, "But Timmy, your old bowl is broken. This new bowl is special. It will make your cereal taste even better."
