Timmy didn't believe her, but he gave the new bowl a try. To his surprise, the cereal did taste better! From that day on, Timmy loved his unusual bowl and never disagreed with his mom again.

Once upon a time, there was a smart girl who liked to play in the garden with her number. Every day, she would go out and use her spade to dig and do wonderful things in the garden.

One day, the girl had an idea. She used her number and her spade to dig and prepare a special bed for a surprise. She worked hard and carefully, and after her hard work was done, she was pleased.

The next day, the girl was excited when she went outside, for she knew something special was going to happen. She was right! The girl looked in the special bed and saw that it had grown two bright red flowers! She was so pleased with her work and smiled happily. She knew that it was her hard work and her smart number that had made the special bed where the flower grew.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun and listen to the birds sing. One day, her mom asked her to clean her room. Lily didn't want to do it because she wanted to play outside. But her mom said she had to do it because it was important to keep the room clean from dust.

Lily started to clean her room, but she didn't want her mom to help her. She wanted to be independent and do it all by herself. She listened to her mom's advice and started to clean the dust from her toys and shelves. It was hard work, but she did it all by herself.

When Lily was finished, she felt proud of herself for being independent and listening to her mom. Her room was clean and she could go outside to play again. She listened to the birds sing and felt happy that she did a good job. From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to listen to her mom and keep her room clean from dust.

One day, a tall boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They wanted to buy some cereal for breakfast. Tim's mom said, "Tim, can you help me carry the cereal?"

Tim was happy to help his mom. He picked up the cereal box and carried it in his arms. "I can do it, Mom!" he said with a big smile. They walked to the counter and paid for the cereal.

When they got home, Tim and his mom sat down to eat the cereal. They both enjoyed their breakfast together. Tim felt proud that he could help his mom and carry the cereal all by himself.

Once upon a time there was an old man who loved to keep things. He kept everything he ever owned; old cars, old furniture and, most importantly, his old television.

One day the old man went to visit his granddaughter who had just turned three years old.

"Grandfather, what is this?" asked the little girl pointing at the old television.

"Why it's an old television, my dear." replied the old man. "I like to keep this with me."

The little girl's eyes lit up. "Can I keep it too?" she asked.

The old man smiled. "Yes, you can keep it, my sweet," he said. "It's a special present for my special granddaughter." 

The little girl was very happy and hugged her grandfather tightly. She knew that her old television would be something she would keep with her always.

Ralph was walking through the forest when he heard a high-pitched cry for help. He quickly ran towards the sound and saw a friendly, yellow bird stuck in a tree. The poor bird was trying to rescue its golden egg which had been stuck between two branches.

Ralph wanted to help the bird, so he ran over and tried to rescue the golden egg. He reached up and managed to grab it, but just as he pulled it free, the egg slipped out of his hands. Ralph gasped as the egg smashed against the ground.

The friendly bird flew down and stared sadly at the broken shell. Tears filled its eyes and it shook its head slowly. Ralph felt terrible and hugged the bird tightly as it cried.

The bird said goodbye and flew away, still carrying the broken egg in its beak. Ralph watched sadly as the friendly bird became a tiny dot on the horizon. He had tried to rescue the egg, but it had ended in disaster.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom loved to eat fruits and vegetables because they were healthy. He would often ask his mom to put a lot of them in his bowl.

One day, Tom's mom gave him a bowl of fruit salad. Tom was very happy and started to eat it. He counted the number of grapes in his bowl and found out there were ten!

Tom finished his bowl quickly because he loved the healthy fruits in it. He asked his mom to make him another bowl, but this time with more fruits. His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Tom!"

Once upon a time, there was a big red ball and a small blue ball. They were best friends and always played together. One day, they saw a drain and wanted to see who could roll down it first. The big red ball went first, and the small blue ball was envious because it wanted to go first too.

Then, it was the small blue ball's turn to roll down the drain. But it got stuck! The big red ball was sad and wanted to help its friend. So, the big red ball rolled back up and pushed the small blue ball out of the drain. They were so happy to be together again.

From that day on, they promised to never separate and always play together. The big red ball and the small blue ball became even better friends, and they never felt envious of each other again. They played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a flower who wanted to grow. The flower was yellow and it was so happy to be in the sunshine. But one day, there was a storm and the sky filled with lightning. The flower was scared, but soon the lightning stopped, and the sky was bright again. A rainbow appeared in the sky and the yellow flower was so happy! It started to grow big and strong, until it was ready to bloom. And it bloomed the most beautiful yellow flower that the world had ever seen!

Once upon a time, there was a prince who was very fast. One day, the prince was walking in the woods, when he heard a sound that made him freeze. It was the sound of a gun being shot. The prince was scared and he ran away as fast as he could. 

But it was too late, the prince had been shot and he was badly hurt. He fell to the ground and he couldn't get up. The prince had to stay on the ground until help came. But help never did come and the prince stayed there for days and days. Finally, the prince died because he wasn't able to get the help he needed. 

The end.

Once there was a child who was very dizzy. She felt like she wasn't getting enough oxygen, so she started to feel tired.

One day, she met a friend and they went to play together. The child got very excited and started to jump around. That made her feel even more dizzy!

Her friend saw her struggling and tried to help. The friend gave her some oxygen, which helped her feel better. She was so relieved that she hugged her friend.

But then the friend did something unexpected. He smacked her! She was so surprised that she started to cry.

The child stopped crying soon after, but she was still confused. She asked her friend why he slapped her.

The friend replied, "Sometimes when we are feeling dizzy, a slap can help us feel better. I'm sorry if I hurt you. Can we be friends again?"

The child nodded, and they hugged again. From then on, they were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sara. She had a dolly, which she loved very much. One day she was playing with her dolly when she noticed something strange. Nearby, she saw an enormous doll!

"Wow," Sara said. "That's a really big doll!"

The huge doll seemed to move closer to Sara. She was very scared, but she bravely asked the doll, "Who are you?"

The enormous doll didn't answer, but it began to change. First its arms and legs moved, and then it started to grow taller and its face became different. 

Sara was very surprised. The enormous doll had changed into a fairy! 

The fairy said, "I'm here to help you, Sara. All you have to do is believe in yourself." 
Sara gasped. She believed the fairy. She hugged her own dolly tight and decided she could do anything!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Clara. She was happy and adventurous. One day, she decided to explore the forest near her house. As she walked, Clara saw a bucket on the side of the path. She wondered what it was doing there.

Clara slowly stepped closer to the bucket. It was old and rusty. She could tell it had been there for a long time. Suddenly, the bucket started to shake and move. Clara was scared and ran away.

The next day, Clara asked her mom why the bucket moved. Her mom told her there was something inside it. Something scary. Clara was so scared she was shaking.

That night, Clara was very brave and returned to the forest. She walked up to the old rusty bucket, and carefully looked inside. To her surprise, all she found was a cute little bunny! She petted it and knew she had nothing to be scared of.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She liked grapes very much. Her mommy said she could buy some if she was careful.

So Lucy went to the store and looked around. She found lots of grapes but some were too expensive! She wanted something cheap. Then she saw a big basket of grapes, they were very sharp and dark green.

She asked the shopkeeper how much they were, and he said they were very cheap! Lucy was so excited, she picked out the biggest, sharpest and juciest grapes and was on her way home.

When she got back home, her mommy was very pleased. She said Lucy had done a great job finding such cheap and delicious grapes! Lucy was so proud and happy. She enjoyed eating her sharp grapes and dreamed of going back to the store for more.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety decided to visit his friend, a rabbit named Bugs. Tweety flew and flew until he arrived at Bugs' house. 

Bugs was happy to see Tweety and offered him a delicious pie to eat. Tweety was very hungry and ate the pie quickly. Bugs was impressed by how graceful Tweety looked while eating the pie. 

After eating the pie, Tweety and Bugs played together and had lots of fun. When it was time for Tweety to go back home, Bugs waved goodbye and Tweety flew away happily. Tweety arrived home safely and went to sleep, dreaming of his next adventure.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play with toys. But they do not like to share. They always fight over who gets the best toy. One day, they find a big box of toys in the attic. They are very happy and run to the box.

"Look, a doll!" Kim says. She grabs the doll and hugs it.

"No, it is mine!" Tim says. He pulls the doll from Kim.

"Give it back!" Kim says. She pulls the doll from Tim.

They pull and pull until they hear a rip. They tear the doll in half. They are both shocked and sad. They look at the doll's head and body in their hands.

"Look what you did!" Tim says.

"Look what you did!" Kim says.

They start to cry. They hear a noise behind the box. They turn around and see a big rat. The rat has sharp teeth and red eyes. It looks hungry and angry. It sees the twins and the doll.

"Yum, yum!" the rat says. It runs to the twins and the doll.

"Help!" Tim and Kim say. They are very scared. They drop the doll and run to the door. They try to open it, but it is locked. They bang on the door and scream for help.

"Mom! Dad! Help!" they say.

Mom and Dad hear the noise and come to the attic. They see the rat and the doll. They open the door and save the twins. They chase the rat away and throw the doll in the trash.

"Are you okay?" Mom says.

"Yes, we are okay," Tim and Kim say.

"Why were you so noisy?" Dad says.

"We were fighting over the doll," Tim says.

"We tore the doll in half," Kim says.

They look at each other and feel sorry.

"We are sorry," they say.

Mom and Dad hug them and say, "We are glad you are okay. But you should not fight over toys. You should share and be kind. Toys are not as important as love. Do you understand?"

"Yes, we understand," Tim and Kim say.

They promise to share and be kind from now on. They learn their lesson and never fight over toys again. They are happy and love each other. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a fast squirrel. He liked to run around the forest, looking for nuts to eat. One day, the squirrel saw something shiny and he wanted to check it out. He couldn't quite get to it, so he let out a loud squeak. 

A kind person heard the noise and came walking over. The person let the squirrel climb on their arm and they moved closer to the shiny thing. Together they reached the shiny item, it was a tiny nut! The squirrel was so happy, he squeaked with joy. 

The person then gently let the squirrel down and watched as the squirrel scampered away. The squirrel was so fast, the person couldn't keep up. But they were happy the squirrel had found a tasty snack.

Anna was a gifted girl who loved to draw and sing. She had a big box of crayons and a book of songs that her mom gave her. She liked to make pictures of her family and friends and sing along with the music.

One day, she found a shiny key under her bed. She wondered what it could unlock. She looked around her room and saw a small chest on her shelf. She had never opened it before. She climbed on a chair and reached for the chest. She put the key in the lock and turned it.

The chest opened and inside was a beautiful crystal. It sparkled in the light and had many colors. Anna was amazed and happy. She picked up the crystal and held it in her hand. It felt warm and smooth.

"Wow, what a pretty crystal!" she said out loud.

"Hello, Anna," a voice said.

Anna was surprised and looked around. She saw no one. Then she realized the voice came from the crystal.

"Who are you?" she asked.

"I am a fairy. I have been waiting for you to unlock the chest. You are the only one who can see me and hear me. You are a gifted girl, Anna. You have a special heart and a creative mind. I am here to be your friend and help you with your dreams."

Anna smiled and hugged the crystal. She felt a tingling in her fingers and a flutter in her chest. She knew she had found a magical treasure and a new friend. She was excited to learn more about the fairy and the crystal. She thanked the key and the chest and put them back on the shelf. She took the crystal with her and ran to show her mom. She wanted to share her joy and wonder with her. She knew her mom would understand and love her gift.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Bob. Bob loved exploring and playing games. One day, Bob was outside. Suddenly, he heard a deep voice calling out to him.

"Come and see me!" called the voice.

Bob was very scared. He ran and ran until he reached a gloomy, old house. The house had a tall cane leaning against its front door. Bob was about to leave when he heard the voice again.

"Come inside!" commanded the voice.

Bob was even more scared but he opened the door and stepped into the old house. Inside, everything was very dark and gloomy. Bob tried to escape, but couldn't find a way out.

Just then, a kind old man with a white cane appeared. He smiled warmly at Bob and said:

"Don't be scared! I'm here to help you. Let me show you the way out of this house."

The old man led Bob out of the gloomy house and into the sunshine. Bob was so happy to be free! He thanked the old man and waved goodbye as he ran off in search of his next adventure.

Lily liked to fold paper. She learned how to make many shapes with paper. She made hats, boats, planes, and flowers. But her favorite shape was a penguin. She loved penguins. They were black and white and funny.

One day, Lily wanted to make a unique penguin. She found a blue paper and a yellow paper. She folded the blue paper into a penguin body. She folded the yellow paper into a penguin beak and feet. She glued them together. She had a blue and yellow penguin. She was very proud.

She showed her penguin to her mom and dad. They smiled and hugged her. They said her penguin was very unique and beautiful. They put her penguin on the fridge. Lily was happy. She wanted to make more unique penguins. She looked for more paper. She found red, green, purple, and orange. She folded and glued and smiled. She made a rainbow of penguins. She loved them all.

Once there was a little girl who loved yoga. She tried it every day and was very excited to do more new poses. 

One day, she asked her mom if they could go to a yoga studio. Her mom agreed and they set off.

When they arrived at the studio, the little girl was so happy. But when they opened the door, the teacher inside was lazy. She was not prepared and so the class was cancelled. 

The little girl was very sad. She was not able to do yoga that day. She looked up at her mom and said, "I hope I can do yoga tomorrow."

But the next day, the studio was closed. The teacher had decided to stay home and be lazy.

The little girl was very disappointed. She couldn't do her yoga and was sad all day. She had been so excited to try new poses, but it didn't happen. She had lost hope.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when she suddenly realized that she needed to go to the toilet. She quickly ran to the bathroom and did her business.

When she came back to her room, she saw that her favorite toy was missing. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She felt sad and started to cry.

Her mom heard her crying and came to her room. "What's wrong, Lily?" she asked.

"I can't find my toy," Lily replied, still crying.

"Don't worry, we'll find it together," her mom said. And they searched the whole house until they found the toy under the bed.

Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom tightly. "Thank you, mommy!" she said, feeling much better now.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Blue. Blue loved to fly up high in the sky and feel the wind on his feathers. One day, Blue saw a big, unusual cloud in the sky. He decided to soar up and take a closer look. As he flew closer, he saw that the cloud was shaped like a giant thermometer! Blue had never seen anything like it before.

Blue was curious and wanted to know more about the thermometer cloud. He flew around it, trying to find out where it came from. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise coming from inside the cloud. It sounded like someone was playing music! Blue was amazed and wanted to see who was making the noise. He flew even closer to the cloud and saw that there was a group of birds playing instruments inside.

Blue was so happy to have discovered something new and exciting. He flew back to his nest and told all his bird friends about the unusual thermometer cloud and the birds playing music inside. They were all amazed and asked Blue to take them to see it too. And so, Blue and his friends soared up into the sky to explore and discover new things together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe. Joe was three years old and very enthusiastic. He loved to play outside with his toys. 

One day, Joe's mommy asked him to go and fetch some juice from the store. Joe eagerly agreed and ran to the store. 

When he got there, he had to wait in line with all the big people. Joe was getting impatient, but then he noticed some juice at the back of the store. He urged himself to get there sooner, so he could get it and be back home.

Giggling with excitement, Joe got hold of the juice and rushed back to his mommy. His mommy was very proud of him, and gave him a big hug.

Joe opened the juice and started drinking it with a smile on his face. His enthusiastic curiosity made his mommy smile, too.

The end.

Mia and Leo are friends. They like to play in the park. Mia likes to swing on the big swing. Leo likes to slide on the slide. But they are shy to talk to other kids.

One day, they see a new kid in the park. He has a red hat and a blue bike. He looks at Mia and Leo and smiles. He says, "Hi, I'm Sam. Do you want to play with me?"

Mia and Leo are scared. They don't know Sam. They hide behind the swing and the slide. They whisper to each other, "Who is he? What if he is mean? What if he takes our toys?"

Sam sees them hiding. He feels sad. He wants to make friends. He rides his bike to them and says, "Don't be shy. I'm nice. I have a lot of toys. Do you want to see?"

Mia and Leo peek out from behind the swing and the slide. They see Sam has a big bag of toys. He has cars, balls, dolls, and books. They look fun. Mia and Leo are curious. They come out from their hiding places and say, "Okay, we'll play with you."

Sam is happy. He opens his bag and shows them his toys. He says, "You can choose any toy you like. We can share. Do you like cars or balls or dolls or books?"

Mia and Leo look at the toys. They see something they like. Mia picks a doll. Leo picks a car. They say, "Thank you, Sam. These are nice toys. We like dolls and cars."

Sam says, "You're welcome, Mia and Leo. I like dolls and cars too. Do you want to play with me on the swing and the slide?"

Mia and Leo nod. They say, "Yes, we want to play with you on the swing and the slide."

They put their toys in Sam's bag. They hold hands and run to the swing and the slide. They take turns swinging and sliding. They laugh and talk. They have fun.

They are not shy anymore. They are friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was so excited because today was very special. 

She was going to help her Mommy sort some silver. In her Mommy's drawer, there were lots of different pieces of silver. 

Mommy said "Hi Lucy! Today, we're going to sort these silver pieces."

Lucy smiled and said "Yes, Mommy!"

Then, they both got to work. Together, they sorted the silver pieces into small piles. When they were done, Mommy smiled and said "Good job, Lucy! You did a great job sorting out the silver pieces."

Lucy beamed with pride. She was so happy to help her Mommy and now the silver was all sorted out. She loved the feeling of accomplishment!

Once there was a bossy little girl named Emma. She wanted to go on a kayak. So she grabbed her oars, hopped onto the kayak and began to paddle. She wanted to go far away, but her oars weren't very powerful. She poked at the water with her oars, but the kayak just wouldn't move.

The water seemed to be against her. She started to get angry, so she tried even harder. She pushed and she poked, but the kayak wouldn't move. Emma was getting very mad.

She thought about her predicament and decided to ask for help. She called out to a nearby duck. â€œCan you please help me?â€ she pleaded. The duck just laughed and continued to swim.

So she tried one last time. She put her feet on the paddle and pushed as hard as she could. Slowly the kayak was moving. Emma had done it! She was going on an adventure!

Once upon a time, there lived a small bunny called Max. Every day, Max would hop around looking for something to do. One day, he noticed a sparkly chamber. He couldn't believe his eyes! Inside, he saw lots of treats and toys. He got closer to the chamber and noticed it was locked.

Max hopped away and soon came across his friend, Jack. "Jack! I found this amazing chamber with lots of treats inside. How can I get inside?"

But Jack shook his head. "Max, that chamber is not for us. We must not try to take what is not ours. That would be very stupid!"

Max knew Jack was right, so he decided to leave the chamber alone. He knew that taking what wasn't his was wrong and he wanted to be a good bunny.

The moral of the story is to include others in everything we do and never do stupid things. Taking what isn't ours is not right and it's important to remember that.

Ben liked to look at small things with his microscope. He had a microscope that his dad gave him for his birthday. He could see bugs, leaves, and hairs with his microscope. He liked to learn new things and ask questions.

One day, he found a feather on the ground. He wondered what it looked like with his microscope. He took it to his room and put it on a slide. He turned on his microscope and looked through the eye piece. He saw many tiny parts that made up the feather. He saw colors and shapes that he had never seen before. He was amazed.

He wanted to show his mom what he found. He ran to the kitchen where his mom was making dinner. He said, "Mom, mom, look what I found with my microscope! It's a feather, but it's not just a feather. It has so many things inside it. Come and see!"

His mom smiled and said, "That sounds very interesting, Ben. I'm glad you're having fun with your microscope. But I'm a little busy right now. Can you wait until after dinner?"

Ben felt sad. He wanted to share his discovery with his mom. He said, "But mom, it's so cool. You have to see it. Please, please, please!"

His mom saw that he was very excited. She did not want to disappoint him. She said, "Okay, Ben. I'll come and see your feather. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you'll eat your dinner and go to bed on time. You look very sleepy. You need to rest after a long day of exploring."

Ben nodded and said, "I promise, mom. Thank you, mom. You're the best mom ever!" He hugged his mom and ran back to his room. He waited for his mom to come and see his feather. He felt happy. His mom encouraged him to keep learning and to take care of himself. He loved his mom and his microscope.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun and rain. One day, she saw a big rainbow in the sky. 

Lily: "Mommy, look! A rainbow!" 

Mommy: "Yes, it's very pretty. Do you want to draw a picture of it?" 

Lily: "Yes, please!" 

So, Lily ran inside to get some paper and crayons. She tried hard to draw the rainbow, but it was difficult. 

Lily: "Mommy, can you help me wrap the colors of the rainbow in my picture?" 

Mommy: "Of course, sweetie. Let's start with red." 

Together, they wrapped the colors of the rainbow in Lily's picture. It was the most beautiful rainbow Lily had ever seen.

Once upon a time, there was a big ship. It was so mighty that it could sail through strong storms. One day, the ship saw a little bird who was tired and needed help. The ship offered to give the bird a ride to a safe place. The bird was happy and flew onto the ship's deck. They sailed together until they found a nice spot for the bird to rest. The bird thanked the mighty ship for its help and flew away. From that day on, the ship always looked out for animals who needed help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved firemen. He would always watch them drive by in their big red trucks with their loud sirens. One day, Timmy saw a fireman walking down the street. He ran up to him and said, "Hi Mr. Fireman! I enjoy watching you put out fires!"

The fireman smiled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. It's my job to keep everyone safe from fires." Timmy looked up at the fireman and said, "You are so graceful when you climb up the tall ladder to put out the fire." The fireman chuckled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. It takes a lot of practice to be a good fireman."

Timmy was so happy to meet a real fireman. He waved goodbye as the fireman got back into his big red truck and drove away. From that day on, Timmy knew he wanted to be a fireman when he grew up.

Once, there was a furry spider. He was walking along the path and saw a house. He wanted to get in, so he asked the house if he could pass. The house said no, so the spider was sad.

He saw a bunny and asked if he could pass. The bunny said yes! The spider was so happy. He went inside the bunny's house and found a nice warm bed.

The bunny said, "You can stay here if you like." The furry spider happily said yes. He stayed in the bunny's home for days.

One day, the bunny asked the furry spider if he wanted to go outside and play. The spider said yes! He was so excited.

They went outside together and had a great time. The furry spider had never had so much fun before. In the end, the spider said goodbye to his new friend, the bunny, and went back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a furry teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Lily and Teddy went outside to play. It started to rain, and they got wet. 

Lily said, "Teddy, I feel wet." 

Teddy said, "I feel wet too." 

Lily said, "Let's go inside and get dry." 

They went inside and got dry. Lily said, "I love the rain, but I don't like to be wet." 

Teddy said, "I love the rain too, but I don't like to be wet either." 

Lily hugged Teddy and said, "I'm glad we're dry now." Teddy hugged Lily back and said, "Me too."

Lily liked to play in the garden with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a teddy bear. She loved her teddy bear the most. She hugged him and kissed him every day.

One day, Lily saw a big seed in the garden. She wondered what it was. She dug a hole and put the seed in it. She watered it and waited. She hoped it would grow into a pretty flower.

The next day, Lily went to the garden to check on the seed. She was surprised to see a green sprout. It was very tall and thick. It had sharp leaves and thorns. Lily was curious. She touched the sprout. It hurt her finger. She cried.

The day after, Lily went to the garden again. She was shocked to see a huge plant. It was taller than her house. It had big purple flowers and long vines. It smelled bad. Lily was scared. She ran away.

The day after that, Lily went to the garden once more. She was terrified to see a monster. It was the plant. It had grown eyes, teeth, claws and wings. It roared and snapped at her. Lily screamed.

Lily's mom and dad heard her scream. They came to the garden. They saw the monster. They were angry. They got a shovel, a rake and a hose. They fought the monster. They cut its vines, sprayed its flowers and dug its roots. The monster wilted and died.

Lily's mom and dad hugged her. They were glad she was safe. They told her she should never plant strange seeds. They said they could be dangerous. They said she should only plant good seeds. They said they would help her grow a nice garden.

Lily was sorry. She said she was sorry. She said she learned her lesson. She said she would never plant strange seeds again. She said she would only plant good seeds. She said she loved her mom and dad. She said she loved her teddy bear. She hugged him and kissed him. He was not scary. He was soft and warm. He was her friend.

Once there was a little boy named Tim who liked to explore his house. One day he went to the attic and saw a big box in the corner. He kneeled down and carefully opened the box. Inside he found a sweet old toy. When he opened the toy it started to play a sour melody. 

Tim said to himself, "What is this funny sound?" He looked around and then he saw an old lady smiling at him. 

The lady said, "That's my grandma's old music box. She used to sing me a sweet song when I was little."

Tim listened to the music carefully and then said, "It's sour, but it's beautiful!"

The old lady smiled and said, "That's the power of music." 

Then, Tim and the old lady danced around the attic to the sweet, sour melody until it was time for Tim to go back home.

Once upon a time there was a little mouse named Sam. He was always dreaming of being rich.

One day, Sam found a big, shiny button. He thought it could make him rich, so he decided to press it. 

Suddenly, Sam heard a magical voice. "I will give you anything you want," said the voice.

Sam was so excited. He said, "I want to be rich!"

The voice replied, "Your wish is granted. Press the button again, and you will be rich!"

Sam happily pressed the button. Suddenly he found himself in a big house filled with gold coins. He was so happy to be rich!

The End.

One day, a little boy named Tom was playing in his room. He liked to build towers with his blocks and knock them down with his cars. He was having fun until he saw something on the wall. It was a spider! A big, black, hairy spider with eight legs and two eyes. Tom was scared of spiders. He dropped his blocks and cars and ran to his bed. He hid under his blanket and trembled.

"Mommy! Mommy!" he cried. "There is a spider in my room! Help me!"

His mommy heard him and came to his room. She saw the spider on the wall and smiled. She was not scared of spiders. She thought they were interesting and helpful. She picked up a cup and a paper and went to the wall. She put the cup over the spider and slid the paper under it. She lifted the cup and the paper and carried them to the window.

"Look, Tom," she said. "This is the spider. He is not here to hurt you. He is here to catch flies and bugs. He is your friend."

Tom peeked out from his blanket and looked at the spider. He saw that it was not so big or scary. It was just a little spider with a shiny body and tiny feet. It moved around in the cup and made a soft sound.

"Can I touch him?" Tom asked.

"Sure, but be gentle," his mommy said. She opened the window and let the spider out. The spider crawled on Tom's hand and tickled him. Tom giggled and felt brave.

"Bye, spider," he said. "Thank you for being my friend."

The spider waved his legs and jumped off Tom's hand. He spun a web on a tree and waited for his dinner. Tom and his mommy waved back and closed the window. Tom went back to his blocks and cars and played happily. He was not scared of spiders anymore. He liked them. He hoped to see the spider again.

Once upon a time there was a robot named Bob. He was a friendly robot who liked to play with his friends. One day, Bob made a new friend named Ted. When Bob and Ted played together, Bob enjoyed it very much.

However, Bob's other friends were very jealous. They wished they could play with Bob too, but they couldn't because Ted was always there.

One day Bob and Ted decided to play in the rain. They ran out and splashed in the puddles. Bob and Ted laughed and chased each other around. But it wasn't long before they were completely soaked.

The jealous friends had an idea. They ran to the shed and grabbed a big towel. Then, they carefully dried off Bob and Ted. Bob was so glad to be dry and he thanked his friends for their help.

Bob and Ted smiled, hugged their friends and went back to playing. Bob and Ted played together a lot after that. No matter what, the jealous friends were always there to make sure they both stayed dry and happy.

Lily and Max were twins. They liked to play and share. One day, Mom gave them a big muffin for a snack. It had chocolate chips and nuts on top.

"Wow, thank you, Mom!" Lily and Max said. They were very hungry and happy.

They took the muffin to the table. They looked at it and smiled. Then they looked at each other.

"How do we eat it?" Lily asked.

"Let's split it!" Max said. He took a knife and cut the muffin in half. He gave one half to Lily and kept one half for himself.

"Here you go, Lily. This is your half. It has more chocolate chips," Max said.

"Thank you, Max. You are very kind. Your half has more nuts," Lily said.

They bit into their muffin halves. They chewed and swallowed. They made yummy noises.

"Mmm, this is so good!" Lily said.

"I agree, this is delicious!" Max said.

They finished their muffin halves. They licked their fingers and lips. They looked at each other and hugged.

"I'm glad we split the muffin. It was more fun to share," Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. I'm glad we are twins. You are my best friend," Max said.

They ran to Mom and gave her a big hug and a kiss.

"Thank you, Mom, for the muffin. We loved it!" Lily and Max said.

Mom smiled and hugged them back.

"You're welcome, my sweeties. I'm glad you enjoyed it. And I'm proud of you for being so nice to each other," Mom said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, Lily was playing with her friends and it started to get dark outside. Her friend, Timmy, said, "I can't see anything! I wish we had a flashlight."

Lily remembered that she had a flashlight in her bag. She took it out and turned it on. The light was very bright and everyone could see in the dark. Timmy said, "Wow, Lily! You're so humble for sharing your flashlight with us."

Lily smiled and said, "It's okay, Timmy. We can all share it." They continued to play hide-and-seek and when they were done, Lily folded up the flashlight and put it back in her bag. She was happy that she could help her friends see in the dark.

John went to the park with his family. His mom gave him a tray to play with. He spun around and around with it. He was so successful that he made other children at the park join him. All the friends spun around in a circle with their trays and it was really fun. Everyone was happy and John was the most successful spinner! He kept spinning and spinning until it was time to go home. Everyone said goodbye and wished each other a good day. John went home with a big smile on his face, thinking about how much fun he had spinning with his tray.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a chain on the ground. It is shiny and long.

"Look, a chain!" Sara says. "Let's play with it."

They take the chain and run around. They make a circle with the chain. They pretend it is a snake. They laugh and have fun.

But then, a grumpy man comes. He is angry. He says the chain is his. He says they are bad children. He takes the chain away.

Sara and Ben are sad. They cry. They want the chain back.

"Go away, you little thieves!" the grumpy man says. He walks away with the chain.

Sara and Ben hug each other. They say they are sorry. They say they are still friends.

They see a flower. It is pretty and pink. Sara picks it up. She gives it to Ben.

"Here, a flower for you," she says. "You are my friend."

Ben smiles. He takes the flower. He gives it to Sara.

"Thank you, Sara. You are my friend too."

They kiss each other on the cheek. They are happy again. They forget about the chain and the grumpy man. They play in the park. They laugh and have fun.

Luke and Emma were best friends. Every day they went to the park together and had a lot of fun. One day they wanted to do something special.

"Let's eat a sandwich!" said Luke.

"I dare you," said Emma.

So Luke was brave and ate a sandwich. It was delicious.

But then Emma got a grumpy face. She said that she wanted a sandwich too.

"No, you can't have a sandwich," said Luke.

Emma was very sad. She started to cry and stomped off.

Luke felt bad for not sharing the sandwich. He started to follow Emma but it was too late. Emma had already gone home and was never seen again.

One day, Daisy was gazing out the window of her house. She saw a boy in the distance, beyond the deep woods. She wanted to go meet him but she was afraid. Suddenly, Daisy had a wonderful idea. She wanted to win a race to the boy. 

With excitement, Daisy went outside and started running to the boy. Suddenly, she stopped when she saw how deep the woods were. She was scared! Her mom noticed Daisy standing there and said, "You can do it! Believe in yourself.â€ 

Daisy felt brave and charged through the woods. After a few minutes, she saw the boy. He smiled and waved to Daisy. She smiled back and kept running. When Daisy finally reached him, the boy asked if she wanted to race against him. She eagerly nodded. 

The race began! Daisy was determined to win and kept running, even when she was tired. She passed the boy, who gave Daisy a big thumbs up. In the end, Daisy won the race and both children laughed and smiled.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was getting ready to go outside to play. She put on her sweater because it was cold outside. But when she tried to zip it up, the zipper got stuck! Lily tried and tried, but she couldn't manage to get it unstuck.

Lily's mom came in and saw her struggling. "What's wrong, sweetie?" she asked. Lily showed her the stuck zipper on her tough sweater. "Oh no," said her mom. "Let me see if I can help." 

But even her mom couldn't manage to get the zipper unstuck. Lily was starting to get upset because she really wanted to go outside and play. "Don't worry," said her mom. "We'll figure it out together." 

After trying a few different things, they finally managed to get the zipper unstuck. Lily was so happy and thanked her mom for helping her. "No problem, sweetie," her mom said. "I'm always here to help you when you need it." And with that, Lily went outside to play with her friends, warm and cozy in her tough sweater.

Once upon a time, there was a clean teaspoon. The teaspoon was so special that it never got tired. Every day, the teaspoon went off on an adventure.

On this day, the teaspoon went to the beach. The sun was shining and the birds were singing. The teaspoon was very happy.

The teaspoon played in the sand and splashed in the water. But after a while it was time to rest. So the teaspoon lay down on a soft blanket of sand and fell asleep.

The teaspoon didn't wake up for a long time. When it did, it felt very refreshed. With a smile on its face, the teaspoon continued exploring. It was ready for more adventures!

Once upon a time, there were two friends who wanted to make something special. They decided to make a jar, so they started gathering the materials needed. 

â€œLetâ€™s use this special clay to make the jar,â€ said one friend. 

â€œGood idea,â€ said the other.

The two put the clay on the ground and started to shape the jar with their hands. After a few minutes, they had made the jar. They were so proud of their work and they hugged each other in happiness. 

â€œLetâ€™s make something special to put inside the jar,â€ said one friend. 

The two friends went out to find something special and eventually found a special pebble. They put the pebble inside the jar and smiled knowing that this jar was now something special. 

The friends realised that they had done something successful. They high-fived each other and celebrated their success.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. They made a lot of noise and a big mess. They did not put anything back in its place.

Mom came in and saw the messy living room. She was not happy. She said, "Sara and Ben, what have you done? This is a mess! I have a meeting soon and I need the living room to be clean. You have to restore it to how it was before. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They did not want to make Mom angry. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We will restore it. We will put everything back in its place."

Mom smiled. She said, "Thank you, Sara and Ben. I appreciate your help. You have ten minutes to restore it. Then you can have a snack and read a book with me."

Sara and Ben worked together to restore the living room. They picked up their toys and put them in the toy box. They stacked the books on the shelf. They folded the blankets and put them on the couch. They swept the floor and threw away the trash.

They finished in time. They showed Mom the restored living room. Mom was proud of them. She said, "Well done, Sara and Ben. You did a great job. The living room looks nice and clean. You are good helpers. Now you can have a snack and read a book with me."

Sara and Ben were happy. They hugged Mom and said, "We love you, Mom. You are the best." They had a snack and read a book with Mom. They enjoyed their time together.

Tom was a little sheep who liked to play with his friends in the field. He had soft white wool that kept him warm and cozy. He was not afraid of anything, or so he thought.

One day, a big dog came to the field. He barked and ran after the sheep. The sheep were scared and ran away. Tom tried to run too, but he tripped on a rock and fell down. He saw the dog coming closer and closer. He felt very afraid.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "Someone help me!"

He heard a voice behind him. It was his friend, Anna, another sheep. She had black wool and big horns.

"Don't worry, Tom, I'm here!" she said. "I'll protect you from the dog!"

She stood in front of Tom and faced the dog. She lowered her horns and charged at the dog. The dog was surprised and yelped. He turned around and ran away.

Anna came back to Tom and helped him up.

"Are you okay, Tom?" she asked.

"Yes, thank you, Anna," Tom said. "You are very brave. You saved me from the dog."

Anna smiled and nuzzled him.

"You're welcome, Tom," she said. "You are my friend. Friends help each other."

Tom realized that Anna was right. He was glad that he had a friend like her. He hugged her and thanked her again.

They went back to the other sheep and told them what happened. The other sheep praised Anna for her courage and Tom for his gratitude. They all played together happily in the field. Tom learned that being brave is not about never being afraid, but about facing your fears with the help of your friends.

Anna liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long hair, a pink dress, and a flexible body. Anna could bend her arms and legs and make her do different poses.

One day, Anna's mom said, "We have to move to a new house, Anna. It is bigger and has more space for your toys."

Anna was happy. She packed her dolls in a big box and put Lily on top. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. You will like the new house. It has a big room for us to play."

The next day, they drove to the new house. Anna was excited. She ran to her new room and opened the box. She took out Lily and hugged her. She said, "Look, Lily. This is our new room. It is so big and bright. We can play here all day."

But then, she saw something that made her sad. On the wall, there was a big poster of a superhero. He had a mask, a cape, and a big letter S on his chest. He looked strong and brave. Anna did not like him. She said, "Who is that, Mom?"

Mom said, "That is your new brother's poster. He likes superheroes. He will share this room with you. He is coming tomorrow."

Anna did not want to share her room. She did not want a new brother. She said, "No, Mom. I don't like him. I don't want him here. This is my room. This is Lily's room."

Mom said, "I know, Anna. But you have to be nice and flexible. He is your family. He will be your friend. You will have fun together. You can teach him how to play with dolls. He can teach you how to play with superheroes. You can increase your imagination and learn new things."

Anna did not believe Mom. She did not think she could have fun with a boy who liked superheroes. She did not think he would like Lily. She did not think he would be flexible. She hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will always be together. We will always be happy. We don't need anyone else."

Once upon a time there was a brother and sister who loved to play together. One day they went to the park and saw the most interesting mug. It was big, colourful and looked like it belonged to a magical creature. The brother was very tempted to steal it but the sister was obedient and wouldn't let him.

The brother said "Come on, just take it! It'll be fun!"

The sister replied firmly "No! That would be wrong, stealing is not allowed!"

Eventually, the brother listened to his sister and put the mug back. Both of them were glad that they had been obedient and followed the rules. After that, they ran off and played their favourite game. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Becky. She was happy and smiley, but her clothes were always pale and grey. People used to laugh at her and they asked "Why do you wear a grey shirt everywhere?" Becky didn't know what to say.

One day, Becky was walking in the park when she saw a butterfly. It was so pretty and colorful, so she reached out to catch it. The butterfly tickled her hand and flew away. As it flew away, Becky cried. But then, her new friend, a little bird, came flying to her.


"Don't be sad, Becky," said the bird. "I can help you make your shirt colorful."

The little bird gave Becky colorful feathers and told her to make a shirt with them. Becky made the most beautiful shirt, with all the colorful feathers, and it made her so happy. She wore the shirt everywhere, and everyone loved it.

The moral of the story is: When you are kind to nature, nature will be kind to you. And never be afraid to be yourself and show off who you are.

The next day, Becky went back to the park and the butterfly was there. It flew to her and kissed her on the cheek, as if to say thank you.

Becky smiled and knew that nature had welcomed her with open arms.

Once there was a lion who was feeling very frustrated. He wanted to take a turn, but he didn't know what to do. He saw a bright light that made him feel happy. It was glowing all around him and he wanted to play with it. 

He stepped closer and saw a group of stars. He started to run around and around, chasing the stars. As he ran, the stars began to shimmer. He laughed and smiled as he watched them glow in the night sky. 

He kept running until he saw a rainbow. The colors glowed brightly and the lion was amazed. He wanted to explore the colors. He ran up to the rainbow and started playing with it. He jumped and he laughed and he played. 

Finally, the lion stumbled and fell asleep. He dreamed of the warm glow from the stars and the rainbow and that made him feel happy. When he woke up, he felt much better. He had gone on a magical turn and he was no longer frustrated.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious berry in the forest. Animals from all around wanted to try it, so they gathered together to decide who would go first. It was decided that the brave rabbit would try it, and so he hopped over to the berry. When he tried to take a bite, a magical force surrounded him and the berry and he couldn't escape! He tried to resist the mysterious power, but it was too strong, and so he was stuck! 

The other animals were sad and didn't know what to do. Then an idea came to a brave squirrel who suggested they all worked together to try and help the rabbit. So, they all tried to pull the rabbit away from the berry but the magical force just kept getting stronger! 

Just then, a wise owl arrived and said he knew how to break the spell. He told the animals to resist the mysterious power of the berry by not giving in to it, and the power would be broken. So the animals joined forces and resisted, and sure enough, the magical force started to gradually disappear! Finally, the brave rabbit was free and able to enjoy the berry for himself.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Meg and Tom. Tom had a cloth that he was very proud of. He loved to zoom around the room with it. One day, Meg said to Tom, "I can fly too, Tom, watch me!" Meg jumped up and span around in the air, flying in a circle. Tom was amazed and said, "Wow! You are so independent Meg!" Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy, her daddy, and her little dog, Max. One day, Lily and Max went outside to play in the yard. The sun was shining, the birds were singing, and the grass was soft and green.

As they played, Max saw a big, red ball. "Let's play with the ball, Lily," Max said. Lily smiled and nodded. They ran to the ball, but Lily had to be careful not to slip on the wet grass. Max kicked the ball high into the air, and Lily tried to catch it. "Not yet, Max!" she said, as the ball flew over her head.

They played with the ball all day, laughing and having fun. When it was time to go inside, Lily and Max were tired but happy. They had a great day playing together, and they couldn't wait to do it again tomorrow.

Anna and her mom were waiting for dad to arrive. They had not seen him for a long time, because he had to work far away. Anna missed him a lot and wanted to hug him and play with him. She had a picture of him in her room that she looked at every night.

"Mom, when will dad be here?" Anna asked.

"Soon, sweetie, soon. He said he would be here by noon. He loves you very much, you know. You are his loyal daughter." Mom said.

Anna smiled and nodded. She was loyal to dad, and to mom too. She always did what they told her and tried to be good. She hoped dad would bring her a present, maybe a doll or a book.

They heard a car honk outside. Anna ran to the window and saw dad's car. He was here! She jumped up and down and clapped her hands. Mom grabbed her coat and they ran outside to meet him.

But when they got to the car, they saw that dad was not alone. There was another woman in the car, a woman they did not know. She had long hair and a big smile. She got out of the car and hugged dad.

"Who is that?" Anna asked, feeling confused and scared.

Mom looked at dad with a sad and angry face. She did not say anything.

Dad looked at them and said, "Anna, mom, this is Lisa. She is my new friend. I'm sorry, but I'm not coming home with you. I'm going to live with Lisa now. Goodbye."

He got back in the car and drove away with Lisa. Anna and mom were left alone on the sidewalk, crying. They had lost dad, and he had broken their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle bunny. One day, the bunny was walking through the forest. Suddenly, it heard another creature. It was a fox.

The bunny stopped. The fox said, "where are you going?"

The bunny remained still. It wanted to remain safe.

The fox said, "Please do not be scared. I just wanted to ask if you would like to join me to the lake? The lake is a very beautiful place."

The bunny thought carefully. Then, it nodded. The fox smiled.

The fox and the bunny walked together to the lake. When they arrived, the bunny ran to the lake's edge. It was so clear and blue.

The fox pointed to a rock that was in the middle of the lake. He said, "That's our special spot. It's where we can remain safe."

The bunny hopped onto the gentle waves of the lake and made its way to the rock. From the rock, the bunny and the fox watched the stars together. 

They stayed there until nightfall. They both knew that the rock was a special place where they could remain safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spike. Spike had a big, shiny toy that he loved to play with. All the other dogs in the park were jealous of Spike's toy because it was so pretty and fun.

One day, a big dog came to the park and wanted to play with Spike's toy. Spike said, "You can play, but you have to pay me two treats." The big dog agreed and gave Spike two treats. They played with the toy together, and it was so much fun.

After playing, the big dog thanked Spike and went home. All the other dogs saw how much fun they had and decided to pay Spike treats to play with his toy too. Spike was very happy, and all the dogs in the park learned to share and play together.

Once upon a time, there was a humble vet. She loved to fly. Every day, she would fly up high through the sky. She would soar up and around the clouds. 

The vet was a very special veterinarian. She went around to all the farms to help sick animals. She treated cows, horses, and pigs with her gentle care.

The vet took the duck to her office and gave him medicine. She was so gentle and patient as she took care of him. The duck was so happy and feeling much better in no time. 

The vet was so happy that the duck was feeling better. She flew the duck back to his farm. From then on, the duck and his family were very thankful for the help of the humble vet.

But then, Timmy slipped on a rock and fell into the river. He couldn't swim and the water was too deep. Max tried to save him, but it was too late. Timmy drowned in the river. Max was very sad and missed his best friend.

Ben and Mia were sad and angry. They did not want to play on the beach or in the garden. They wanted to go to the island. They waited until their mom was busy in the kitchen. Then they sneaked out of the house and ran to the boat. They pushed the boat into the water and climbed in. They took the oars and started to row.

They rowed and rowed for a long time. They got tired and thirsty. They looked at the island. It did not seem to get any closer. They looked at the shore. It seemed to get farther and farther. They started to feel scared. They wished they had listened to their mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jemima. She loved to swing in the park. One day, she was playing with some blocks. She made a neat stack of them, and was feeling very successful. Then suddenly, a gust of wind blew the stack into the air. Jemima shouted, "My stack!" but it was too late. The stack broke apart as it hit the ground. She ran over to pick up the blocks, feeling very sad.

Just then, a kindly old man came over to her. He asked in a gentle voice, "What is wrong, little one?" She told him what had happened, and he gave her a big smile. He said, "You know what? If you swing with all your heart, I bet your stack will come back together." 

So Jemima tried with all her might. She swung so hard, her feet almost left the ground. But nothing happened as her stack lay there on the ground. The old man said sadly, "I guess it wasn't meant to be". 

Jemima was very disappointed and sadly picked up the blocks. She packed up her things and went home. Sadly, her stack didn't come back together.

John and Bill were brothers. They both liked school and both wanted to be the best in school. One day, when they were both in school, John got a better grade than Bill. Bill was jealous and started to quarrel with John. They shouted and kept arguing.

John didn't understand why Bill was so angry about the grades. So he started crying. The teacher saw what was happening and told them to stop. She asked them why they were quarrel. Bill said he was jealous of John's good grade.

The teacher spoke calmly and asked them to try and be kinder to each other. She said John should be proud of his good grade, and that Bill should do his best too.

The brothers stopped quarrelling and hugged each other. From then on, they tried to be kind to each other and be happy when one of them did well in school.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived with her sister. They were very happy and loved to play together. But one day, something terrible happened - the sister got very sick. The little girl was so sad and scared that her sister might not get better.

The little girl decided to give her sister a special gift. She carefully wrapped a fragile doll in a blanket and took it outside to bury in the ground. She whispered softly, "I will always love you my sister."

The day was warm and the sun was shining, but the little girl's heart felt heavy. After she finished burying the doll, she closed her eyes and said a small prayer.

The next morning, the little girl's sister was feeling better. The little girl was so happy! She knew that the fragile doll had helped her sister get better. 

From that day on, the little girl knew that love was the most fragile, yet the strongest thing of all.

Once upon a time, there lived a kind giant. He built a comfy house for himself in a lush, green forest. Every day, he went out from the forest and shared his kindness with neighbors.

Jimmy had been waiting all day for his grandpa to arrive. His parents had said he was coming, but Jimmy couldn't wait any longer.

They were happy. They were cheerful. They waited for the meal.
