Once upon a time, there was a little seed. The little seed was dry and wanted to grow. It needed water and sun to grow big and strong.

One day, the rain came and gave the seed some water. The sun also shined on the seed. The seed said, "Thank you, rain and sun! Now I can grow!" The seed started to grow into a little plant.

The little plant wanted to have a meeting with other plants. It asked the sun, "Can you help me have a meeting with other plants?" The sun said, "Yes, I will help you!" The sun shined on other seeds, and they started to grow too.

Soon, there were many little plants. They all had a meeting and talked about how they grew. They were happy to be together and grow in the sun and rain. And they all lived happily ever after.

Ben is sleeping in his bed. He has a big dream. He is a superhero. He can fly and help people. He likes his dream.

But then, he hears a loud noise. It is his alarm. It rings high and fast. It makes Ben wake up. He does not like his alarm. He wants to stay in his dream.

He tries to cover his ears with his pillow. He says, "Go away, alarm! Let me sleep!"

But the alarm does not go away. It keeps ringing. It is time for Ben to get up. He has to go to school. He has to learn and play.

His mom comes to his room. She sees Ben hiding under his pillow. She smiles. She says, "Good morning, Ben! It is a new day. You have to turn off your alarm and get ready."

Ben groans. He does not want to get up. He says, "But mom, I like my dream. I am a superhero. I can fly and help people. Can I stay in my dream?"

His mom shakes her head. She says, "No, Ben. You can be a superhero later. Now you have to be a good boy. You have to go to school. You can learn and play. You can make new friends. You can have fun."

Ben sighs. He knows his mom is right. He turns off his alarm. He gets out of his bed. He puts on his clothes. He brushes his teeth. He eats his breakfast.

He says, "OK, mom. I am ready. Let's go to school."

His mom hugs him. She says, "I am proud of you, Ben. You are a good boy. And you are also a superhero. You can do anything you want. You can fly and help people. You can have big dreams. But you also have to live in the real world. You have to balance both."

Ben nods. He understands. He says, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

He takes his backpack. He follows his mom to the car. He looks at the sky. He sees the sun. He smiles. He thinks, "Maybe I can fly and help people after school. Maybe I can have both. Maybe I can be a superhero and a good boy."

Once upon a time, in a charming little town, there was a big mud puddle. This mud puddle was very special because it would supply fun for all the kids in the town. They loved to play in the mud and get dirty.

One sunny day, a little boy named Timmy and his friend Sally went to play in the mud puddle. Timmy said, "Sally, I think today we will find something amazing in the mud!" Sally smiled and replied, "Yes, Timmy! Let's have fun!"

They played and played, and then, just as Timmy had said, they found something in the mud. It was a shiny, golden key! They were so happy and excited. "I knew we would find something great!" said Timmy. They took the key home and knew that it was the start of a new adventure.

One day, Jimmy and his mommy went to the beach. Jimmy looked out at the ocean - it was so blue and clear! A little bird was flying way up high. Jimmy wanted to join him, so he ran to the water.

Suddenly, Jimmy felt a big splash of water all over him! He had dived in! He swam around for a little bit, and he was having so much fun!

When Jimmy was done swimming, he and his mommy went back home. Before going to bed, Jimmy decided to explore his closet. 

When he opened the door and looked inside, Jimmy saw so many cool things! He saw a big yellow ball, lots of books, and a clear treasure box!

Jimmy gasped. He couldn't believe his eyes! He wanted to dive in and explore his closet forever. But it was time for bed, so Jimmy had to go to sleep. 

The next day, Jimmy was so excited to explore his closet again!

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and a daddy who were playing with their toddler son in the park. Everything seemed to be happy and peaceful until, suddenly, there was a loud noise. The noise scared the toddler, who began to cry and panic. 

Mummy and Daddy immediately went to the toddler, who was trembling and scared. They calm him down and told him that everything was okay. Daddy said that it was just a silly game that some people were playing.

The toddler looked around and saw lots and lots of people marching and shouting, waving banners. He thought it was very exciting and wanted to join in. But then Mummy and Daddy explained that it was a war, and that it was dangerous and foolish. 

The toddler nodded, understanding the seriousness of the situation. Daddy picked him up and they quickly went back home, to the safety of their cosy house. 

The end.

Once, there was a boy named Max. He was three years old and very proud. One day, he wanted to be even prouder. He decided to go to the refrigerator and get himself a snack.

Max carefully opened the door and reached in. He pulled out a bottle of juice and smiled. Then, he reached in and grabbed a piece of cake.

Max was so proud of himself. He put his snack on the kitchen table, and carefully opened the juice and the cake. He was very satisfied with his work.

Max ate his snack and felt even prouder! He was so happy that he had grown enough to reach the refrigerator and take out his own snack. He was very proud indeed.

Tom was a fat cat who liked to sleep all day. He did not like to play with his friends, the mice, the birds, and the dog. He only liked to eat and nap on the sofa.

One day, his friends came to his home and knocked on the door. They wanted to invite him to a picnic in the park. They had cheese, seeds, and bones to share.

"Tom, Tom, come out and play with us!" they called.

But Tom did not answer. He ignored them. He was too lazy to get up. He thought he had enough food in his bowl and he did not care about the park.

"Fine, Tom, be that way. We will go without you. You are no fun at all!" his friends said. They left and went to the park. They had a lot of fun and made new friends.

Tom missed the picnic. He did not know what he was missing. He stayed on the sofa and ate and napped. He was bored and lonely. He wished he had gone with his friends. He learned a lesson. He should not ignore his friends. They are more important than food and sleep.

One day, little Toby and his dad were walking together in the park. Suddenly, Toby's dad reached in his pocket and took out a small battery. He looked at it in amazement, as if it was the most precious thing in the world. Toby asked him what it was, but his dad just stayed quiet and smiled.

After a while, though, Toby's dad spoke up. He explained that the battery was magical; whatever it touched suddenly vanished! Toby was so excited - he wanted to try it out!  His dad said it was okay, but warned him that it could make him feel uncomfortable.

Sure enough, when Toby touched the battery to a small pebble, it disappeared! Toby was so surprised he stumbled back, his face full of wonder. But just then, something even more amazing happened. A large pebble appeared in Toby's hand! His dad smiled softly and said, "Magic can be a wonderful thing."

Sara and Ben like to play with cardboard. They cut and color and glue it to make different things. One day, they make a big cardboard house with a door and windows. They put pillows and toys inside and pretend to live there.

Mom comes to see what they are doing. She smiles and says they are very clever. She also says it is almost time for lunch. She asks them what they want to eat. Sara says she wants cheese and Ben says he wants ham. Mom says okay and goes to the kitchen.

Sara and Ben keep playing in their cardboard house. They make up stories and act them out. They have a lot of fun. Then, Sara remembers something. She says to Ben, "I have a surprise for you. I made you something." She goes to a corner of the house and gets a small cardboard box. She gives it to Ben and says, "Open it."

Ben opens the box and sees a picture of a dinosaur. He likes dinosaurs a lot. He is very happy and says, "Wow, thank you, Sara. This is awesome. How did you make it?" Sara says, "I used crayons and scissors and glue. I saw a dinosaur book in the library and I copied it. I wanted to give it to you for your birthday, but I forgot to mention it."

Ben hugs Sara and says, "You are the best sister ever. This is the best birthday present ever. I love you." Sara says, "I love you too. Happy birthday, Ben." They put the picture on the wall of their cardboard house and admire it. They hear Mom calling them for lunch. They get out of their house and run to the kitchen. They are hungry and excited. They tell Mom about their cardboard house and their surprise. Mom says she is proud of them and happy for them. She gives them cheese and ham sandwiches and juice. They eat and talk and laugh. They have a good day.

Lily and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But Lily and Ben liked the gorilla best. The gorilla was big and black and had a funny face.

"Hello, gorilla!" Lily said, waving her hand. "Do you want to play with us?"

The gorilla looked at Lily and Ben and made a loud noise. He sounded happy. He picked up a banana and peeled it. He ate the banana and smacked his lips.

"Mmm, delicious!" the gorilla said. "Do you want some?"

Lily and Ben laughed. They had never heard a gorilla talk before. They nodded and said yes. The gorilla threw them another banana. Lily and Ben caught it and peeled it. They ate the banana and smacked their lips.

"Mmm, delicious!" Lily and Ben said. "Thank you, gorilla!"

The gorilla smiled and nodded. He threw them another banana. Lily and Ben shared it with Mom and Dad. They all enjoyed the banana and thanked the gorilla. The gorilla waved goodbye and went to sleep. Lily and Ben said goodbye and went to see the other animals. They had a fun day at the zoo.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big sign that said "Do not pick the flowers". Lily wanted to pick a flower for her mom. She thought the sign was bossy.

"Come on, Ben, let's pick a flower. The sign is silly. Mom will like it," she said.

"No, Lily, we have to listen to the sign. It is a rule. If we break the rule, we will be in trouble," Ben said.

Lily did not care. She ran to the flower bed and picked a yellow flower. She smelled it and smiled. Ben followed her and shook his head.

Suddenly, Lily sneezed. She sneezed again and again. The flower made her nose tickle. She dropped the flower and rubbed her nose.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.

"No, I'm not okay. The flower made me sneeze. It hurts. I don't like the flower. I'm sorry, Ben. You were right. We should have listened to the sign," Lily said.

Ben hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. Let's go back to the slide. Maybe that will make you feel better."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Ben. Thank you. You are a good friend. Next time, I will listen to the sign. And to you."

Sara liked to write. She wrote on paper, on walls, on books, on anything she could find. She used pens, pencils, crayons, markers, and sometimes even her fingers. She wrote her name, her family's names, her friends' names, and words she learned at school. She wrote big and small, neat and messy, colorful and plain. She wrote every day.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom. She saw a vendor who sold ice cream. She wanted ice cream, so she asked her mom.

"Mom, can I have ice cream, please?"

"Not now, Sara. You just had lunch. Maybe later, okay?"

Sara was not happy. She was stubborn. She wanted ice cream now. She saw a big sign on the vendor's cart. It had words and pictures of ice cream. She had an idea. She took a marker from her pocket and ran to the sign. She started to write on it.

She wrote "Sara" and "ice cream" and drew a smiley face. She thought it was pretty.

The vendor saw her. He was angry. He shouted at her.

"Hey, stop that! What are you doing? You are ruining my sign!"

He ran to her and took the marker from her hand. He looked at the sign and frowned. He said to her mom.

"Look what your daughter did! She wrote on my sign! She has to pay for it!"

Sara's mom was shocked. She apologized to the vendor. She said to Sara.

"Sara, that was very naughty. You can't write on other people's things. That is not nice. You have to say sorry to the vendor and help him clean the sign."

Sara felt bad. She realized she made a mistake. She said sorry to the vendor and helped him clean the sign. She used a wet cloth and rubbed the marker off. It took a long time.

The vendor was still upset, but he accepted her apology. He said to her.

"Next time, don't write on my sign, okay? If you want ice cream, you have to ask nicely and pay for it."

Sara nodded. She learned her lesson. She said to him.

"Okay, I won't write on your sign again. Can I have ice cream now, please?"

The vendor smiled. He said to her.

"Sure, you can have ice cream now. What flavor do you want?"

Sara smiled back. She said to him.

"Chocolate, please."

The vendor gave her a chocolate ice cream cone. She thanked him and licked it. It was yummy.

She said to her mom.

"Mom, I'm sorry I wrote on the sign. I won't do it again. I love you."

Her mom hugged her and said.

"I love you too, Sara. I'm glad you said sorry and helped the vendor. That was very good of you. Now, let's enjoy our ice cream and have fun at the park."

They ate their ice cream and played at the park. Sara was happy. She still liked to write, but she knew where and when to write. She was a good girl.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He was 3 years old. He was very curious and he wanted to explore the world around him. One day, he wanted to climb something. So he found a big tree and started to climb it. He climbed higher and higher until he reached the highest number of branches. He was so proud of himself.

But then, something happened. He realised he was stuck! He was very embarrassed. He called for help but nobody was there. He tried to climb down, but he was too scared to move.

After a while, a kind lady came to help him. She helped him to climb down. When they got to the bottom, they had a big hug and Tim thanked her. He promised to himself that he would never climb so high again.

Once upon a time, there was a poor boy named Timmy. He lived in a small village with his family. They didn't have much food to eat and Timmy was always hungry. One day, Timmy's parents decided to take him on a journey to find an oasis. An oasis is a place in the desert where there is water and food.

Timmy was very excited to go on this journey. They walked for many days and nights, and finally, they found the oasis. Timmy was so happy to see all the water and trees with fruits. He ate until he was full and drank until he was no longer thirsty. Timmy's parents were happy too, they decided to stay at the oasis for a while and rest.

After a few days, Timmy's family decided to go back home. They filled their bags with fruits and water from the oasis. Timmy was sad to leave, but he knew he would always remember the oasis and the fun times he had there.

The duck packed a tight bag full of decorations. She was so excited that she went to the surprise party really early.

When she arrived, her friends were nowhere to be seen. She was confused and called out to them, but no one answered. 

Suddenly another duck showed up! She asked if the duck was here to organize the surprise party. The duck started to get suspicious, but the other duck said she knew all about it. 

The duck trusted her, but she soon realized the party had been a trick. The other duck had just been waiting to surprise her instead. 

The duck was very disappointed and ran away in tears. The other duck only laughed - it had been a bad plan all along!

"Look, Ben, they are so good!" Lily says. "They have nice costumes and funny hats."

"Yes, they are fun," Ben says. "Can we go on the stage too?"

Lily and Ben run to the stage. They climb the steps and join the group. They try to sing and dance like the other kids. But they do not know the words or the moves. They bump into the other kids and knock down their hats. The other kids get angry.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mark. One day, Mark wanted to take a nap. But his mum couldn't find his blankie anywhere.

One day, a lizard was walking through the forest. He was feeling a bit grumpy. Suddenly, he heard a noise. He guessed it was someone talking. He looked around and he saw a three year old girl. She waved at him and said hello. The lizard was surprised. He waved his tail and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very bad. She didn't listen to her mom all the time and always got into trouble. So, her mom decided to punish her.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Andrew. He was three years old and he loved going on adventures. One day, he decided to go explore a trail he had never seen before. He picked up his backpack and set off.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. Lucy loved to go to the park and fly her kite. One day, she was flying her kite when she found something on the ground. She picked it up and saw it was a little blouse. Lucy decided to carry it home with her.

So, the next morning, Lucy went back to the park with the blouse. Suddenly, a black cat appeared and started to meow loudly. Lucy was scared and ran away. Then she realized she had left the blouse behind. When she went back to get it, the blouse was gone.

When Lucy got home, she was sad. Where had the blouse gone? Her mom was angry and said it had probably been taken away by a thief. Lucy was very upset and couldn't stop thinking about the blouse.

The next day, the little blouse was found in the park. It was dead. Poor Lucy! The blouse had been taken away by a thief and she never got to take it back home. This was a sad ending for Lucy and the little blouse!

Ben was a brave and curious boy. Every day he wanted to do something new. Every day he asked his parents to do something different.

Today was no different. Ben asked, "Mommy, can I do something with the oven?"

His mom said, "No, Ben. It's dangerous. You need to be careful around the oven."

Ben was a bit disappointed, but he soon forgot about it and played with his toy cars. He felt very happy and content.

Hours later, after dinner, Ben was getting ready for bed when he saw a nasty smell coming from the oven. He opened the oven and saw a pile of ashes inside. His face turned miserable.

It turned out that Ben had forgotten to turn off the oven. Without him noticing, the oven had been on all day, burning everything inside. His parents had been right - Ben should have been careful around the oven.

Once upon a time there was a happy lady who loved to jump. Whenever she felt excited or enthusiastic, the lady would jump up and down with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite lamp in her room that she loved to turn on every night. One day, her little brother wanted to play with the lamp, but Lily refused to let him. "No, no, no!" she said. "This is my lamp and I don't want you to touch it."

From that day on, Lily and her brother took turns playing with the lamp and they both loved it very much. They were never jealous of each other again and they always shared their toys with each other.

Once there was a young girl named Lily. She liked to play with her doll near the big church. One day, she lost her doll and felt very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest behind her house. One day, she found a map that led to a treasure. She was so excited and followed the map.

Once upon a time, there was a happy monkey named Max. Max lived on an island with lots of trees and bananas. One day, Max went for a walk and found a big coconut. Once upon a time, there was a little silver bunny. He was sad because he had no one to play with. But then, one day, he met a little girl. She was very kind, and she smiled at the bunny and said "Hello, Bunny!"

Anna and Ben wanted to help Mom and Dad decorate the big tree for Christmas. They saw many shiny and pretty things in a big box. Mom and Dad said they were ornaments and they could hang them on the tree.

But they wanted to put some ornaments on the higher branches too. They saw an enormous ornament in the box. It was a star. It was gold and sparkly. They wanted to put it on the top of the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a twin named Sam and Sue. They were very nice and generous with each other. They always shared their things and helped each other with whatever they needed.

Imagine there was a perfect waffle. It was huge and round with lots of little holes. It smelled like butter and there were syrup spots all around it. It was so delicious, it was like it was baked by the best baker ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside and peek at the birds in the trees. One day, Timmy's friend told him a joke that made him laugh so hard he fell off his swing. Timmy didn't realize that he had left his toy truck in the grass.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and helpful boy named John. Today, John wanted to help his mom pick some cherries, so he went to the cherry tree in his backyard.

When the apron was full, John and his mom smiled at each other. His mom hugged him and said, "Thank you for your help, John. I'm so proud of you!" John smiled and said, "You're welcome, mom. I'm happy to help."

Once upon a time there lived a little boy. He was only three-years-old and he loved adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a friend named Max who was very brave. One day, they went to the park to play. They went on the swings and the slide. Once upon a time, there was a famous lamp living in the town. The lamp was known by everyone, even the oldest man in the town could still remember it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys in the park. One day, she saw a group of birds eating bread crumbs on the ground. She wanted to play with them too, but they flew away when she got too close.

Suddenly, a police car drove by with its sirens blaring. The loud noise scared Lily and she started to cry. A kind police officer came over and asked her what was wrong. Lily told him about the birds and how they scattered away.

The police officer smiled and said, "Don't worry, we'll find them for you." He asked his partner to help look for the birds. After a few minutes, they found the birds and brought them back to Lily. She was so happy that she gave the police officers a tight hug. From that day on, Lily knew she could always count on the police to help her when she needed it.

One day, Little Miss Bunny was walking in the woods. She was looking for something sweet to eat. Suddenly, she heard a sharp cry in the distance. She stopped and was curious. She decided to follow the sound.

Little Miss Bunny walked through the trees until she saw an office in a clearing. She could tell it was somebody's office because it had a big window with a desk and a chair.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden and watch the plants grow. One day, she found a bean and decided to plant it in the ground.

Her mom came over and was also surprised to see how big the plant had become. "Wow, Lily! Your bean plant is huge! You did a great job taking care of it," she said.

George and his mom were discussing what to do with his old mattress.

"What should we do with this mattress, George?" His mom asked.

"It's all dirty and old, let's get a new one", George replied. 

"Well, we can't just throw it away, it still has life in it. Maybe we can clean it up", his mom said.

"Let's clean it up!", George shouted.

His mom went and got a bucket of soapy water and a soft brush. She scrubbed the mattress until it was nice and clean.

Together, George and his mom brought the mattress back into his bedroom and put the clean sheets back on.

Now the mattress was fresh and comfy. George smiled and thanked his mom. 

"Thanks for helping me make my bed comfy again!", he said. 

His mom smiled back and said, "Anytime, George. You should always take good care of your mattress!"

Once upon a time there was a party. All the people were very excited. They were all wearing their best clothes and were very happy.

The little girl felt much better and the warmth of her mum's hug made her stop crying.

The little girl had a very good time and she felt so much better now. She knew that with a little love and lots of hugs we can always make everything better.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat yummy cookies. One day, Timmy's mom made a big batch of cookies. Timmy was so happy! He ate one cookie, then another, and another. 

Soon, Timmy's tummy was full. He wanted to share his cookies with his friends. So, Timmy asked his mom to load some cookies into a big bag. Then, Timmy went to his friend's house and gave him the bag of cookies. 

Timmy's friend was so happy! He ate a cookie and said, "These cookies are yummy! Can we test how many we can eat?" Timmy smiled and said, "Sure!" They had a fun time testing how many cookies they could eat. In the end, they both ate too many cookies and had to take a nap. The end.

Once there was a loyal dog called Max. Every day he would wait for his owner to come outside to play. But one day Max noticed a parade.

The parade filled the street with colourful flags, music and happy people. Max barked excitedly and joined in the parade. He ran alongside the people, wagging his tail and playing with a red balloon.

When the parade ended, Max found his owner again. His owner was smiling and said, "I'm glad you enjoyed the parade, Max! You're such a loyal dog."

Max wagged his tail and barked excitingly. The parade had been lots of fun and he couldn't wait for the next one.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to draw. They had many colors and papers to make pictures. One day, they found a big eraser in the art room. It was white and soft and could erase anything.

"Wow, this is a great eraser!" Ben said. "Let's use it for our drawings."

"OK, but we have to share it," Lily said. "It is not ours, we have to give it back later."

They took the eraser and started to draw. Ben drew a car, Lily drew a flower. They used the eraser to fix their mistakes. They had fun with the eraser.

But then, Tom came in. He was a mean boy who liked to take things from others. He saw the eraser and wanted it.

"Hey, give me that eraser!" he said. "It is mine, I lost it yesterday."

Ben and Lily knew he was lying. They had never seen him with the eraser before. He was trying to trick them.

"No, it is not yours, it is from the art room," Ben said. "You are telling a fake story."

"I don't care, I want it now!" Tom said. He grabbed the eraser from Ben and ran away.

Ben and Lily were sad and angry. They wanted their eraser back. They followed Tom and saw him hiding behind a tree. He was laughing and playing with the eraser.

They decided to teach him a lesson. They found a rock that looked like the eraser. It was white and hard and could not erase anything. They sneaked behind Tom and swapped the rock for the eraser. Tom did not notice.

They ran back to the art room with the eraser. They were happy and proud. They finished their drawings and put the eraser back where they found it.

Tom came back later. He wanted to erase his drawing and make a new one. He tried to use the rock, but it did not work. It only scratched his paper and made a loud noise.

He realized he had been fooled. He felt stupid and ashamed. He learned that lying and stealing are bad. He wished he had been nice to Ben and Lily.

The end.

Moral: Honesty is the best policy. Don't take what is not yours. Share and be kind.

One day, a little boy was ready to go play in the park. He ran up to his mother and said thank you. His mother smiled and thanked him for giving her a hug. He was so excited to go!

One day, a new fish named Sparkle came to the sea. Sparkle was very pretty and shiny. Fin started to play with Sparkle and Ollie felt jealous. Ollie wanted to change and be shiny like Sparkle too. He said to Fin, "I want to be shiny like Sparkle."

Fin didn't want Ollie to change. He liked Ollie just the way he was. But Ollie didn't listen. He swam away to find a way to change himself. He found a shiny rock and rubbed it on his shell, hoping to become shiny like Sparkle.

But instead of becoming shiny, Ollie's shell became rough and dull. He felt very sad. He swam back to Fin and showed him his shell. Fin was sad too. They couldn't play together like before because Ollie's shell was too rough. Ollie wished he had never tried to change.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Cat. Cat was three years old and loved to eat soup.

John was feeling very worried. He was running down the street so fast that he couldn't see where he was going. Suddenly, he felt a hand on his shoulder. He quickly spun around and saw an old lady.

Her kids smiled and started to run around and giggle. They all waved as they scrambled out of the house.

On the way to their destination, Mom told the children a story. It was a story about a foolish man who wanted something, but kept putting it off. Despite all the warnings, he never did anything. 

"Don't be like that man," Mom said. "Not when it comes to your dreams. Wave goodbye to your fears and go for it!" 

The children all waved their arms in the air, feeling brave and excited. Mom smiled and knew they were ready for anything life threw at them. As they continued on their journey, the family was filled with an incredible feeling of joy and adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved lumber. She would spend her days running around and playing in the forest with the big trees. 

One day, while reading a book under the shade of one of the trees, she sneezed. Suddenly, a voice called out from the nearby woods.

"Who dares to sneeze so loud in my forest?!" bellowed the voice.

The little girl was afraid, so she said nothing. 

"Come out now, if you dare!" the voice continued.

The little girl stepped out of the tree's shade, and there before her was a large, proud lumberjack.

The lumberjack narrowed his eyes and grabbed his axe, then angrily said, "You have disturbed my forest and must pay!" 

The little girl was terrified and tried to run away, but the lumberjack was too fast. He caught her and cut all the trees in the forest, smashing them to pieces.

The little girl sadly watched as the last tree fell and her beloved forest disappeared. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but one day it started to rain. Lily's mom gave her a strong umbrella and said, "Don't forget to catch the raindrops with your umbrella!"

Lily ran outside and opened her umbrella. She watched as the raindrops fell onto her umbrella. Suddenly, she saw her friend Timmy walking by. "Hi Timmy!" she said. "Do you want to catch raindrops with me?"

Timmy smiled and said, "Yes, I want to catch raindrops too!" They both held their umbrellas high and tried to catch as many raindrops as they could. They laughed and had so much fun together.

When the rain stopped, Lily and Timmy said goodbye and went back home. Lily's mom asked her, "Did you have fun playing in the rain?" Lily replied, "Yes! Timmy and I caught lots of raindrops with our strong umbrellas!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Tina. She had a toy phone she liked to carry everywhere. Tina liked to mark things with the phone: phone books, notebooks, walls and sometimes even her siblings. 

One day she was walking with her mom and heard a spicy scent. She followed her nose and found a spice shop, with rows of jars filled with all sorts of spices. She asked her mom if she could buy some, and together they picked out a few. On the way back, Tina marked the shop's door with her phone!

Tina was so excited to show everyone at home what she had marked. She carefully placed the jars of spices on the table and proudly pointed to the shop's door, showing off her mark. Her siblings were so surprised and impressed by her mark!

Tina was so proud of her marking skills that she spent all day wanting to mark more and more things! She marked the walls in her room and other things around the house with her phone. 

It was a good day full of fun and learning. Tina had marked many things and tasted some new and spicy flavors!

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl who was playing in the garden. She loved to wander around, looking at the flowers, humming a sweet song.

Suddenly, she saw a dead bird in the grass. She was very sad. She started to cry.

Her father, who was watching from the window, went outside and said, "Don't worry sweetheart, I can help you fix this." He grabbed a rake and said, "Help me collect the leaves and we can give the little bird a proper burial."

The girl nodded and they started to rake together. They made a tiny hole in the ground and put the dead bird inside. The girl said her goodbyes and put a flower on top of the hole. 

Then, her dad put his arm around her and said, "Come on, let's go have a fun day. What do you say?"

The girl nodded again and they both smiled. Together, they went off to explore the garden, singing a happy song.

Once there was a girl who had a special box. Inside the box were three special things. The girl had the box for her birthday, and she liked it very much. 

Every night, the girl added something new to the box. She would pick something up from around the house and add it to the box. Sometimes it would be something small, like a little rock. Other times it would be something big, like a toy.

One day something special happened. The girl picked something up that was very expensive. It was so expensive that it couldn't be just any object. It was much more special. So she added it to the box, and it was the best thing in the box. 

The girl was so happy when she put the special item in the box that she wanted to show it to everyone. She wanted everyone to know how special it was. But it was only for her, and she treasured it always.

Tom and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They saw many things in the water, like fish and seaweed and rocks.

One day, they found a crab. It was small and red and had big claws. It was hiding under a shell. Tom wanted to touch it, but Lily was scared.

"Stay away, Tom!" Lily said. "The crab can pinch you!"

Tom did not listen. He reached for the crab. The crab saw Tom's hand and snapped its claw. Tom cried out and pulled his hand back. He had a red mark on his finger.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom said. "The crab hurt me!"

Mom and Dad heard Tom and came to see what happened. They saw the crab and the shell and Tom's finger. They hugged Tom and Lily and told them to be careful.

"Crabs are not toys, Tom," Mom said. "They are living things that need their space. They can pinch you if they feel threatened."

"Sorry, Mom," Tom said. "I just wanted to see the crab. It was not an ordinary crab. It was a special crab."

Lily nodded. She felt sorry for Tom and the crab. She said, "Maybe we can leave the crab alone and look for other things. There are many other things on the beach that are special too."

Tom agreed. He said, "OK, Lily. Let's go and find some more shells. Maybe we can find a starfish or a sand dollar."

They left the crab and the shell and went to explore the beach. They had fun and learned a lot. They did not bother the crab again. The crab was happy and stayed under the shell. It was an ordinary crab, but it was also a special crab.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a bell. Every day, she would take her bell outside and ring it. Everyone in the village would hear it and smile. Even the birds in the sky seemed to be singing along.

One day, the little girl's mommy said to her, "Go out and get some hay for the sheep."

The little girl beamed. She took her bell outside and got some hay. But then she noticed something strange--the flowers were all shriveled up. She was so ashamed! She had forgotten to ring her bell that day and the flowers were sad without it.

The little girl hurried home and told her mommy what she had done. Mommy said, "It's alright. The flowers will be happy if you ring the bell again tomorrow." 

The little girl took her bell out every day from then on and made sure to ring it. The flowers were happy, and the birds sang with joy. And the little girl was happy too.

Maisy loved ducks. She saw them every day in her backyard. She would run out of the house in delight when she saw the ducks. One day, she decided to go to the pond to feed them.

When Maisy arrived at the pond, she saw several ducks wading in the water. She was so excited and held out her hands full of breadcrumbs. The ducks paddled closer and began to eat the crumbs, one by one.

Maisy watched them happily. She whispered, "I love you ducks". The ducks made peaceful sounds, as if they were trying to tell her they loved her too.

Maisy and the ducks stayed together for a while, until it was time for Maisy to go home. Just before she left, she called out to the ducks "Bye! I'll come back soon!". The ducks replied with a quack, as if they were telling her they would be there, waiting.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary man. He was walking in a park and he saw something very special - a peach tree! He picked a peach off the tree and smelled it, and it smelt so sweet. He ate the peach, and he felt so happy. 

He was just about to leave, when something special happened - a magical bird arrived from the sky, with a twinkle in its eye! The bird grabbed the peach out of the man's hands, and flew away with it. 

The man was so surprised that he quickly followed the bird. He followed the bird for many days, until finally the bird stopped at a fair. The man watched from afar as the bird put the peach onto a stall, and it was sold to a little girl. She smiled and danced around with joy. 

The man was so happy for the little girl, and he knew that the peach was special. Even though it was just an ordinary peach, it had made two people very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little purple dog named Spot. Spot was walking in the cold park. He started to shiver because it was very cold. He wanted to find a warm place to rest.

Spot saw a big cross in the park. He thought that maybe the cross could help him stay warm. But when he got close to the cross, he met a mean cat. The cat did not want Spot to be near the cross.

Spot and the cat started to fight. They both wanted the warm cross. But then, they saw a little girl with a warm blanket. The girl saw them shivering and felt sad. She put the blanket on Spot and the cat. They stopped fighting and became friends. They all stayed warm together under the blanket.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was 3 years old and she was not happy. She hated her wallet. It was big and black and it made noises when she walked. It was frustrating!

Every day, the little girl would take the wallet with her. But she always wished she didn't have to.

One day, the little girl's mommy noticed her daughter was not happy. Her mommy had an idea. She gave the little girl a surprise. It was a brand new wallet!

The little girl was so excited. It was green and soft, and it was so small! It fit in her pocket! She was so happy and no longer frustrated.

The little girl could go places without her old, noisy wallet. She was so thankful. She never had to hate her wallet again.

One day, a little girl named Sally went to the park with her mom and baby brother. The sun was shining and it was the perfect day to play outside. Sally brought her favorite toy, a big red ball, to play with at the park.

Sally saw another little girl named Lucy playing with her own toy, a pretty blue doll. Sally wanted to play with the doll, so she asked Lucy, "Can I play with your doll, please?" Lucy said, "Yes, if you let me play with your ball." So, they decided to share their toys and play together.

Sally and Lucy played and shared their toys all day long. They had so much fun that they became best friends. Even the baby brother was happy, watching them play and share. At the end of the day, they all went home with big smiles on their faces, knowing they had the perfect day at the park.

Bugs was a 3 year old girl. She was very excited to visit her grandma. She hopped up to her door, opened it, and ran inside.

"Grandma!" Bugs said, "What are we going to do today?"

"I have a great surprise for you! We're going to organize your new parrot. It'll be so much fun. I already bought you a delicious food for it."

Bugs clapped her hands together. "Yay," she said. She ran over to Grandma and hugged her.

Grandma helped Bugs organize the parrot's cage. They swept out the cage, put in fresh food, and set up the perch.

Bugs held up the delicious food and waved a spoon at the parrot. All of a sudden it flew right into the cage!

Bugs gasped. She was so excited she had trouble calming down. "Can we organize a new game for the parrot now?" she asked her Grandma.

Grandma laughed. "Of course, my little one," she said. Together they got to work organizing all kinds of new games for the parrot. 

Bugs spent the whole day playing and organizing games with her new parrot. She was so happy; it was the best day ever.

Little Dan was so excited for his first day at school. He carried his backpack so tight, he was determined not to forget anything. As he walked out of the house he noticed a puddle near the entrance. He hopped over the puddle, giggling to himself.

When he arrived at school, he put his backpack on the table and waited for the bell to ring. He watched as the other children ran and played. Suddenly, he noticed the same puddle from outside. It had somehow followed him!

Little Dan hopped over the puddle again. He knew there was no way it could carry him, so he just stared and watched. The other children continued to play, but Little Dan just stayed in one place, studying the curious puddle. 

The bell suddenly rang, and the children went to their classes. Little Dan's eyes were still focused on the puddle, wanting to get a closer look. He asked his teacher if he could stay and investigate the mysterious puddle. With permission granted, Little Dan carried on, analyzing the puddle with curiosity and joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dress up in pretty clothes. One day, her mommy gave her a box of shiny jewelry to play with. Lily was so happy and put on a necklace and some bracelets.

But then, Lily got confused because she didn't know which piece of jewelry to wear next. So, she decided to test each one by trying them on and looking in the mirror. She finally found the perfect combination of jewelry to wear.

Lily felt so pretty and happy with her jewelry. She showed her mommy and daddy and they said she looked beautiful. From that day on, Lily loved to wear her jewelry and test out new combinations.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to read books, especially funny ones. One day, he found a funny novel at the library and borrowed it.

Timmy was so excited to read the novel that he forgot to cover it when he went outside to play. Suddenly, it started to rain and the novel got wet. Timmy was very sad because he couldn't read the novel anymore.

Timmy learned an important lesson that day. He realized that he needed to cover his things when he wasn't using them to keep them safe. From then on, Timmy always covered his things and never lost or damaged them again.

Mum had lots of work to do. She wanted to cut apples, carrots and onions for dinner. She picked up the knife and started to cut quickly. The weather outside was nice and sunny. Mum put the clean vegetables in a bowl. 

Dad was outside in the garden. He was cutting the grass with a loud mower. He was very careful and always made the grass look clean and neat. 

After dinner, mum and Dad went out for a walk in the fresh air. The weather was warm and sunny, it was a perfect day. They enjoyed watching the birds and the bees flying around in the sky. Soon it was time to go home. 

When they got home, Mum and Dad were very tired. They both went to bed and had a good sleep. What a lovely day it had been!

Once there was a silly little girl. She loved to drink from her cup. She took big drinks and didn't stop until the cup was empty!

One day, the girl was listening to her mommy. But she could not hear well. She started to feel very sad.

Her mom noticed she was not happy so she took the girl to the doctor. The doctor said she needed special ear drops. He gave her a special bottle to keep in her pocket.

Every morning and night, the girl would take a few drops in her ear. Soon, she could hear much better!

She was so happy that she ran and gave her mommy a big hug. Then she grabbed her cup and had a big drink to celebrate!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but it was very hot outside. She put on her uniform and went outside to play with her friends. 

They decided to play a game of hide-and-seek, but one of her friends was missing. They looked all over for her, but they couldn't find her. Lily thought hard about how to solve the problem. 

Finally, she had an idea! She remembered her friend's favorite hiding spot in the treehouse. They all ran to the treehouse and found her friend hiding inside. They were so happy to have solved the problem and continue playing in the hot sun.

Once upon a time, there was a duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond all day long. One day, Ducky saw a big storm coming. Ducky realized that he needed to find a safe place to hide. He looked around and saw a big tree with a hole in it. Ducky quickly swam over to the tree and crawled inside the hole.

As the storm raged on, Ducky was safe and dry inside the tree. He was so happy that he had found a safe place to hide. After the storm passed, Ducky crawled out of the tree and saw that many of his friends were hurt. They had not been as flexible as Ducky and had not found a safe place to hide during the storm.

Ducky realized that it was important to always be prepared and to find a safe place to hide during a storm. He told all his friends about the tree with the hole and they all learned to be more flexible like Ducky. From that day on, all the ducks in the pond were prepared for any storm that might come their way.

Bobbie was tired. She yawned, stretch her arms and legs, and sat up in bed.

"It's the morning, Bobbie," said Mom. 

"Yay!" said Bobbie. She hopped out of bed and ran outside.

The sun was warm, and the breeze gentle. The grass was soft and green beneath her toes. It was a beautiful day in the new season.

Bobbie ran and played for a long time. At last, though, she was very tired. She yawned, sitting down in the grass.

"It was a tough day, Bobbie," said Mom, coming to sit beside her. 

Ready for bed, Bobbie nodded and yawned, snuggling up close to Mom. Together they counted stars until the moon was high and then they walked inside. 

Bobbie yawned again and went to bed, asleep in a moment.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in a jungle. He liked to roar very loudly to show how strong he was. One day, he saw a little dancer who was dancing in the jungle. The lion was amazed by her dance and wanted to be her friend. 

But the little dancer was very spoiled and didn't want to be friends with the lion. She thought she was too good for him. The lion was sad, but he didn't give up. He practiced his roar and tried to impress the little dancer. 

Finally, the little dancer saw how hard the lion was trying and realized that he was a good friend. She danced with him and they became the best of friends. From that day on, the lion would roar and the little dancer would dance, and they would have fun together in the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to play with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lucy's mom came into her room and said, "Lucy, let's add some pretty beads to your dolls' string necklaces to make them even more attractive!" 

Lucy was excited and said, "Yes please, Mommy!" They went to the store and picked out colorful beads. Lucy's mom showed her how to add the beads to the string and they worked together to make beautiful necklaces for Lucy's dolls. 

When they finished, Lucy said, "Thank you, Mommy! My dolls look so attractive now with their new necklaces." Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lucy. I'm glad you like them." Lucy hugged her mom and played with her dolls happily ever after.

Today was a sunny day and the sun was shining brightly. It shined through the windows and it was very warm. Henry was a young boy of three. He had a lot of toys to play with. He could play with cars, blocks, and even his own little dishwasher.

One day, Henry decided he wanted to take his dishwasher outside. He dragged it all the way outside and put it in a patch of rough grass. He started to load it up with leaves, sticks, and stones. As the dishwasher started to get full, Henry opened up the door and started to turn it on.

The dishwasher made a loud noise as it started up. The sun shined down on the dishwasher and made it shine in the grass. Henry grabbed some soap and started putting it into the dishwasher. As it swirled around in the spinning water, Henry was delighted to watch and marvel at the bubbles that were created.

Finally, after a few more tries the dishwasher was loaded up with the objects Henry put in and the water was ready. Henry smiled with joy as he watched his dishwasher come to life, now that it shined in the sun outside.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so proud of herself because she had learned to do something very special in school. Everyday she went to the gym to practice with all the other kids.

Every night when she got home, she showed her mom a secret. She would rub her hands together and then spread her palms wide apart. She was so proud that she could make the sparkles appear! She had learned how to do it in the gym.

Every night before bed, the little girl would practice her sparkles. She wanted to get better and better each day. She was so proud of how well she was doing!

Soon enough she was making twinkles and glitters, too. Her roommates at school were also impressed with her skills. The little girl was so proudâ€”she just kept getting better and better.

The end.

One day, a little girl named Sally was walking along the beach. She noticed the beautiful red tide in the water. She wanted to search and see what was in the water. So she got down on her stomach and started looking in the water. She could see lots of different animals swimming and playing in the red tide. She saw crabs and fishes, and she even saw a tiny starfish! She was so excited that she started clapping her hands and giggling. She watched the animals for a while longer until the tide started to go away. Sally said goodbye to the animals and started to walk back home. She was so happy she got to search in the red tide!

Anna and Ben were very happy. They were going to the festival with Mom and Dad. The festival had many fun things. There were balloons, games, music, and food. Anna and Ben wanted to try everything.

They saw a big tent with a sign that said "Lemonade". Anna and Ben loved lemonade. They ran to the tent and asked for a cup. Mom and Dad paid the man and gave them the cups. Anna and Ben took a big sip.

But the lemonade was not sweet. It was bitter. It made their faces twist and their tongues hurt. Anna and Ben did not like the bitter lemonade. They spit it out and yelled.

"Yuck! This is bad lemonade! It is bitter! We want sweet lemonade!"

Mom and Dad heard them yell. They came to the tent and tasted the lemonade. They agreed that it was bitter. They asked the man why the lemonade was bitter. The man said he ran out of sugar and used salt instead.

Mom and Dad were angry. They told the man that he should not sell bitter lemonade. They asked for their money back. The man said he was sorry and gave them their money back.

Anna and Ben threw away their cups and wiped their mouths. They did not want to drink bitter lemonade again. They wanted to find something else to enjoy at the festival. They saw a big truck with a sign that said "Ice Cream". Anna and Ben smiled. They loved ice cream. They ran to the truck and asked for a cone. Mom and Dad paid the lady and gave them the cones. Anna and Ben took a big lick.

The ice cream was sweet. It made their faces happy and their tongues cool. Anna and Ben liked the sweet ice cream. They licked and smiled.

"Mmm! This is good ice cream! It is sweet! We like sweet ice cream!"

Mom and Dad saw them smile. They came to the truck and tasted the ice cream. They agreed that it was sweet. They thanked the lady for the ice cream. The lady said she was glad they liked it.

Anna and Ben finished their cones and wiped their hands. They wanted to see more of the festival. They saw a big stage with a sign that said "Clowns". Anna and Ben laughed. They loved clowns. They ran to the stage and sat on the grass. Mom and Dad followed them and sat next to them. The clowns came out and did funny tricks. They made balloons, jokes, music, and faces. Anna and Ben giggled and clapped.

"Ha ha! This is fun! We love clowns!"

The end.

Tom and Lily went to the lake with Mom and Dad. They wanted to swim and play in the water. They had a big bag with clothes and toys and snacks. Mom said they had to unpack the bag and put everything in the right place.

Tom and Lily helped Mom unpack the bag. They took out the swimsuits and the towels and the sunscreen. They put them on a big blanket near the water. They took out the toys and the books and the balls. They put them on another blanket under a tree. They took out the snacks and the drinks and the plates. They put them in a cooler next to the car.

"Good job, Tom and Lily!" Mom said. "Now we can have fun at the lake!"

Tom and Lily ran to the water. They splashed and swam and laughed. They saw colorful fish and shells and rocks. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Lily felt something sting her arm. She looked and saw a red bump. She cried and ran to Mom.

"Ow, ow, ow! Mom, it hurts!" Lily said.

Mom looked at Lily's arm. She saw a mosquito flying away.

"Oh, no, Lily. A mosquito bit you. I'm sorry, sweetie. Let me put some cream on it. It will make it feel better." Mom said.

Mom took out some cream from the bag and rubbed it on Lily's arm. She hugged Lily and kissed her.

"There, there. It's okay, Lily. The mosquito is gone. The cream will help. Do you want to go back to the water?" Mom asked.

Lily nodded. She felt better. She smiled and hugged Mom.

"Thank you, Mom. I love you." Lily said.

"I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go back to the water. Tom is waiting for us." Mom said.

Tom and Lily went back to the water. They played with Mom and Dad. They forgot about the mosquito. They had a wonderful day at the lake.

Once upon a time there was a family that lived in a house. Every day, the family would cook a delicious dinner. 

One day, the parents said to the 3 year old child, "It's time to eat dinner. Just put everything in order." 

The child was delighted, as this was their favorite dinner. So the child started putting the food in order on the table. Every food smelled so delicious and looked so yummy.

Suddenly, there was a strange smell coming from the corner. The child went to have a look and found a plate full of vegetables that were beginning to rot. The child said in a worried voice, "It's no good. The vegetables have started to rot!" 

The parents heard this and said, "Don't worry! Let's just throw away the vegetables and eat the other delicious foods." 

So the child happily threw away the vegetables and enjoyed the delicious dinner. Everyone was happy, and they lived happily ever after.

Tim was a boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many toys, like cars, balls, and blocks. He played with them every day, and he did not like to share them with anyone. He did not want to let his sister, Lily, or his friends, Sam and Mia, touch his toys.

One day, his mom made a snack for him and his sister. She cut some apples and cheese, and put them on a plate. She called Tim and Lily to the kitchen, and said, "Come and eat your snack, children. It is good for you, and it will make you strong."

Lily ran to the kitchen, and said, "Thank you, mom. I love apples and cheese." She took a piece of each, and sat at the table. She smiled, and ate her snack.

Tim did not run to the kitchen. He did not say thank you. He did not love apples and cheese. He said, "No, mom. I do not want a snack. I want to play with my toys." He refused to eat his snack, and stayed in his room.

Mom was sad, and said, "Tim, you need to eat your snack. It is not good to skip your snack. You will be hungry, and you will not be strong. Please, come and eat your snack."

Tim did not listen to his mom. He said, "No, mom. I do not need a snack. I am not hungry, and I am strong. I have my toys, and they are enough for me." He refused to eat his snack, and played with his toys.

Later, Sam and Mia came to visit Tim and Lily. They wanted to play with them, and have fun. Lily was happy, and said, "Hi, Sam and Mia. Do you want to play with me? I have some toys we can share, and we can also play outside."

Sam and Mia said, "Yes, Lily. We want to play with you. You are very nice, and you have nice toys. We can also play outside, and run and jump."

They went to Lily's room, and saw her toys. They saw some dolls, some books, and some puzzles. They said, "Wow, Lily. You have cool toys. Can we play with them?"

Lily said, "Sure, Sam and Mia. You can play with them. We can take turns, and have fun. I also have some snack left, if you are hungry. Do you want some apples and cheese?"

Sam and Mia said, "Yes, Lily. We are hungry, and we love apples and cheese. Thank you for sharing your snack with us. You are very kind, and you are strong."

They took some apples and cheese, and ate them. They smiled, and said, "Mmm, this is yummy. This snack is good for us, and it makes us strong."

They played with Lily's toys, and had fun. They took turns, and helped each other. They laughed, and said, "Lily, you are a good friend. We like to play with you."

They also went outside, and played in the yard. They ran and jumped, and played tag and hide and seek. They had more fun, and said, "Lily, you are very fast and smart. You are strong."

Tim heard them from his room. He was bored, and lonely. He did not have fun, and he did not have friends. He only had his toys, and they did not talk to him. He was hungry, and weak. He did not eat his snack, and he did not play outside. He said, "I wish I had some snack, and some friends. I wish I was strong."

He went to the kitchen, and saw the empty plate. He saw the crumbs of apples and cheese, and the napkins. He said, "Oh, no. There is no snack left. Mom was right. I should have eaten my snack. It was good for me, and it would have made me strong."

He went to the yard, and saw Lily, Sam, and Mia. He saw them playing, and having fun. He saw them smiling, and laughing. He said, "Oh, no. They are having fun, and they are friends. They are nice, and they are strong. I want to play with them, and be their friend."

He ran to them, and said, "Hi, Lily, Sam, and Mia. Can I play with you? I have some toys we can share, and we can also play outside."

Lily, Sam, and Mia looked at him, and said, "Hi, Tim. We are glad you came. You can play with us, and be our friend. You have nice toys, and we can also play outside."

Once upon a time, there was an unhappy elderly ostrich. His name was Ollie. Ollie was older than all the other ostriches, so he was always alone. He worried a lot because he wanted to feel loved like the other birds.

One day, Ollie went for a walk. He saw a little girl with her parents. She was about three years old and had beautiful blonde curls. Ollie was filled with excitement and he ran over to say hello.

The little girl was so happy when she saw Ollie. She began to pet him and told him stories. Everyone around them was watching in amazement. Ollie felt so relaxed and loved.

From that day on, Ollie and the little girl remained friends. Whenever Ollie was feeling lonely, the little girl was there to make him feel happy again. He never had to worry anymore!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop and play in the grass. One day, Benny saw his friend Lucy playing with a new machine. Benny asked, "What is that machine?"

Lucy replied, "It's a toy car. Do you want to play with it?"

Benny said, "Yes, please!" and hopped over to play with Lucy and the toy car. But then, Benny's other friend, Sammy, came over and saw Benny playing with the toy car. Sammy felt jealous and said, "I want to play with the toy car too!"

Lucy said, "Okay, we can all play together." So, Benny, Lucy, and Sammy took turns playing with the toy car and had a lot of fun. Benny was happy that he got to play with his friends and the new machine.

John was playing in the park. He heard a noise and looked to see what it was. He saw a little bird with an injured wing and a bandage around it. John wanted to help the bird. He got some soft leaves and put them near the bird so it could rest. He was careful to not scare the bird away. 

The little bird stayed and even started to eat the leaves that John had given it. After a while, the bird was feeling much better. John heard the bird sing and it was a peaceful sound. He knew then that the bird was all healed. 

John picked up the bird and carefully placed it in a tree. He watched as the bird flew away, happy and healthy. John smiled to himself and waved goodbye.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play soccer with other kids. They have a big game today. They want to win the trophy.

They run and kick the ball. They try hard. The other team is good too. The game is close. Tom and Lily are tired.

"Come on, Lily, we can do it!" Tom says. He passes the ball to Lily. Lily sees a chance. She shoots the ball. It goes in the goal. They score!

Tom and Lily are happy. They hug and jump. The whistle blows. The game is over. They win the trophy!

They hold the trophy high. They smile. The other kids clap and cheer. It is loud. Tom and Lily are proud.

They care for each other. They are good friends. They share the trophy. They have fun. They love soccer.

Lily was a 3 year old girl who loved playing in the park near her house. One day, as she was playing with her friends, a magical rabbit hopped over. He said hello in a friendly manner and introduced himself. His name was Sugar. 

Lily was very excited to meet him and asked what he was doing there. He told them that he wanted to show them a new kind of game. 

The magical rabbit showed them a game called "Pass the Sugar". He asked each one of them to introduce themselves and then the rabbit spoiled them with a handful of sugar for each of them. Together, they had so much fun playing the game and sharing the sugar. 

At the end of the day, the magical Rabbit said his goodbyes and went on his way. Lily, who had so much fun playing the game, was so sad to see him go. She waved goodbye as he hopped off and promised to herself that she would come back with her friends to play again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a kitten named Mittens. Mittens was very cool, with soft fur and bright eyes. Lily loved to play with Mittens and cuddle him.

One day, Mittens got very sick. Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do. Her mommy told her to pray for Mittens to get better. So, Lily closed her eyes and prayed for Mittens to feel better soon.

The next day, Mittens was feeling much better! He was running around and playing with Lily again. Lily was so happy and thanked God for answering her prayer. From that day on, Lily made sure to pray every night for Mittens and for all the other animals in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a large train. It had big wheels and many carts. Every day, it went all around town. One day, it stopped in the station, and a little boy stepped on board. He wanted to ride the train. When the train started moving, he kissed his mom goodbye.

The train moved very fast. Soon it was going so fast, it sped out of town into the countryside. The boy thought, â€œIâ€™ll find the way home,â€ but he couldnâ€™t. He kept riding and riding, and he was so very far from home.

Eventually, night came and it got very cold. The boy started to cry because he was so scared. He knew he was lost. And he never found his way back home.

Suddenly, the boy heard a loud boom! It was the train, crashing into a tree. After the crash, the train was very broken. Sadly, the boy never got to kiss his mom goodbye again.

Tom was troubled. He had a bad dream last night. He saw a big monster with sharp teeth and red eyes. The monster chased him and wanted to eat him. Tom was scared and ran away. He woke up and cried.

Mom heard Tom and came to his room. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. It was just a dream. The monster is not real. You are safe with me." She kissed him and rubbed his back. She said, "Do you want to relax with me on the rug? We can read a book or play a game. That will make you feel better."

Tom nodded and followed Mom to the living room. There was a soft and cozy rug on the floor. Mom and Tom sat on the rug and picked a book. It was a book about animals. Tom liked animals. He pointed at the pictures and said their names. Mom read the words and made funny sounds. Tom laughed and forgot his bad dream.

They finished the book and played a game. They pretended to be animals and crawled on the rug. They made noises and tickled each other. They had fun and smiled. Tom was not troubled anymore. He was happy and relaxed. He said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you." Mom said, "I love you too, Tom. You are my brave boy." They hugged and cuddled on the rug. They felt warm and cozy. They closed their eyes and slept.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there was a small shop. In the shop, there were many toys with a price. A boy named Tim went to the shop with his mom. Tim saw a toy he liked but his mom said, "No, the price is too much."

Tim was sad and went to the park. At the park, he saw a dog. The dog had a toy just like the one in the shop. Tim wanted to play with the dog and the toy. But the dog did not want to share. The dog bit the toy and ran away.

Tim went back to his mom and told her about the dog. His mom said, "It's okay, we can save money and buy the toy later." Tim felt better and they went home. Tim knew he would get the toy one day and he would not let a dog bite it.

Sara and Ben love to play at the park. They like to swing, run, and climb. But their favorite thing is the slide. They take turns to go down the slide, and laugh when they land on the soft grass.

One day, they see a new slide at the park. It is bigger and faster than the old slide. Sara and Ben are curious and excited. They want to try the new slide. They run to the new slide and wait in line.

When it is Sara's turn, she climbs up the ladder and sits on the top. She looks down and feels scared. The new slide is too high and too steep. She does not want to go down. She wants to change her mind and go back to the old slide.

Ben sees that Sara is scared. He climbs up the ladder and sits next to her. He holds her hand and says, "It's okay, Sara. I am here with you. We can go down together. It will be fun. Trust me."

Sara looks at Ben and feels brave. She trusts her brother. She nods and says, "Okay, Ben. Let's go." They hold hands and slide down the new slide. They go fast and feel the wind in their hair. They scream and smile. They land on the soft grass and hug each other.

They did it! They tried the new slide and they liked it. They feel proud and happy. They run back to the line and wait for another turn. They have a lot of fun at the park. The park is peaceful and sunny. Sara and Ben love the new slide.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tim. One day, Tim was walking through a huge corn field and he felt so excited. As he was walking, he decided to whistle as loud as he could. He sang a tune and it echoed across the orange field. Soon, Tim had some company. 

He heard another whistle coming from the cornfield. Tim shouted, â€œWho is out there?â€

He heard a loud and bubbly voice reply, â€œItâ€™s me! Iâ€™m Kevin.â€

Kevin was a friendly orange butterfly. He was dancing in the corn. He said to Tim, â€œLetâ€™s play a game. Iâ€™ll fly ahead and you try to find me in the corn.â€

Tim loved the game and they played together until the sun went down. By the end of the day, Kevin was exhausted and decided to fly back home. Before leaving, he said to Tim, â€œThanks for a wonderful day! Letâ€™s play again soon!â€

Tim waved goodbye to his new friend and then he started whistling the same tune as he walked back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly flying by. "Wow, that butterfly is so pretty!" she said.

Suddenly, a mosquito flew by and bit Lily on the arm. "Ouch! That mosquito is not nice," she said.

Lily's mom heard her cry and came outside. "Are you okay, Lily?" she asked. "No, a mosquito bit me," said Lily. "I don't like mosquitoes."

"Don't worry, I'll send the mosquito away," said Lily's mom. She swatted the mosquito and it flew away.

"Thank you, Mommy," said Lily. "Now I can play outside without any mosquitoes bothering me." And she went back to chasing after the beautiful butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Bun. Bun was very thoughtful and loved to hop around in the grass. One day, Bun saw a new friend coming to visit. Bun was so happy to see the new friend and welcomed them with a big hug. 

Bun and the new friend played together all day long. They hopped and jumped and had so much fun. When it was time for the new friend to go home, Bun said goodbye and thanked them for coming to play. 

From that day on, Bun and the new friend were the best of friends. They would play together every day and Bun was always so happy to welcome the new friend to their home.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Annie. One day she went out of her house and saw her busy neighbor. He was very impatient and Annie wanted to know what he was doing. She asked her neighbor what he was doing, but he didn't answer. Annie was curious so she kept following him around. 

Next, the neighbor stopped in front of a tree and started digging around its roots. After a few minutes the neighbor revealed a box. Annie was very excited to see what was inside. 

Annie asked her neighbor what he had found, but he told her to wait. She became impatient but her neighbor said she had to be patient. Finally, the neighbor opened the box and showed Annie some colorful stones. Annie was so amazed. She thanked her neighbor for showing her the precious stones. 

The neighbor smiled and said that patience is a virtue. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old. One day, she was at her home and she noticed a large fireplace in the living room. Lucy was so amazed by the fireplace that she just had to admire it. 

She exclaimed, â€œWow, this is amazing!â€ 

Her mom replied, â€œIsnâ€™t it? It's a beautiful fireplace!â€ 

â€œCan I touch it?â€ asked Lucy. â€œYou wouldn't burn yourself,â€ her mom said. 

So Lucy carefully touched the fireplace. It was warm, and she admired its large size. 

Lucy said, â€œI love this fireplace!â€ 

Her mom smiled and said, â€œIt's special and it keeps us warm.â€ 

Lucy was happy, and from then on she visited the fireplace every day to admire it.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl. She had long wavy hair and a trim waist. Everywhere she went, she stopped to look at all the wonderous things around her. One day, the little girl was out walking with her mom. The little girl noticed a bright red bird. She was so excited! She paused to admire it and tried to get closer. But when she reached out her hand, the bird flew away. The little girl was so curious to know where it went! She looked all around, but it was gone. Her mom gave her a hug and they continued walking. The little girl admired all the other things they passed, while her mom told her stories. They had a lot of fun and the little girl never forgot the curious red bird.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful pole. The pole stood near a lake and it made the lake look lovely. Every morning, two ducks would come to the lake and find the pole. They liked to separate and explore the lake. The pole was their favourite thing. 

One day, the ducks decided to invite their friends to the lake. They gathered all of the animals around the pole and made a plan. They decided to play hide-and-seek near the pole. 

The animals had so much fun. They played until the sun went down. The ducks were happy because the pole had made their day special. 

From that day on, the pole had a special place in their hearts. The ducks continued to go to the lake every morning, and the pole was a reminder of the beautiful memories they had made.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Laura. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her. Every day, Laura would go out into her garden and observe the things she could see.

One day, Laura went out into the garden and noticed a dark pattern on the ground. She noticed it had a line of dots on either side with a long line in the middle. Laura wanted to know what it was and felt brave enough to find out.

As she got closer, Laura heard some voices. She stopped and hid behind the flowers to listen.

"What is that strange pattern on the ground?" she heard one voice ask.

"I don't know," replied another voice. "But I'm sure it must mean something."

Laura was intrigued. She watched and waited to see what would happen.

Suddenly, out of the darkness came a little creature. Laura couldn't believe her eyes! It was a baby hedgehog, sniffing its way along the path she had seen from a distance.

The hedgehog went on its way, leaving Laura with a newfound understanding of the mysterious pattern she had observed in the dark. She was sure the hedgehog had made the pattern on the ground and she was certain it must mean something!

Once there was an old man who loved his flute. He would play it every day and it filled him with joy and happiness. One day, he wanted to show his flute to his neighbor. He went next to the neighbor's house and asked if he could come in.

But the neighbor shook his head and said, "No, I don't want to see it. I'm too busy."

The old man was very sad and he shrugged. He wondered why his neighbor was so mean and didn't want to share his happiness.

That night, the neighbor's house caught on fire and all his belongings were destroyed. The old man sighed and shook his head, feeling sad.

The moral of the story is: sharing our joy and love with others makes us more fulfilled and happy in life. If the old man's neighbor had taken the time to listen to his flute and share in the old man's joy, he wouldn't have lost all his belongings in the fire.

Barney was very tired. He had been playing all day. All his toys were put away and he lay down on the rug. He was so tired, he did not even notice the hard envelope under his cheek. 

He was very snuggly and drifted off to sleep. He was having a lovely nap. After a while, mum noticed he had fallen asleep. She gently picked him up and put him in his bed.

Mum kissed him on the forehead and put the hard envelope near his bed. That night Barney slept very soundly. In the morning he was fresh and full of energy, ready to play with his toys again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in nature. She liked to look at the trees and flowers and listen to the birds sing. One day, she saw an amazing butterfly flying around. It was so pretty with its colorful wings. 

Lily wanted to touch the butterfly, but she knew she shouldn't catch it. So, she decided to poke her finger out and the butterfly landed on it. She was so happy! She watched it for a while and then let it fly away. From that day on, Lily loved to explore nature and find amazing things.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill, who would always share their days together. One morning Jack woke Jill up and said, "We must go and share a special experience. I know something exciting that we can both share and it will be beautiful." 

Jill excitedly got dressed and followed Jack outside. When she looked around the corner, she saw the most beautiful sight. A rainbow filled the sky and the sun was glowing a brilliant orange. She shouted: "Wow! That's so beautiful!" 

Jack smiled, pleased that his friend was so happy. He said, "Let's stand together and share in the beauty of this wake. We can share this experience forever." 

So the two friends happily shared this beautiful wake together and cherished the moment forever.

Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a big castle. Every day, the king would take big steps around the castle to make sure everything was in order. 

One day, the king decided to take a walk down to a nearby creek. As he stepped closer and closer to the water, he noticed something disgusting in it. The king noticed the creek was filled with slimy trash, which made him really sad. 

The king stepped back and decided to clean up the creek. He gathered all of his friends from around the castle and asked for their help. Everyone took a step towards the water and started to pick out the slimy trash. 

After several hours of hard work, the creek was clean again! The king was so happy, he gave everyone a big hug. From that day forward, the king made sure to take care of the creek so it wouldn't get disgusting again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and wear her fancy cap. One day, she went to a party with her friends. They all wore their fancy clothes and danced to the music. 

Suddenly, Lily's cap fell off her head and into a puddle of mud. She felt sad and didn't want to dance anymore. Her friends saw how sad she was and decided to help. They cleaned her cap and put it back on her head. 

Lily was so happy and started to dance again. But then, another girl accidentally stepped on her cap and it got squished. Lily was upset again and didn't know what to do. 

Her friends came up with an idea to make a new cap for her. They used colorful paper and stickers to make it look even fancier than before. Lily was overjoyed and danced happily with her friends all night long. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved bugs and would often go outside to play with them. One day, he found a bug that he wanted to keep, but it was stuck in a hole. Timmy felt frustrated because he couldn't get the bug out.
