Suddenly, Timmy's dad came outside and saw him looking sad. Timmy told his dad about the bug and how he couldn't lift it out of the hole. His dad smiled and said he could help. He used a stick to lift the bug out of the hole and gave it to Timmy.

Timmy was so happy and thanked his dad for helping him. He ran inside to show his mom the bug and told her how his dad lifted it out of the hole. From that day on, Timmy felt grateful for his dad's help and continued to play with bugs outside. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but her room was always a mess. One day, her mom came in and saw all the toys on the floor. She said, "Lily, it's time to organize your toys so they don't get lost."

Lily didn't know what organize meant, but her mom showed her how to put all the dolls in one corner and the blocks in another. Lily was happy because she could find her toys easier now. Her mom said, "When we organize our things, it makes our life easier."

Lily didn't understand what her mom meant by "life", but she knew that having her toys organized made her happy. She also learned that some toys were rare and needed to be taken care of. From that day on, Lily made sure to organize her toys every night before bed. She learned that being organized was a good thing and made her life better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl with brown hair. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she saw a brown dog in her yard. The dog looked very tired.

"Hi, dog! Do you want to rest?" the girl asked. The dog wagged its tail and lay down on the soft grass. The girl sat down next to the dog and they both took a nice rest together.

After a while, the girl and the dog woke up from their rest. They played catch with a ball and ran around the yard. They had so much fun. At the end of the day, the girl gave the brown dog a big hug and said, "Goodbye, new friend!" The dog barked happily and went back to its home. The girl went inside her house, ready for a good night's rest.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Susie. She loved playing outside and being with nature. 

One day, Susie woke up to a beautiful winter morning. She ran to the window and saw that everything was covered in a blanket of white snow. She gasped in amazement and excitement. She quickly got dressed and ran outside to play.

Susie started to build a snowman and make snow angels. As she was playing, she realized that winter was even more fun than summertime. She loved how everything was so peaceful and the snow was so beautiful. 

Susie also realized that winter was special and she wanted to enjoy it as much as possible. She began to make plans to go sledding and have a snowball fight with her friends. She was so happy and excited to spend the winter outdoors!

The sun rose in the sky. It was time for the two best friends to go outside and explore. They began to walk through the fields, when one of them suddenly shouted "watch out!". A big rock was up ahead.

The friends slowed down and were very careful not to trip. They found a new path that had not been taken before. They explored for what felt like ages and then the sun began to set.

The two friends knew that it was almost time to head back home, but the path before them seemed so long and daunting. They decided to take the same path that they had found earlier.

It was almost dark, but the two friends trusted that the path would lead them back home safe and sound. As they rounded the corner, they saw a beautiful light in the distance. It was the sun, rising in the sky. The two friends knew that they would make it back safely, just like they had done hundreds of times before. They kept walking, careful and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He loved to nap under a large tree in the jungle. One day, he saw a little bird sitting on a branch of the tree. The bird was chirping and singing a sweet song. The elephant was happy to see the bird and he asked if he could nap beside him. The bird said yes and they both took a nap under the large tree. When they woke up, they became good friends and the elephant promised to visit the bird every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Pinky. Pinky was very humble and always helped others. One day, Pinky saw a bird who couldn't fly because its wings were hurt. Pinky decided to help the bird and took care of it until it was better. 

As the days went by, Pinky saw many animals who needed help. Pinky always helped them with a happy heart. One day, Pinky met a snail who was very sad. The snail wanted to see the beautiful flowers on the other side of the garden, but it was too slow. Pinky had an idea! Pinky said, "I will spring you over to the other side of the garden so you can see the flowers!" 

The snail was very happy and thanked Pinky. Pinky learned that helping others can make them happy and that makes us happy too. So, Pinky continued to help others and spread joy wherever it went.

One day, a little girl named Jill went for a walk in the park. She saw a beautiful white bird sitting atop a tall tree. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I have a bird like that." Her mom replied, "No dear, you can't have a bird like that." Jill felt very sad.

Then, the bird spoke to her in a loud voice and demanded, "Give me a gift if you want me to be your friend." Jill said, "I don't have a gift for you." The bird became angry and said, "If you don't give me a gift, I won't be your friend."

Jill thought and she remembered her mom had made some cookies. She carefully took out one of the cookies and offered it to the bird. The bird accepted the gift and said, "Thank you Jill, I appreciate your thoughtfulness and kindness." Then, the bird flew away.

Jill learned a valuable lesson that day: being careless is not the same as being caring. She realized that sometimes, it's more important to show kindness and thoughtfulness than to receive gifts.

Once upon a time, there lived a brave knight. He was tall and had a big, shiny shield. Every day he would wear it so nothing could hurt him. One day he went on an adventure. He followed a colorful rainbow road until he came to a magical forest.

Inside the forest, the knight saw so many new things. Everywhere he looked he saw colorful flowers and trees. But then something strange happened. He heard a small voice coming from behind a big tree! When he looked closer, he saw a little fairy.

The fairy was very small and sparkly. She asked the knight if he would like to see her special magic. He said yes, so the fairy waved her wand and the ground started to sparkle. Suddenly, a shield appeared in front of the knight. The fairy explained that it was a very special shield. Whenever the knight wore it, nobody could hurt him.

The knight thanked the fairy for her help and then went off to explore the forest. From then on, he always wore his special shield. The more he explored, the more colorful the forest became!

Once there was a wise old owl who lived high up in a tree. Every day he looked down from his perch and watched the children running around on the lawn below. He watched as they played hide and seek and laughed out loud.

The owl liked to watch the children and he liked to think too. He thought about all sorts of things, like what the world would be like if he could fly down and join the children on the lawn. 

But he knew he was too old to do such a thing. He had to be wise and stay in his tree.

One day he noticed something in the sky. It was a kite! It was fluttering and spinning around in the air - just like the owl wished he could do. He watched as the kite flew higher and higher in the sky, and then he had an idea. 

He thought that if he could make his own kite, maybe he could fly too. So, he set to work making a kite with his favourite colours - green, yellow and red. When it was finished he looked at it proudly and held it tightly as he flew from his tree to the lawn. 

The children saw him coming and cheered as he flew his kite. They were so happy that the wise old owl was flying just like them. The owl was delighted and flew his kite on the lawn for the rest of the day.

John and his mom were walking in the park one day. John was feeling brave and he wanted to play with the other kids. As he looked around, he saw a pan on the ground. He wondered what it was and he asked his mom.

"Mommy, what's that pan?", John said.

"It's a pan, John. We use it to cook food", said his mom.

John was confused. He didn't understand why someone would leave a pan in the park. He decided to pick it up and bring it home.

When John's mom saw this, she smiled. She said, "John, that's very kind of you. We don't take things from other people without asking. It's not polite."

John nodded and understood. He knew that it was important to ask for permission first before taking something that wasn't his. He put down the pan and walked away with his mom, feeling happy and content. 

The moral of the story is that it is important to be respectful and to always ask permission before taking something that doesn't belong to you.

Once upon a time, there was a big fish named Max. Max loved to swim in the ocean and play with his fish friends. One day, Max saw a shiny hook in the water. He thought it looked fun, so he swam over to it and got caught on the hook! He tried to wiggle free, but he couldn't.

Luckily, a brilliant little girl named Lily was walking along the beach. She saw Max and knew just what to do. She ran to her dad and asked him to help. Her dad came over and carefully took the hook out of Max's mouth. Max was so happy to be free!

To thank Lily, Max's fish friends decided to cook her a special dinner. They made her favorite food, spaghetti and meatballs. Lily was so happy and grateful for the delicious meal. From that day on, Max and Lily became great friends and had many more fun adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around in the springtime. He would jump and play with his friends in the green grass. One day, Benny's friend Sally asked him to help wrap a present for their friend's birthday. Benny was happy to help.

The present was a box filled with popular toys like dolls and cars. Benny and Sally wrapped the box with colorful paper and tied a bow on top. They were excited to give the present to their friend. 

After they finished wrapping, Benny went back outside to play. He hopped and skipped through the fields, enjoying the warm spring sun on his fur. He couldn't wait to see his friend's face when they opened the present.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Andy. Andy lived in a dry land where it hardly ever rained. One day, Andy went out to find some food for his family. Suddenly, he heard a loud thunder. He got scared and started to crawl back to his home as fast as he could.

On his way back, he met a snail who was also crawling. The snail asked Andy, "Why are you in such a hurry?" Andy replied, "I heard a loud thunder and I'm scared. I need to go home." The snail said, "Don't be scared of the thunder. It's just the sound of the clouds bumping into each other. You should be brave like me and keep crawling."

Andy thought about what the snail said and realized that he shouldn't be scared of the thunder. He thanked the snail and continued on his way. When he got home, he told his family what happened and they were proud of him for being brave.

The moral of the story is to not be afraid of things that you don't understand. Just keep crawling and you'll get through it.

Once upon a time, there was a nice princess called Daisy. Daisy loved to measure things. One day, she was measuring a piece of toast, when she heard a voice.

"What are you doing?" said a small voice.

Daisy looked up. It was a fairy. She smiled.

"I'm measuring this toast," said Daisy.

The fairy looked thoughtful. "I wonder why," she said.

Daisy smiled. "Because it's nice to know how much toast I have."

The fairy smiled back. "That's a very good idea," she said.

So Daisy measured the toast and it was just enough for her to have a nice snack. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She liked to explore the park. Today she was very excited because she was going to see a jet. 

Jane said, "Yay! Jet!" 
So Jane ran to the park and followed the jet.
But the jet was too high! Jane wanted to see it better so she wished she could fly.

Suddenly, a hairy monster appeared. He said, "I can take you to the jet. Follow me!" 

So Jane followed the hairy monster. He took her up, up, up until finally they were flying next to the jet. 

Jane was amazed and said, "Wow! Jet!" 

The hairy monster smiled and said, "We can come back and see it again if you want."

And so Jane and the hairy monster flew around the park, looking at the jet over and over again. 

The end.

The sun was shining in the sky when John and his mom went out into the woods. John was excited and liked to run around and pick up leaves.

Mom said, "Look over there! What is that?"

John saw a big, round thing rolling. He said, "It's a ball."

Mom said, "No, it looks like a can. Let's go and see what it is!"

When they got closer, they could see the word "Poison" written on the side and they were scared.

Mom said, "We can't touch it. That's poison and it's bad for us!"

But John wasn't listening. He wanted to see what was inside the can. Mom said, "No! Don't touch it!"

But, it was too late. John picked up the can and opened it! Just then, a big, black spider came out and crawled up his arm! John was so scared that he dropped the can and ran away!

Mom laughed and said, "Don't worry, that spider won't hurt you. It's just scared, like you!"

Once upon a time, there was a big horse. The horse lived in a huge stable with lots of hay. The horse loved to run and play in the fields. One day, the horse saw a little bird with a broken wing. The horse wanted to help the bird and tried to lift it up with its mouth. But the horse was too big and accidentally hurt the bird. The horse didn't understand what it did wrong and felt sad. The bird didn't survive and the horse was left alone in the stable, feeling guilty.

The little boy had a hero. His hero was strong and brave, so the little boy looked up to him. One day, the little boy heard some bad news. His hero was in great danger!

The little boy was very scared. He had to try to be brave and help his hero somehow. He thought and thought, but he couldn't come up with a plan. He felt so helpless!

Finally, the boy decided to go and find the bad person who had hurt his hero. He set off on a journey to find him.

The little boy was so scared, but he kept going. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It said, "I'm the one who hurt your hero." The little boy's heart was very bitter. He thought, "I will find a way to save my hero!" 

He heard a loud noise and jumped. The bad person had been defeated! His hero was safe.

The little boy was relieved and happy. He smiled at his hero and said, "You are my real hero!"

Once upon a time, there was a little red car. The car rolled along the street, looking for someplace to go. All of a sudden, the car's tank ran out of gas. The car came to a stop.

The driver of the car got out and looked at the car. He knew that he had to go and get more gas. He found a gas station and filled up the car's tank. 

When the car was ready to go, the driver hopped back in and turned the key. The engine came to life and the car drove off. 

The little red car drove off, ready to start its next journey. It was happy to be able to keep going.

Once there was a little boy named Peter. Peter loved to play outside. One day he went to a park and saw a strange pipe. It was a terrible pipe, so Peter was scared. He started to wave his arms around to try and make it go away.

But the pipe wouldn't go away. It just kept getting bigger and bigger! Soon it was so big that it touched the sky! The little boy was so scared that he had to cover his eyes.

But then, something amazing happened. A giant hand appeared in the sky and waved at Peter. The hand was gentle and friendly. Peter waved back to the hand and the pipe disappeared right away!

The little boy was so excited. He ran to tell all his friends at the park what he had seen. Everybody was amazed and they all waved to the sky in thanks.

From then on, the little boy was never afraid of the terrible pipe again.

Billy had a pencil. He was so happy. He wanted to draw a picture with it. He asked his mom if he could draw it.

"Yes, of course," said his mom.

Billy started to draw a picture but it wasn't looking very good. He started to feel a bit bad.

"Do you like my picture mommy?" asked Billy.

"It's ok," said his mom. "But we can always do better. Let's try again!"

Billy was not sure if he could do better, but he accepted his mom's suggestion. He decided to give it a try. He picked up his pencil and started drawing again. This time, he was very careful and his picture was much better.

"That looks great!" said his mom. "I'm so proud of you for trying again and for accepting that it wasn't good the first time."

Billy was so happy! He was proud of himself too for accepting his mom's advice.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very adventurous and loved exploring the world around him. One day, he decided to go on a big adventure to find a treasure.

Timmy walked and walked until he found a big, shiny chest. He opened it up and saw a lot of gold and jewels inside. Timmy was very happy, but then he heard a noise behind him. He turned around and saw a man trying to steal the treasure.

Timmy ran as fast as he could with the chest in his hands. He ran all the way back home and hid the chest under his bed. He knew that he had to keep the treasure safe for a whole year until he could use it to buy something very special. And that's exactly what he did. He kept the treasure safe for a whole year and then used it to buy a new bike.

Once upon a time there was a friendly frog who lived in a dry pond. One day, he looked around his pond and noticed that his friends, the fish, could not swim around the pond. There was no water in it.

So the friendly frog decided to solve the problem. He asked his furry friends, the squirrels, if they could help him. The squirrels came up with a plan. 

They found a rod and presented it to the frog. "This rod will help us get the water to your pond,â€ they said.

The frog was so happy! The squirrels then told the frog how to use the rod. He put the rod into the ground and made a hole. The hole started to fill up with water and soon the pond was full! 

The fish and all the other animals were very happy. Now they could swim and play in the pond. And the friendly frog smiled because he had solved the problem.

Once there was a little yellow flower that grew in the garden. It was small and fuzzy and it was very happy.

One day, the little flower saw a neighbour walking past and said, "Hello! What's your name?"

The neighbour said, "My name is Joe. Nice to meet you!"

The little flower said, "It's nice to meet you too, Joe. I'm a flower and I like to grow. Would you like to help me?"

Joe smiled and said, "I'd love to!"

Joe and the flower started digging in the soil and soon the little flower was growing bigger and stronger. Joe watered and fed the flower every day and it became even more beautiful.

One day, the flower was so tall that it touched a bee. The bee got angry and stung the flower until it was hurt.

The flower was in pain but Joe quickly picked it up and said, "It's okay, little flower. We'll get you better soon. Don't worry, I'm here." 

The flower got better with Joe's help and it even became a more vibrant yellow. Joe and the little flower remained friends forever and looked after each other.

One day, a small mosquito was flying around. The mosquito was very hungry. It saw a big, heavy rock and thought it could find food there.

The mosquito tried to bite the rock, but it was too hard. "Ouch!" said the mosquito. "This rock is too sharp!" The mosquito was sad and still hungry.

Just then, a friendly bug came by. "Why are you sad?" asked the bug. The mosquito told the bug about the sharp rock. The bug said, "Don't be sad. I know where to find soft food. Follow me!" The mosquito followed the bug and found a nice flower to eat. They both became good friends and were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily was playing hide-and-seek with her teddy bear, Mr. Snuggles. She hid behind the curtain in the living room. 

Suddenly, Lily heard a loud noise and when she peeked out from behind the curtain, she saw that Mr. Snuggles had vanished! She looked everywhere for him but he was nowhere to be found. 

Lily was very sad without her teddy bear. She decided to make a new friend by drawing a picture of an attractive puppy. She drew it on a piece of paper and put it on her bed. When she woke up the next morning, the puppy was gone! 

But then, Lily noticed something strange. The curtain in her room was moving. She walked over to it and pulled it back. Behind the curtain, she found Mr. Snuggles and the puppy from her drawing! They had been hiding there the whole time. Lily was so happy to have her teddy bear back and to have a new friend too.

Once upon a time there was a mighty dragon. He lived in a cave deep inside a mountain. Every day the dragon would fly out of his cave to care for the animals around his home. He used his mighty mouth to blow gentle warm breath and care for them by keeping them safe. 

The dragon's mighty mouth was so big he could even care for the biggest and tallest of trees. With ever puff of air he blew he was sure to care for all the animals and trees around. 

One day, a little child was walking by and noticed the dragon. The child was a bit scared but the dragon seemed so kind and gentle. He spoke to the dragon and thanked him for caring for his home. 

The dragon smiled and said he was happy to show some care. From that day on the dragon and the little child became friends and the dragon kept on caring for the animals and trees around his home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sam. She loved to explore the world around her and was always interested in learning new things.

One day, Sam asked her father to show her a file from their basement. Her father said he would if she promised to be careful and not make a mess. Sam agreed and her father granted her request.

When they went down to the basement, it was very dark and cold. Sam felt scared and began to cry. Then an orange and yellow light appeared. Sam realized that it was coming from the warm sunlight streaming through the window. The growing warmth gave Sam enough courage to continue the search for the file.

At last, they found the file and Sam's father said, "See, things aren't always as scary as they seem. With courage comes strength and with strength comes confidence". 

Sam learned an important lesson that day - that it is important to stay brave and confident even when things appear scary.

Lily and Ben were going to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They were very happy. They liked to see the animals and play in the park. They put on their hats and sunscreen, because it was a hot day.

They walked to the bus stop, but the bus was late. Mom looked at her watch and said, "Oh no, we will miss the show. The lions and tigers are going to roar and jump soon. What can we do?"

Dad saw a yellow car with a sign on it. He said, "Look, there is a taxi. We can take the taxi to the zoo. It will be faster than the bus." He waved his hand and the taxi stopped.

Lily and Ben climbed into the taxi with Mom and Dad. The taxi driver was nice. He asked them where they wanted to go. Dad said, "To the zoo, please. And hurry, we don't want to miss the show."

The taxi driver nodded and drove away. He turned on the radio and played some music. Lily and Ben sang along. They were excited. They decided to sit by the window and look at the cars and buildings. They hoped to see the lions and tigers soon.

Once upon a time, there was a pan. The pan was very special. It could roll! It would roll down the hill and into the garden.



One day, a little boy saw the pan rolling down the hill. He was so excited he wanted to join in the fun. He chased after the pan but he got scared halfway down the hill. He became fearful of the rolling pan.

The little boy decided to take a rest at the bottom of the hill. Suddenly, the pan rolled right up to him. The little boy surprised and excited, he put his hands out to touch the pan. As he touched it, it stopped rolling.

The boy was so happy he had made a new friend. Everyday after school, he would come back to the hill with his pan and they would roll down the hill together. They would spend the entire afternoon rolling and playing in the garden.

It was a wonderful friendship. They both loved rolling down the hill together; it made them so happy. The little boy was never scared anymore, because he knew his pan was always by his side.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous cat. This cat loved to eat cereal. Every day, the cat would ask his mom to serve him his favorite cereal.

One day, the cat's mom was too busy to serve him cereal. The cat was very sad. He wanted his cereal so much. So, he decided to serve the cereal by himself.

The cat climbed up on the chair to reach the cereal box. But, he fell down and made a big mess. The cereal was all over the floor. The cat's mom was not happy. The cat did not get to eat his cereal that day.

Once upon a time there was an infant named Stevie. Stevie's parents were very harsh to him. They never wanted to cuddle with him, play with him, or take him for walks.

One day, Stevie's parents decided to raise him even more harshly. They stopped giving him food, and they made him sleep in a corner. 

Stevie was too scared to move. Days passed and he got hungrier and angrier. He was so desperate, he tried to run away. But his parents caught him and punished him, telling him he should stay put.

Stevie was very sad and tired. He kept crying and wishing for somebody to help him. But nobody cared. 

Eventually, Stevie died. His parents never even said goodbye, and his life ended in tragedy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his toys and going to the park with his mom and dad. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they had to go to the store because they needed to buy some food for dinner. 

While they were at the store, Timmy saw a fire truck drive by with its lights flashing and its siren blaring. His mom explained to him that the fire truck was going to help someone who was in an emergency. Timmy thought that was very important and he wanted to become a firefighter when he grew up so he could help people too.

As they left the store, Timmy's mom noticed that she had lost her keys. She started to panic because they were important and she needed them to drive the car. Timmy remembered what he had learned about emergencies and he told his mom not to worry, he would help her find the keys. Together, they searched the store and finally found the keys on a shelf. Timmy felt very proud that he was able to help his mom in an emergency.

Once there was a fat cat named Matt. Matt loved to explore the world around him. One day, Matt found a strange object on the floor. It was round in shape and had the word 'magnet' written on it. Matt was curious, so he picked it up. 

Suddenly, a huge pile of toys appeared! Matt was amazed. Everywhere he looked, there were toys - cars, dolls and much more. Matt grabbed as many toys as he could and played with them for a long time. 

At the end of the day, Matt discovered that the magnet was powerful. Every time he held it, a pile of toys would appear. Matt was so happy he had found such a great toy! From that day on, Matt always kept the magnet close by.

Once there was a video that was scary. It was about a giant monster that roared and made everyone afraid.

Two brave kids wanted to beat the monster. So they grabbed their swords and went to face the monster.

The monster was huge, but the kids were brave. They faced the monster and started to fight. They tried to make the monster go away.

Finally, they won the battle and the monster went away. It was the end of the scary video. Everyone was happy and cheered.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very busy playing in her garden. Suddenly, a strong wind blew and covered her with leaves. The little girl was very scared. She started to cry.

When the wind stopped blowing, the girl looked around. All of the leaves were covering her. The leaves were as big as her hand and softly tickled her face.

The girl giggled. She loved when the wind made the leaves cover her. She started to roll around and the leaves danced around her.

She stayed in her garden until the sun slowly set. She hugged the leaves and then said goodbye. She went inside with a big smile on her face. It had been a fun and busy day in the garden!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. One day, Lucy went to a special park with lots of swings. She wanted to spin as fast as she could. 

When she sat down on the swing, she listened to her heart as it pounded with excitement. She arose to her feet and pushed off, spinning around and around until her bright pink dress flew around her, faster and faster.

Suddenly, she heard a loud voice from behind her - it was her Dad! He said, â€œWow, Lucy! Youâ€™re spinning so quickly!

Lucy stopped spinning and smiled at her Dad. She said, â€œI am spinning so fast that I can feel the wind in my face! Can you see my dress? It looks so clear!â€

Her Dad smiled back. He said, â€œYouâ€™re spinning so fast, Lucy! Iâ€™m proud of your courage and your determination to go as fast as you can. I love watching you having so much fun.â€ 

Lucy smiled brightly. She felt her heart was so full of joy and love. She said, â€œI love spinning!â€ and hopped back on the swing to spin again.

The small bear was hungry. He wandered through the house looking for food, but nothing was to be found. He was sad. 

Suddenly, he heard a noise coming from the kitchen. He followed the sound to the fridge and peered in. Inside he saw a delicious treat â€“ a bright red apple! He couldn't reach it though.

He thought for a moment and then leaned down on the ground. He then carefully laid on his stomach, reached inside the fridge and grabbed the apple. 

He stood up and smiled as he savored the sweet treat. He had found something yummy - Just standing up and leaning down had done the trick.

Ben and Lily are playing with blocks. They like to make towers and houses with different colors. Ben has a lot of blue blocks and Lily has a lot of red blocks.

"Look, I made a big tower with blue blocks!" Ben says. He is proud of his tower.

"That's nice, Ben. But I made a house with red blocks!" Lily says. She likes her house.

They look at each other's blocks and smile. They are happy.

Then they see a shiny block on the floor. It is not blue or red. It is brown and shiny. It is a copper block.

"Wow, what is that?" Ben asks. He picks up the copper block and looks at it.

"It is a copper block. It is very pretty and clean. It is my block!" Lily says. She wants the copper block.

"No, it is my block! I saw it first!" Ben says. He holds the copper block tight.

They start to pull the copper block from each other. They are not happy.

"Stop, stop!" a voice says. It is Mom. She comes to see what is wrong.

"Ben and Lily, why are you fighting? You have so many blocks to play with. Why do you want the same block?" Mom asks.

"Because it is a copper block. It is very pretty and clean. We both want it!" Ben and Lily say.

Mom smiles. She has an idea.

"Why don't you share the copper block? You can add it to your blocks and make something new. Maybe a castle or a bridge or a rocket. What do you think?" Mom says.

Ben and Lily think. They like Mom's idea. They stop fighting.

"OK, we can share the copper block. We can add it to our blocks and make something new. Maybe a castle or a bridge or a rocket. That sounds fun!" Ben and Lily say.

They give Mom a hug and a kiss. They are happy.

They take the copper block and add it to their blocks. They make a castle with blue, red and copper blocks. It is very pretty and clean. They play with their castle and have fun. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was very happy, but she wanted to win something very special.

One day, Jane saw a shiny new scooter in the store. It was so pretty! She wanted it so badly. She wished and prayed that she could win it.

The next day, Jane heard a noise outside her window. When she looked out, she saw a great big box with a scooter inside! She was so excited! She ran outside and opened the box. It was her scooter! She had won it!

Jane was very happy. She jumped on it and rode around the yard. But when it started getting dark, Jane was a little frightened. She was so used to riding around in the sunshine. But she remembered how brave she was to win the scooter, and she knew that everything was okay.

So Jane kept riding her scooter, and eventually, she wasn't even a bit frightened anymore. Every day she would ride around, bigger and braver and happier than ever!

Tom and his mom were on a picnic in the park. Tom was gazing around, admiring the beautiful old trees in the park.
He noticed something strange in the grass. He went closer and saw an old wooden puzzle.
Tom was so excited and he said to his mom:
"Mommy, look! A puzzle!" 
Tom's mom smiled and said:
"Why don't you try to put it together?"
Tom was eager to do it, so he carefully picked it up, admired its old brown color, and he started putting it together.
Tom was so proud of himself when he finished the puzzle. He hugged his mom and said:
"Look mommy, I did it!"
His mom hugged him back and said:
"Good job, Tom! You did a fantastic job."
Tom smiled and gazed at his beautiful puzzle.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore and go on adventures. One day, he decided to go on a walk in the forest. He was so excited to see all the trees and animals.

As he was walking, he saw a big, scary bear. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. He questioned if he should run away or stay still. He decided to run away as fast as he could.

Timmy ran and ran, but he didn't know the way back home. He was lost in the forest and didn't know what to do. He felt scared and alone. As it started to get dark, Timmy realized he was in trouble. He wished he had never gone on this adventure.

Unfortunately, Timmy was never found and his family never saw him again. The forest was a dangerous place and Timmy had learned that the hard way.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when she accidentally swallowed a fake nail. She started to cry because she was scared.

Her mom heard her crying and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

"I swallowed a nail," Lily said, still crying.

"Don't worry, I'll save you," her mom said.

Her mom took her to the doctor and the doctor made sure she was okay. Lily was relieved that she was safe and sound.

Once upon a time there was a light man. He wanted to steal something from the store. He saw a thread and thought it was perfect. The light man carefully stole the thread from the store. He was so happy to have it.

The light man walked around with the thread in his pocket. But it did not stay there for very long. The wind blew and the thread flew out of his pocket. It went higher and higher until it was gone.

The light man looked up into the sky and saw the thread dancing in the wind. He smiled. He was happy that the thread was free and he knew it was safe. The light man waved goodbye to the thread before he left.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to pour some milk into her cereal bowl. Lily was happy to help and carefully poured the milk. 

After breakfast, Lily went to check the mailbox with her mommy. They found a letter from her grandma, who lived far away. Lily was so excited to read it! But then she noticed something naughty - a bird had made a mess on the mailbox. 

Lily's mommy got some water and a cloth to clean it up. Lily helped by pouring the water on the mailbox. They cleaned it up together and then went inside to read the letter from grandma. It was a happy day for Lily and her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing on the swings. Suddenly, Lily fell off and hurt her knee. 

Her friend, Timmy, ran to get a towel to help her. He put the towel on her knee to support it. Lily was very grateful and thanked Timmy for his help. 

Then, another friend named Billy came over and said, "Lily, you were foolish to fall off the swing!" Lily felt sad and started to cry. But Timmy said, "Don't worry, Lily. Billy is just being mean. We all fall sometimes. It's okay." 

Lily felt better and hugged Timmy. She was happy to have such a kind and supportive friend. From that day on, Lily knew that it was okay to make mistakes and that her friends would always be there to help her.

Once upon a time there was a dog named Gus. Gus was always a silly dog, and he loved to play. One day, Gus decided he was going to run as fast as he can. He thought this would be a lot of fun. 

Gus started to run, but he was going too fast for his little legs. He started to worry that he would not be able to stop. So Gus yelled to his owner, "help me, I'm going too fast!"

His owner, who was watching from the porch, said "Don't worry, Gus. That's just your silly speed showing off." 

Gus stopped running and smiled. He understood that his silly speed was nothing to worry about. Now, whenever Gus feels like running, he doesn't worry. He knows that his silly speed won't hurt anyone.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play and have fun. But today, they have to go to a lecture with Mom and Dad. A lecture is when a person talks a lot and other people listen. Lily and Tom do not like lectures. They think they are boring.

Mom and Dad give Lily and Tom some snacks and toys to keep them quiet. They say, "Be good and listen to the lecture. It is about animals and plants. You like animals and plants, right?" Lily and Tom nod, but they are not happy.

The lecture starts. The person talks about lions and tigers and bears. He shows pictures and makes sounds. Lily and Tom look at the pictures and try to make sounds too. But they are too loud. Mom and Dad say, "Shh, shh, you are disturbing the lecture. Be quiet, please."

Lily and Tom are hungry. They eat their snacks. Lily has a cracker and Tom has a cookie. But Tom's cookie is spicy. It has pepper in it. Tom does not like spicy food. He makes a face and spits out the cookie. He says, "Yuck, yuck, this cookie is spicy. I do not like it." He cries and coughs.

Mom and Dad are embarrassed. They say, "Sorry, sorry, we did not know the cookie was spicy. Tom, are you okay?" They give him some water and a hug. They say, "We are sorry, but we have to go. The lecture is not for us. We will go to the park instead. You like the park, right?" Lily and Tom nod, and they are happy. They say, "Yes, yes, we like the park. Let's go, let's go." They pack their snacks and toys and leave the lecture. They go to the park and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy who wanted to spin really fast. So every day he went to the beach. He wanted to go as fast as he could. He would try to surf and spin.

The boy enjoyed spinning around in the water. He felt so light and happy. He could almost fly!

But one day, something went wrong. He tried to spin too much and too fast. He twisted and tumbled into the water and he couldn't swim back up.

The jolly boy was so sad. He never got to spin again. He had to stay deep in the sea forever.

Sara and Ben liked to play near the creek. The creek was behind their house. It had clear water and many rocks. Sometimes they saw fish and frogs in the creek.

One day, they saw an old man sitting on a big rock. He had a long beard and a hat. He was holding a stick with a string. He was fishing.

"Hello, old man," Sara said. "What are you doing?"

"Hello, little girl," the old man said. "I am fishing. Do you like fishing?"

"Yes, we do," Ben said. "Can we fish with you?"

"Of course, you can," the old man said. "You are welcome to join me. I have an extra stick and some worms. Come, sit with me."

Sara and Ben ran to the old man. They sat on the rock with him. He gave them a stick and a worm each. He showed them how to put the worm on the hook and throw the string in the water.

They waited for a fish to bite. They talked with the old man. He told them stories about the creek and the animals. He was very kind and funny.

Sara and Ben had a lot of fun. They caught some fish and let them go. They thanked the old man for letting them fish with him.

"You are very welcome, my friends," the old man said. "You made me happy today. Come back anytime you want. The creek is always here for you."

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky lived in a pond with other ducks. One day, Ducky saw a flower in the pond. The flower was small and green. Ducky thought it was interesting. 

Every day, Ducky would swim over to the flower and watch it grow. It started to get bigger and bigger until one day, it bloomed! The flower was now big and yellow. Ducky was so happy to see the flower bloom. 

From that day on, Ducky would swim over to the flower every day to see if it had bloomed again. Ducky loved the flower and thought it was the most interesting thing in the pond.

Once there was a big thief who went around taking things that didn't belong to him. One day, he saw a red fire truck with a big ladder and knew he had to have it. The thief snuck up to the truck and put his hand on the door handle.

Just then, a little girl walked up to him and said, "What do you think you're doing?" The thief said, "I'm taking this truck."

"You can't do that!" the little girl said. "This isn't yours." The thief said, "It will be if I take it!"

The little girl smiled and said, "I think I can help you with that. I can permit you to take the truck if you promise to give it back when you're done."

The thief was so surprised he couldn't say anything. "Do we have a deal?" the little girl asked. The thief nodded and said, "Yes, we do."

So the thief got his wish and took the big red fire truck. He drove it around for the day and was sure to bring it back to the little girl when he was finished.  The little girl smiled and thanked the thief. From then on, the big thief always asked for permission instead of taking things that weren't his.

Jair loved to play with his toys. He especially liked to make stories and act them out with his stuffed animals. He especially liked to go to the market with his mom.

At the market, Jair saw lots of colorful things. He walked around and saw lots of delicious fruit, fish and other things his mom buys. He noticed a lot of people too.

One day, Jair noticed something different at the market. He heard a loud sound coming from the street. There were now a lot of people and the popular music was making them dance.

Jair thought the music was fun and he started to dance too. He began to skip and spin around, but then the music stopped. People stared at Jair and his mom told him he was disturbing the market.

Jair was a bit sad but he still enjoyed the market. He watched the people and listened to the music. Jair knew he wouldn't make the same mistake again. He was happy that he was so popular!

Once upon a time, in an ancient house, there lived a little girl named Amy. Amy had a toy she did not like. She would say, "I hate this toy." The toy was a ball with the number zero on it.

One sunny day, Amy went outside to play. She took her ball with the number zero on it. She threw the ball high in the sky. The ball went up and up, and then it came back down. Amy saw that the ball was fun to play with.

From that day on, Amy did not hate the ball with the number zero on it. She played with the ball every day. Her ancient house was filled with laughter and fun. And Amy learned that sometimes, things we think we hate can become things we love.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little girl who couldn't keep her eyes off her friends. She saw that one of her friends had a piece of gum in her pocket, so she wanted to have some too. She asked her friend if she could have it, but the friend shook her head no. The nosy little girl was disappointed, but then a new idea came to her. She asked her friend if she could have the gum if she could sign her name. The friend was so impressed with the idea, she smiled and said yes.

The nosy little girl quickly grabbed a pen and paper. She was so excited - she had never signed her name before. She carefully wrote her name as best as she could and showed it to her friend. Her friend was amazed and laughed when she saw it. She handed the nosy little girl the gum, and both kids were happy. In the end, the nosy little girl learned the power of signing her name and getting what she wanted.

John was walking on the beach when he saw something very high in the sky. He looked up and saw a jellyfish floating above him! He thought it was so beautiful! He wanted to touch it so he started to jump as high as he could until he was almost as high as the jellyfish. But no matter how high John tried to jump he couldn't get to the jellyfish. He got very sad and started to cry. Suddenly a big hand came down from the sky and picked up the jellyfish. John looked up and saw a giant! The giant was smiling at John and waved goodbye. John waved back and smiled as the giant took the jellyfish away. John was happy that he got to see the jellyfish and waved at it until it was out of sight.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. Her teacher said she was ready to go on a special trip. So, one day, Amy went to the airport with her family.

At the airport, Amy's tummy was shivering because she was feeling excited. But when she saw the airport, it looked so tidy. Everything was in its place and the walls were very clean. She felt calm and happy. 

Then, they got in a big plane. Amy looked out the window and the airport got smaller and smaller. She waved goodbye until the airport was out of sight. 

It was a long flight, but when they finally arrived Amy felt so excited. That day she learned that airports weren't so scary after all.

Once upon a time, there was a big, bald eagle who lived in a forest. He was very proud of his shiny head and loved to fly high in the sky. One day, he saw a little bird who was eating some berries. The eagle wanted to help the little bird, so he swooped down to grab some berries for him.

But, when the eagle landed, he accidentally ate a poisonous berry! He felt very sick and embarrassed because he couldn't fly anymore. The little bird saw that the eagle was in trouble and knew just what to do. He went to get some water and brought it back to the eagle. The eagle drank the water and felt much better.

From that day on, the eagle and the little bird became best friends. They would fly together and eat berries together. The eagle was no longer embarrassed because he knew he had a friend who would always be there to help him.

Once upon a time, there was a crocodile, called Croc. He was feeling very sad one day. He didn't know what to do, until he heard about a magical mineral that would make him feel better. 

`What kind of mineral?` he asked. 

`It's a magic mineral very far away,` came the reply. `If you get it, you will succeed and be happy.`

Croc thought it was worth a try and set off on a long journey. The journey was terrible. It was so hot that he could hardly breathe. But he kept going and eventually he found the mineral. He was so excited. 

He held the mineral in his claws and looked up at the sky.

`I did it!`, he cheered. 

Since then, Croc has been very happy and always remembers to never give up.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They liked to share things. 
One day, they decided to play chess. The pieces were furry and soft. They took turns, deciding who went first. The friends had lots of fun. 
After they finished playing, they shared a snack. It was yummy! 
The friends laughed and smiled. They enjoyed spending time together and sharing things. 
The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little worm named Wiggly. Wiggly was a nice worm who lived in a big green garden. He had many friends, like the bees, birds, and bugs. They all liked to play together in the sun.

One day, Wiggly found a big book under a tree. He wanted to read it, but he was too small. So, he asked his friend, the bee, to help him. The bee said, "Sure, Wiggly! I will help you read the big book."

The bee and Wiggly started to read the book together. They read about big trees, pretty flowers, and cute animals. They had so much fun reading the book that they read it all day long. When they finished, Wiggly said, "Thank you, bee, for helping me read the big book. I had a lot of fun!"

From that day on, Wiggly and the bee would always read books together under the big tree. They loved to learn new things, and they were always happy to share their stories with their friends in the big green garden.

Tom and Mia like to play with stamps. They have many stamps of animals, flowers and cars. They also have ink pads of different colors. They can make pictures with stamps on paper.

One day, they have a new idea. They want to mix the colors of the ink pads. They think it will be fun to see what happens. They take two ink pads, one red and one blue, and press them together. They make a new color: purple!

"Look, Mia, we made purple!" Tom says. He is happy.

"Wow, Tom, that is funny!" Mia says. She is surprised.

They try to mix other colors. They mix yellow and red, and make orange. They mix yellow and blue, and make green. They mix all the colors, and make brown.

They stamp their paper with the new colors. They make funny pictures of animals, flowers and cars. They laugh and have fun.

They show their pictures to their mom. She likes them very much. She says they are very creative. She puts their pictures on the fridge.

Tom and Mia are proud. They hug their mom. They love to play with stamps. They want to mix more colors tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy rock. A little boy saw the rock and wanted to hold it. He tried to pick it up, but it was too heavy for him. 

A man walked by and saw the little boy struggling. He asked the boy, "Do you need help?" The boy said, "Yes please, the rock is too heavy for me to hold." 

The man picked up the rock and gave it to the boy. The boy was so happy and said, "Thank you! I did it! I held the rock!" The man smiled and said, "You did it! That's a success!" 

The boy was so proud of himself and ran home to show his mom. He told her all about how he held the heavy rock and it was a big success. His mom was proud of him too. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and polite girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to write a note to put on the fridge. Lily was happy to help and got her crayons and paper. She wrote a sweet message that said, "I love you mommy". 

Lily's mommy was so happy when she saw the note on the fridge. She gave Lily a big hug and a kiss. Lily felt happy and proud that she could make her mommy smile. From that day on, Lily loved to write notes and put them on the fridge for her mommy to see. 

Whenever Lily's mommy saw the notes, she felt loved and happy. She would always thank Lily for being so thoughtful and polite. And Lily would smile and feel proud of herself for making her mommy happy with her writing. The end.

Lily was a healthy kid who liked to play with her toys and her dog. She had many toys, but her favorite was a big teddy bear that she called Bobo. She hugged Bobo every night and took him everywhere.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. Lily brought Bobo with her and put him on a bench while she played on the swings. She was having fun until she saw a big boy grab Bobo and run away. Lily was very scared and sad. She ran after the boy and shouted, "Give me back my Bobo!"

The boy did not listen. He laughed and threw Bobo in a trash can. Lily saw Bobo get dirty and smelly. She felt very angry and hurt. She started to cry very loud. She wanted her Bobo back.

Lily's mom heard her cry and came to help her. She saw what the boy did and scolded him. She told him to say sorry and to give Bobo back to Lily. The boy was ashamed and afraid. He said sorry and gave Bobo back to Lily.

Lily's mom hugged Lily and wiped her tears. She took Bobo out of the trash can and cleaned him with a tissue. She told Lily that Bobo was still her friend and that he loved her. She told Lily that she was brave and kind. She told Lily that she loved her too.

Lily smiled and hugged her mom and Bobo. She felt better and happy. She thanked her mom and said sorry for crying. She said she loved her mom and Bobo too. She learned that sometimes bad things happen, but good things can happen too. She learned that crying is okay, but smiling is better. She learned that she was a healthy kid who liked to play with her toys and her dog.

George was visiting his uncle and aunt. His uncle was a jazz musician and he was very proud of his jazz.

One day, George asked if he could borrow some jazz. His uncle said, "Yes, but remember to take good care of it!"

George said "Okay!" with a big smile.

He went back home and put the jazz on to listen. But it sounded terrible! George thought it was so terrible he couldn't listen anymore.

He quickly took the jazz back to his uncle and said, "I'm sorry, Uncle. I borrowed some jazz but it was terrible. Can I borrow something else?"

His uncle smiled and said, "It's alright. Why don't you borrow my guitar instead?"

George was delighted. He thanked his uncle and happily went home with his guitar.

Anna likes to play with her blue pot. She fills it with water and sand and makes soup. She stirs it with a big spoon and pretends to taste it. She thinks it is yummy.

One day, Anna wants to show her blue pot to her friend Ben. She takes it to his house and knocks on the door. Ben opens the door and smiles. He likes Anna and her blue pot.

"Look, Ben, this is my blue pot. I can make soup with it. Do you want to play with me?" Anna asks.

"Yes, Anna, I want to play with you. Your blue pot is nice. Can I have some soup?" Ben says.

"Sure, Ben, you can have some soup. Here, I will give you a bowl and a spoon. Be careful, it is hot." Anna says.

Anna and Ben sit on the grass and eat their soup. They pretend it is chicken and carrot and noodle soup. They slurp and giggle and say it is delicious. They are happy and have fun with the blue pot.

Once upon a time, there was a big bridge over a river. People would walk and drive over it every day. One day, a big fire started and the bridge began to burn. The fire was so hot that it made people feel dizzy. 

The firefighters came quickly to put out the fire, but it was too late. The bridge was burnt down and nobody could use it anymore. The people who lived on one side of the river couldn't get to the other side. 

But then, the people had an idea. They built a new bridge, even stronger and safer than the old one. And now, everybody could cross the river again. The end.

Bob was walking along the street when he spotted something small and thin on the ground. As he got closer, he saw it was an old rag. He bent down to pick it up and noticed that it was perfect for wiping his shoes. Excitedly he started to do so, but suddenly the rag got caught on his heel! Bob tried to pull it off, but it was stuck tight.

"Oh no!" he said to himself.

Just then a little girl walked past. She saw Bob struggling, so she stopped and asked him what was wrong.

"My rag is stuck on my heel," he told her.

The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "Here, let me try to help you." She carefully pulled and prodded until finally the rag came off.

Bob was so thankful for the girl's help. "Thank you so much," he said.

The little girl smiled and said, "You're welcome. Have a nice day!"

Bob waved goodbye and continued on his way, happy that he had been able to wipe his shoes and with a smile on his face.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together. One day, they go to the park with Mom and Dad. There is a big maze in the park. Mom and Dad say they can go in the maze, but they have to stay together and not get lost.

Anna and Ben run into the maze. They see many paths and walls. They try to find the way out. They turn left and right and left again. They see some flowers and some birds. They have fun.

But after a while, they get tired. They do not see the way out. They do not see Mom and Dad. They do not see anyone. They feel scared.

"Ben, I do not like this maze. It is boring and hard. I want to go out. I want to see Mom and Dad. Do you know the way out?" Anna says.

"No, Anna, I do not know the way out. I am sorry. I wish we did not go in the maze. Maybe we can shout for help. Maybe someone will hear us." Ben says.

They shout for help. They shout loud and long. They hope someone will hear them. They hope someone will find them. They hope someone will take them out of the maze. They hope they will see Mom and Dad soon. They hug each other and wait.

Once upon a time there was a poor boy. He had a book he wanted to display. He took the book everywhere he went, carefully balancing it in his hands while he walked. One day, he decided to take the book to a shop. The shopkeeper smiled at the boy and the book. He asked the boy if he wanted to display the book in the window for everyone to see. The boy was so excited, he said yes! So the shopkeeper carefully put the book on display. Everyone who passed by the shop commented on how beautiful the book was. The poor boy was so proud of himself and his special book; he knew this was the best thing to do with his beloved book.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they went to the store with their mom and saw a big ball of string. Tom wanted to buy it, but Lily said no. She said they had enough toys at home.

"But I like string," Tom said. "I can make things with it. Please, mom, can I have it?"

Mom looked at the string and smiled. She said they could share it if they were nice to each other. She bought the string and gave it to Tom and Lily.

Tom was happy. He thanked mom and ran to the car with the string. Lily was jealous. She wanted the string for herself. She thought Tom would not let her play with it.

When they got home, Tom started to make things with the string. He made a necklace, a bracelet, a hat, and a spider web. He showed them to mom and Lily. Mom said they were very good. Lily said nothing.

Lily waited until Tom was busy with his spider web. Then she grabbed the string and ran to her room. She locked the door and hid the string under her bed. She thought she was clever.

But Tom saw what she did. He was angry. He knocked on her door and asked for the string back. Lily said no. She said it was hers now. Tom said that was not fair. He said mom bought it for both of them. Lily said she did not care. She said she liked string more than Tom.

Tom and Lily started to yell at each other. They said mean things. Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily's door was locked and Tom was crying. She asked them to stop fighting and open the door. Lily said no. She said she wanted to keep the string.

Mom was sad. She said they were not being nice to each other. She said they had to share the string or she would take it away. She said they had to say sorry and hug. Lily felt bad. She knew mom was right. She opened the door and gave the string to Tom. She said she was sorry. Tom said he was sorry too. They hugged and said they loved each other.

Mom was happy. She said they were good twins. She said they could play with the string together. She said they could make more things and have fun. Tom and Lily agreed. They thanked mom and went to the living room with the string. They made a kite, a cat, a snake, and a rainbow. They showed them to mom and smiled. Mom said they were very creative. She said she was proud of them. Tom and Lily were happy. They said they were proud of each other. They said they liked string. They said they liked sharing.

Lily and Tom were playing with their pens and papers. They liked to draw and write things they saw or imagined. Lily was drawing a big flower with many colors. Tom was writing his name and some numbers.

"Look, Lily, I can write one, two, three, four, five!" Tom said, showing his paper to Lily.

"Wow, Tom, you are very smart!" Lily said, smiling. "I like your numbers. They are neat and clear."

"Thank you, Lily. I like your flower. It is pretty and cheerful. It makes me happy." Tom said, looking at Lily's paper.

"Thank you, Tom. I like to draw flowers. They are beautiful and smell good." Lily said, holding her paper.

"Do you want to trade papers?" Tom asked. "I can give you my numbers and you can give me your flower."

"Okay, Tom. That sounds fun." Lily said, nodding. "But first, let us complete our papers. We can add some stickers and glitter to make them more special."

"Okay, Lily. That sounds good." Tom said, agreeing. "Let us find some stickers and glitter in the box."

Lily and Tom went to the box where they kept their stickers and glitter. They chose some that they liked and went back to their papers. They stuck some stickers and sprinkled some glitter on their papers. They were very careful and happy.

"Look, Lily, I am done. I put some stars and hearts on my numbers. They are shiny and cute." Tom said, holding his paper.

"Look, Tom, I am done too. I put some butterflies and rainbows on my flower. They are colorful and lovely." Lily said, holding her paper.

"Wow, Lily, your paper is very nice. I like your butterflies and rainbows. They are fun and sweet." Tom said, admiring Lily's paper.

"Wow, Tom, your paper is very nice too. I like your stars and hearts. They are bright and warm." Lily said, admiring Tom's paper.

"Thank you, Lily. Thank you, Tom." They said together. "Do you want to trade papers now?"

"Yes, please." They said together. They traded papers and hugged each other. They were very happy and proud of their papers. They put them on the wall to show their mom and dad. They were very cheerful.
